label: 1000 Genomes
definition: A cohort of individuals from 26 populations whose genomes are sequenced and genotyped by the 1000 Genomes Project to catalogue human genetic variation and provide a reference for studies of common disease.

label: AddNeuroMed Cohort
definition: A cohort of people with Alzheimer disease, mild cognitive impairment and healthy cognition, established in 2006 at centres in Finland, Italy, Greece, Poland, France and the United Kingdom to investigate longitudinal brain changes using magnetic resonance imaging.

label: Adenoma Prevention with Celecoxib trial
definition: A randomised trial cohort of adults at high risk of recurrent colorectal adenomas, recruited at centres in the United States, Australia, Canada and Great Britain, comparing celecoxib with placebo for prevention of colorectal adenomas and assessment of treatment safety.

label: Advanced Study of Aortic Pathology
definition: A cohort of adults undergoing elective surgery for aortic valve or ascending aortic disease at Karolinska University Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden, recruited consecutively from 2007 for observational investigation of aortic pathology.

label: Africa Wits-INDEPTH partnership for Genomics studies
definition: A cohort of adults in rural and urban Burkina Faso, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa, established in 2012 and followed longitudinally to investigate genomic, environmental and behavioural influences on body composition and cardiometabolic disease.

label: Arthritis Research UK Osteoarthritis Genetics
definition: A case-control collection of people of European ancestry with severe osteoarthritis and unrelated controls from the United Kingdom, assembled for genome-wide investigation of genetic susceptibility to osteoarthritis.

label: Asian Cancer Project
definition: A case-control collection of Asian women with breast cancer and controls in Thailand contributing to investigation of genetic susceptibility to breast cancer.

label: Aspirin for Asymptomatic Atherosclerosis Study
definition: A randomised trial cohort of men and women aged 50–75 years in central Scotland without clinical cardiovascular disease but with a low ankle brachial index, comparing daily aspirin with placebo during 1998–2008 for prevention of cardiovascular events.

label: AtheroExpress
definition: A biobank of patients undergoing vascular surgery at University Medical Center Utrecht and formerly Antonius Hospital Nieuwegein, with vascular tissue, molecular measurements and at least three years of follow-up to investigate atherosclerotic plaques and subsequent cardiovascular events.

label: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study
definition: A cohort of adults aged 45–64 years from Forsyth County, Jackson, Minneapolis suburbs and Washington County in the United States, followed prospectively to investigate atherosclerosis, cardiovascular risk factors and clinical cardiovascular disease.

label: Atopic Dermatitis Research Network
definition: A consortium of academic medical centres conducting clinical investigations in people with atopic dermatitis to understand skin immunity and susceptibility to bacterial and viral infections and to develop approaches to prevent infectious complications.

label: Australia Cancer Study
definition: A case-control collection of women with epithelial ovarian cancer and population controls in Australia, with cases recruited through the New South Wales and Victorian cancer registries alongside the Australian Ovarian Cancer Study to investigate ovarian-cancer risk.

label: Australian Ovarian Cancer Study
definition: A case-control collection of Australian women aged 18–79 years with newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian cancer and population controls, recruited during 2002–2006 to investigate ovarian-cancer susceptibility.

label: Australian Twin Registry
definition: A registry of volunteer twin pairs and higher-order multiples in Australia, enrolling members since the late 1970s to support health, medical and scientific research.

label: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children
definition: A birth cohort of children and their families recruited through pregnancies in the Bristol area of the United Kingdom during 1990–1992, with later recruitment of eligible children, followed prospectively to investigate genetic and environmental influences on health and development across the life course.

label: Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster trials
definition: A project combining successive Berlin–Frankfurt–Münster treatment trials in children and adolescents with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia at centres in Germany, Austria and Switzerland to evaluate risk-adapted treatment, survival and toxicity.

label: Bladder Cancer Prognosis Programme
definition: A cohort of patients with newly diagnosed bladder cancer in the West Midlands, United Kingdom, recruited from December 2005 and followed prospectively to investigate lifestyle factors, molecular predictors, recurrence, progression and quality of life.

label: Brazilian Cohort
definition: A cohort of 45 babies from Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil, whose exomes provide population-specific reference variants for genetic investigation and diagnosis of rare diseases.

label: Breast Cancer Association Consortium
definition: A consortium of breast-cancer studies that pools participant-level tumour characteristics and epidemiological data to investigate breast-cancer risk factors and differences in the causes of tumour subtypes.

label: Bruneck study
definition: A cohort of residents of Bruneck, Italy, sampled by age and sex in 1990 and followed through repeated examinations to investigate atherosclerosis, cardiovascular disease and other age-related disorders.

label: Cancer and Leukemia Group B
definition: A consortium of institutional cancer trial cohorts, established in 1956 as the Acute Leukemia Group B, that coordinates trials of treatments for adult solid tumours and haematological malignancies to improve patient outcomes and investigate malignant disease biology.

label: Cancer Genome Atlas
definition: A project combining genomic characterisation of 33 cancer types through collaboration between the United States National Cancer Institute and National Human Genome Research Institute to map cancer-associated molecular changes and support prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

label: Cancer Prevention Study
definition: A cohort of adult men and women across all United States states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, enrolled by the American Cancer Society in 1982 and followed prospectively for mortality in relation to lifestyle, medical history and other exposures.

label: Cancer Prostate in Sweden
definition: A case-control collection of men with newly diagnosed prostate cancer and controls matched by age and residence in Sweden, used to investigate inherited susceptibility to prostate cancer.

label: Candesartan in Heart failure Assessment of Reduction in Mortality and morbidity
definition: A project combining three parallel placebo-controlled trials of candesartan in people with symptomatic heart failure, with reduced or preserved left ventricular function, across 26 countries, to evaluate mortality and hospitalisation; recruitment begins in March 1999.

label: Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Study
definition: A case-control collection of people with type 2 diabetes and controls from Japan contributing genome-wide association and replication data to investigations of type 2 diabetes susceptibility through the Cardiometabolic Genome Epidemiology Network.

label: Cardiogenics Study
definition: A case-control collection of patients with myocardial infarction and unaffected controls recruited in Cambridge, Leicester, Lübeck, Regensburg and Paris for investigation of coronary-disease genetics, including gene expression in monocytes and macrophages.

label: CARDIoGRAMplusC4D
definition: A consortium of coronary-disease genetic studies combining European, South Asian and East Asian case-control data to identify susceptibility variants for coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction. CARDIoGRAMplusC4D joins the Coronary Artery Disease Genome-wide Replication and Meta-analysis and Coronary Artery Disease Genetics consortia.

label: Carolina Head and Neck Cancer Epidemiology
definition: A case-control collection of people with newly diagnosed squamous-cell head and neck cancer and controls matched by age, race and sex, recruited during 2002–2006 in 46 North Carolina counties to investigate cancer risk factors.

label: CARTaGENE cohort (CHU Sainte-Justine, Quebec, Canada)
definition: A biobank of men and women aged 40–69 years sampled from four metropolitan areas in Quebec, with prospective health information and biological specimens for investigating genetic and environmental determinants of chronic disease.

label: Center for Autism Research and Treatment
definition: A research and clinical centre at the University of California, Los Angeles, that investigates autism, provides patient care and trains researchers and clinicians working with autistic children and adults and their families.

label: Center on Antisocial Drug Dependence
definition: A Colorado research centre founded in 1997 that investigates genetic contributions to adolescent externalising behaviours, including drug abuse and conduct disorder.

label: Centre dEtude du Polymorphisme Humain
definition: A research foundation, the Centre d’Etude du Polymorphisme Humain, that investigates human genetic variation, particularly in complex diseases, to improve understanding, diagnosis and personalised medicine.

label: Chicago Asthma Genetics
definition: A cohort of adults and children aged at least six years with clinically confirmed asthma, recruited through asthma clinics at the University of Chicago Medical Center for genetic investigation of asthma.

label: Children, Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm, Epidemiology
definition: A birth cohort of children enrolled at three to four months of age between 1994 and 1996 for prospective investigation of environmental, genetic and socioeconomic determinants of childhood asthma, allergic disease and their prognosis.

label: Cholesterol and Atherosclerosis Pharmacogenetics
definition: A cohort of African-American and White men and women completing six weeks of open-label simvastatin treatment to investigate genetic, demographic and clinical determinants of lipid-lowering response.

label: Cilento study
definition: A cohort of residents of the genetically isolated villages Campora, Gioi and Cardile in Cilento, southern Italy, providing genealogical and genomic data to investigate human genetic variation and the inherited determinants of complex traits and disease.

label: COIN
definition: A randomised trial cohort of patients with advanced colorectal cancer in the Continuous or Intermittent (COIN) trial, comparing uninterrupted oxaliplatin and fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy with planned treatment breaks to assess survival and treatment burden.

label: COIN-B
definition: A randomised trial cohort of patients with advanced colorectal cancer and no previous chemotherapy for metastases, recruited at 30 UK hospitals and one in Cyprus to compare intermittent chemotherapy combined with either intermittent or continuous cetuximab.

label: Colorectal Cancer Study of Austria
definition: A case-control collection of Austrian participants with colorectal cancer or colorectal polyps and colonoscopy-confirmed polyp-free controls, assembled to investigate genetic susceptibility to colorectal neoplasia.

label: Consortium for the Longitudinal Evaluation of African Americans with Early Rheumatoid Arthritis
definition: A project combining longitudinal and cross-sectional registry cohorts of African Americans with rheumatoid arthritis recruited through United States clinical centres to investigate genetic, clinical and environmental determinants of disease severity.

label: Consortium of Minority Population Genome-Wide Association Studies of Stroke
definition: A consortium of stroke cohorts from minority populations, including African Americans, that combines genome-wide association results to identify genetic susceptibility to stroke.

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg
definition: A project combining population surveys, follow-up cohorts and an acute myocardial infarction registry in the Augsburg region, established in 1996 to extend MONICA and support epidemiological, genetic, health-economic and health-care research.

label: Copenhagen Hospital Biobank
definition: A biobank of patients receiving hospital care in the Capital Region of Denmark, established at Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen in February 2009 and subsequently expanded to other hospitals, retaining leftover clinical blood samples to enable research on health and disease.

label: CROATIA-Korcula Study
definition: A cohort of adult volunteers recruited on Korčula island, Croatia, from 2007 to 2014 for family-based, cross-sectional investigation of genetic variants associated with common diseases, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, glaucoma and stroke.

label: Danish Glostrup Cohort
definition: A cohort of men and women in the Danish Glostrup population examined at age 60 to investigate inflammatory, haemostatic and genetic correlates of atherosclerosis.

label: Diabetes Genetics in Pakistan
definition: A case-control collection of people of Punjabi ancestry, predominantly originating from Mirpur, Pakistan, with type 2 diabetes or normal glucose regulation, assembled to investigate genetic susceptibility to diabetes and related glycaemic traits.

label: Diabetes in Mexico Study
definition: A cohort of people with type 2 diabetes and controls in Mexico City, Mexico, with a prospective design and genetic data used to investigate susceptibility to type 2 diabetes.

label: Diabetes Prevention Program
definition: A randomised trial cohort of people with impaired glucose tolerance and elevated fasting glucose recruited at 27 United States centres to compare lifestyle intervention, metformin and placebo for delaying or preventing type 2 diabetes.

label: Diabetes Reduction Assessment with Ramipril and Rosiglitazone Medication
definition: A randomised trial cohort of people with impaired fasting glucose or impaired glucose tolerance from 21 countries, assigned in a factorial design to ramipril, rosiglitazone or corresponding placebos to evaluate prevention of diabetes and effects on atherosclerosis.

label: Diabetes Research on Patient Stratification
definition: A project combining prospective European cohorts of people with prediabetes and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes to discover biomarkers of glycaemic deterioration, treatment response and diabetes subtypes through repeated metabolic and molecular assessment.

label: Dortmund Health Study
definition: A cohort of residents of Dortmund recruited during 2003–2004 and followed through questionnaires to investigate the frequency and consequences of headache and other chronic conditions, including their relationships with social factors.

label: Duke Cognition Cohort
definition: A cohort of adults in the United States with cognitive and genetic measurements contributing to research on genetic influences on general cognitive function.

label: DUNDEE
definition: A cohort of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer whose matched tumour and blood samples were collected through the Dundee bioresource facility, one of the four Scottish collection sites (Edinburgh, Glasgow, Dundee and Aberdeen) of the Scottish High Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer whole-genome sequencing study.

label: Durban Diabetes Study
definition: A cohort of urban Black residents of eThekwini Municipality, South Africa, assessed in a population-based cross-sectional survey combining questionnaires, clinical measurements, biomarkers and genetic data to investigate chronic diseases and their risk factors.

label: Dutch and Belgian Lung Cancer Screening Trial
definition: A randomised trial cohort of current and former smokers selected from the Dutch and Belgian general population to compare low-dose computed-tomography screening with no screening for reduction of lung-cancer mortality.

label: Dutch Microbiome Project
definition: A cohort of Dutch Lifelines participants providing faecal samples for metagenomic characterisation of gut microbial composition, function, virulence and antibiotic resistance in relation to health.

label: Edinburgh Stroke Study
definition: A cohort of patients with recent stroke recruited at Western General Hospital in Edinburgh, United Kingdom, from April 2002 to May 2005 and followed prospectively to investigate inflammatory markers, disability and mortality after stroke.

label: ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48
definition: A randomised trial cohort of people with atrial fibrillation in the multinational Effective Anticoagulation with Factor Xa Next Generation in Atrial Fibrillation–Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction 48 (ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48) trial, comparing edoxaban with warfarin for prevention of stroke and systemic embolism, with recruitment beginning in November 2008.

label: EPIGEN
definition: A project combining population-based genomic data from northeastern, southeastern and southern Brazil to investigate ancestry, admixture, kinship, inbreeding and deleterious genetic variation, known as the EPIGEN Brazil Initiative.

label: Erasmus Rucphen Family Study
definition: A cohort of descendants of 22 founder families and their spouses in southwest Netherlands, examined from 2002 to 2005 as part of the Genetic Research in Isolated Populations programme to identify genetic risk factors for complex disorders.

label: Estonian Biobank
definition: A biobank of volunteer adults aged at least 18 years resident throughout Estonia, linking blood samples, health examinations and questionnaires with national registries to support population-based genetic and health research.

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer
definition: A cohort of men and women, mostly aged 35–70 years, recruited during 1992–2000 at 23 centres in ten European countries and followed prospectively to investigate relationships between nutrition, lifestyle, cancer and other diseases.

label: European Prospective Investigation of Cancer-Norfolk
definition: A cohort of men and women aged 39–79 recruited in Norwich and surrounding Norfolk communities in 1993–1997, followed through questionnaires and examinations to investigate diet, lifestyle and health as part of the European Prospective Investigation of Cancer.

label: EuroTARGET project
definition: A project combining prospectively recruited patients with metastatic renal cell cancer from 62 European centres and patients from previous studies to identify host and tumour biomarkers that predict response and toxicity during targeted therapy.

label: Extremely Low Gestational Age Newborns
definition: A birth cohort of infants born before 28 weeks of gestation at 14 sites, followed to investigate exposures associated with brain injury and subsequent neurological and developmental outcomes.

label: Fatty Acid Sensor Study
definition: A cohort of participants receiving fish-oil supplementation for six weeks, with triglyceride measurements and genotyping used to investigate inherited variation in the metabolic response to omega-3 fatty acids.

label: Finnish Twin Cohort Study
definition: A project combining longitudinal Finnish twin cohorts established in the 1970s and 1990s, including the older twin cohort, FinnTwin12 and FinnTwin16, with repeated phenotyping and molecular measurements for investigation of health and disease.

label: FINRISK
definition: A project combining independently sampled Finnish adult population cohorts recruited through five-yearly health surveys during 1972–2012 and followed through national registers to monitor risk factors, health behaviours and non-communicable disease.

label: Flemish Gut Flora Project
definition: A cohort of volunteers from Flanders, Belgium, with health and lifestyle questionnaires, biological samples and genetic data assembled to investigate relationships between the gut microbiome, health and lifestyle.

label: Gabriel Advanced Survey
definition: A cohort of children living on farms and reference children examined cross-sectionally for asthma, atopy and household microbial exposures in the GABRIEL Advanced Study.

label: GCAT Genomes for Life
definition: A cohort of adults aged 40–65 years in Catalonia, Spain, followed prospectively in Genomes for Life (GCAT) to assess epidemiological, genomic and epigenomic contributions to chronic disease.

label: GENESIS
definition: A case-control collection of French women with breast cancer and an affected sister, without a detected BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation, together with unaffected sisters and unrelated controls. GENESIS (GENE SISters) investigates inherited breast-cancer susceptibility alongside environmental factors and tumour characteristics.

label: Genetic Analysis of Multiple Sclerosis
definition: A case-control collection of people with multiple sclerosis from multiple countries and controls from Sweden, the United Kingdom and published studies, assembled to identify genetic variants associated with multiple-sclerosis susceptibility.

label: Genetic Consortium for Anorexia Nervosa
definition: A consortium of anorexia-nervosa sample collections assembled internationally for genome-wide and exome-array analyses of genetic susceptibility to anorexia nervosa in collaboration with the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 3.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica
definition: A cohort of families in Costa Rica, including extended pedigrees and parent–child trios with asthma probands, assembled to identify common and rare genetic determinants of asthma and related phenotypes through sequencing and family-based analyses.

label: Genetic Overlap between Metabolic and Psychiatric traits
definition: A case-control collection of people in Greece with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes or both, analysed alongside population controls from Greek cohorts to investigate shared genetic susceptibility to the two disorders.

label: Genetic Prostate cancer risk stratification for targeted screening
definition: A cohort of men aged 40–69 with a family history of prostate cancer, recruited through London clinics, a UK prostate cancer study and public advertisements to evaluate genetic risk assessment and prostate biopsy for targeted prostate cancer screening.

label: Genetic Research in Isolated
definition: A project combining family-based and population-based investigations of a genetically isolated population in southwest Netherlands, initiated in 1995 as Genetic Research in Isolated Populations to identify genetic factors in neuropsychiatric, cardiovascular and metabolic disorders.

label: Genetics of diabetes Audit and Research
definition: A cohort of people with type 2 diabetes and non-diabetic controls in Tayside, Scotland, recruiting from 1998 and linking biological samples to longitudinal health records to investigate genetic and environmental determinants of diabetes onset, progression and treatment response.

label: Genetics of Healthy Aging
definition: A cohort of siblings aged at least 90 years and younger controls aged 50–75 years, recruited during 2004–2008 in 11 European countries to investigate genetic determinants of healthy ageing and longevity.

label: GenomeAsia 100K project
definition: A cohort of people from diverse Asian population groups whose genomes are sequenced by the GenomeAsia 100K Project to catalogue genetic variation, population structure, disease associations and founder effects and to support genetic analyses.

label: German Multiple Myeloma Study Group
definition: A consortium of multiple-myeloma clinical trial cohorts coordinated through centres across Germany to evaluate treatment strategies for patients at different disease stages.

label: Ghana Prostate Study
definition: A case-control collection of men in Accra, Ghana, recruited from population screening and Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital between 2004 and 2012 to investigate prostate-cancer risk factors.

label: Glaucoma Inheritance Study in Tasmania
definition: A cohort of people with glaucoma and their relatives in Tasmania, Australia, recruited through affected probands identified in 1994–1996 and assessed with pedigrees and eye examinations to investigate familial primary open-angle glaucoma.

label: Greece Hellenic Isolated Cohorts
definition: A project combining the MANOLIS cohort from mountainous villages in Crete and the Pomak cohort from mountainous northern Greece to investigate genetic determinants of complex traits in founder populations.

label: Health and Retirement Study
definition: A cohort of adults aged over 50 years and their households in the United States, surveyed every two years from 1992 to investigate changes in health, cognition, economic circumstances, work, retirement and family relationships during ageing.

label: Health2000 Study
definition: A cohort of adults in mainland Finland sampled for health interviews and examinations in 2000–2001, primarily at age 30 or older, to characterise public-health problems, their determinants and treatment, and functional and work capacity.

label: Heart Protection Study
definition: A randomised trial cohort of adults aged 40–80 at increased risk of coronary death, recruited in 1994–1997 to evaluate simvastatin and antioxidant vitamins, each against placebo, for prevention of mortality and major vascular events.

label: Hoorn Diabetes Care System
definition: A cohort of people with type 2 diabetes receiving primary care in West-Friesland, the Netherlands, enrolling from 1998 and assessed annually to investigate the course of diabetes, its complications and treatment.

label: Hospital Discharge Register Sweden
definition: A registry of people discharged from inpatient care in Sweden, initiated in 1964 and nationwide since 1987, recording somatic and psychiatric diagnoses for longitudinal population research.

label: Human Genetics Initiative
definition: A project combining clinical data and biological materials from psychiatric genetic studies in a shared National Institute of Mental Health repository, organised into disorder-related collections to support research on mental illness.

label: Hunter Community Study
definition: A cohort of men and women aged 55–85 residing in Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia, followed longitudinally with questionnaires, clinical assessments, biological samples and linked health records to investigate health and ageing.

label: Icelandic Cancer Registry
definition: A registry of people diagnosed with cancer in Iceland, established in 1954 to record nationwide cancer diagnoses and support cancer research.

label: Identification of Men with a genetic predisposition to ProstAte Cancer
definition: A cohort of men aged 40–69 years from families with BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, including mutation carriers and age-matched non-carriers, undergoing annual prostate-specific antigen testing in an international investigation of targeted prostate-cancer screening.

label: IIBDGC genotyped CD study
definition: A cohort of genotyped patients with Crohn's disease collected through the International Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium at sites in Europe, North America and Australia to investigate genetic susceptibility and gene–environment interactions.

label: Indiana Sisters Study
definition: A cohort of premenopausal women of European-American ancestry, with an extended European-American and African-American sample, providing bone-density and genetic measurements for investigation of inherited variation in skeletal traits.

label: INfancia y Medio Ambiente Project
definition: A project combining cohorts of pregnant women and their children from seven Spanish areas to investigate environmental exposures and child health through coordinated assessments, questionnaires and biological sampling.

label: International Cancer Genome Consortium-Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
definition: A cohort of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia whose tumour genomes are analysed within the International Cancer Genome Consortium to identify alterations involved in disease development and progression and potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

label: International Headache Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of headache clinic and population-based cohorts that combines genome-wide association data from migraine cases and controls of European ancestry to identify genetic susceptibility loci for migraine.

label: International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of research groups that combines multiple sclerosis case collections from people of European descent across 15 countries with control datasets to investigate genetic susceptibility to multiple sclerosis.

label: International Schizophrenia Consortium
definition: A consortium of schizophrenia case-control collections that combines genome-wide genetic data, including European-ancestry samples, to investigate inherited susceptibility to schizophrenia and shared genetic risk with bipolar disorder.

label: Italian Network on Genetic Isolates Studies
definition: A consortium of genetically isolated population cohorts from Val Borbera, Friuli Venezia Giulia and Carlantino in Italy, combining genomic and phenotypic data to investigate genetic variation and complex traits.

label: Leeds Melanoma Cohort
definition: A cohort of patients aged 18–75 with newly diagnosed stage I–IIIA primary melanoma, recruited in England from 2000 to 2012 and followed to investigate factors associated with tumour thickness and melanoma survival.

label: Leiden Longevity Study
definition: A cohort of families containing at least two long-lived siblings, with men aged at least 89 years and women at least 91 years, and information on their relatives and spouses, assembled to identify inherited determinants of exceptional longevity.

label: LifeLines
definition: A cohort of residents of the northern Netherlands and their families, recruited during 2006–2013 across three generations, with repeated examinations, questionnaires and stored biological samples to investigate environmental, phenotypic and genomic influences on chronic disease and healthy ageing.

label: Living Biobank
definition: A biobank of healthy Chinese and Malay participants from Singapore's Multi-Ethnic Cohort and Singapore Health 2012 collections, assembled for phenotype recall investigations of carriers of genetic variants with substantial effects.

label: Los Angeles component of The Womens Contraceptive and Reproductive Experiences Study
definition: A case-control collection of White and African-American women aged 35–64 in Los Angeles, United States, with invasive breast cancer or no previous breast cancer, contributing to the Women's Contraceptive and Reproductive Experiences investigation of breast cancer risk factors.

label: Lothian Birth Cohort
definition: A research programme comprising two cohorts, the Lothian Birth Cohorts of 1921 and 1936, whose members took an intelligence test at age 11 in the Scottish Mental Surveys of 1932 and 1947 and were recruited in older age, mostly in Edinburgh and the Lothians, for repeated study of cognitive ageing.

label: Lund Stroke Register
definition: A registry of people with a first-ever stroke in the Lund-Orup district, identified through prospective and retrospective surveillance to describe stroke ascertainment, hospitalisation and patient outcomes.

label: Marseille Thrombosis Association Study
definition: A cohort of unrelated patients with documented venous thrombosis recruited at La Timone Hospital in Marseille, France, in 1994–2005, excluding recognised major thrombophilias, for investigation of genetic susceptibility to venous thrombosis.

label: Mexican Biobank
definition: A biobank of individuals from rural and urban localities across all 32 Mexican states, linking genome-wide genotypes to disease and complex-trait information to investigate population history and genetic and environmental contributions to health.

label: MIRAGE
definition: A cohort of families including siblings discordant for Alzheimer disease, with African-American and white family samples, assembled for genetic investigation through the Multi-Institutional Research on Alzheimer Genetic Epidemiology (MIRAGE) programme.

label: Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia Collaboration
definition: A consortium of schizophrenia case-control collections from three National Institute of Mental Health repository studies, including people of European and African-American ancestry, combining genetic data to identify schizophrenia-susceptibility variants.

label: MOnica Risk, Genetics, Archiving and Monograph
definition: A project combining prospective population cohorts from European countries to examine cardiovascular risk factors and their associations with subsequent stroke and other cardiovascular events.

label: Monitoring of Trends and Determinants in Cardiovascular Disease
definition: A project combining standardised cardiovascular surveillance in populations aged 35–64 years across 26 countries in Europe, North America and the Western Pacific to relate changes in mortality and morbidity to risk factors and medical care.

label: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
definition: A cohort of men and women aged 45–84 years from six United States centres, including White, African-American, Hispanic and Chinese-ancestry participants, established in 2000 to investigate the prevalence, determinants and progression of subclinical cardiovascular disease.

label: Multicenter Family Study
definition: A project combining seven collections of families with multiple members affected by schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder, including European-ancestry and admixed families from research sites in Europe, Australia and the United States, to investigate common and rare genetic contributions to schizophrenia.

label: Multiethnic Cohort Study of Diet and Health
definition: A cohort of adults aged 45–75 years from multiple ethnic groups in Hawaii and California, principally Los Angeles County, recruited during 1993–1996 and followed prospectively to investigate diet and other determinants of cancer.

label: Multiple Environmental and Genetic Assessment of Risk Factors for Venous Thrombosis
definition: A case-control collection of patients younger than 70 with a first deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, recruited through six Dutch anticoagulation clinics in 1999–2004, with partner and population controls, for investigation of environmental and genetic thrombosis risk factors.

label: National Health Service Blood and Transplant
definition: A special health authority that provides blood donation services in England and organ transplantation services across the United Kingdom, managing donated blood, organs, tissues and stem cells and conducting research on treatments and processes.

label: National Study of Colorectal Cancer Genetics
definition: A case-control collection of people with colorectal cancer and spouse or partner controls, established in 2003 across United Kingdom centres to identify inherited variants that confer susceptibility to colorectal cancer.

label: Netherlands Twin Registry
definition: A registry of twins and their relatives with longitudinal phenotypic and genetic data, established to investigate inherited and environmental contributions to variation in health, fertility, development, growth and behaviour.

label: New England-based Case-Control Study of Ovarian Cancer
definition: A case-control collection of women aged 18–80 with epithelial ovarian cancer and population controls from eastern Massachusetts and New Hampshire, recruited in four phases from 1984 to 2008 to investigate ovarian-cancer risk factors.

label: NIDDK
definition: A cohort of patients with gastroparesis recruited through the Gastroparesis Clinical Research Consortium (GpCRC), a network of gastrointestinal tertiary centres in the United States sponsored by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), whose registry provided the gastroparesis cases of the GWAS Catalog study tagged NIDDK.

label: Nijmegen Biomedical Study
definition: A cohort of adults from Nijmegen, the Netherlands, established in 2000 with population sampling from 2002 to investigate genetic variation, lifestyle and environmental exposures in relation to disease and population traits.

label: Northern Ireland Cohort for Longitudinal Study of Ageing
definition: A cohort of adults aged 50 years and older living in private accommodation in Northern Ireland, recruited in 2013–2016 and followed through surveys and health assessments to investigate ageing, health and social circumstances.

label: Northern Sweden Population Health Study
definition: A cohort of residents of Karesuando, Soppero and the Vittangi area in Norrbotten, northern Sweden, surveyed in 2006 and 2009 to characterise population health, including environmental and inherited determinants of allergic sensitisation.

label: Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort study
definition: A birth cohort of children and their parents in Norway, recruited through pregnancies with births during 1999–2009, combining repeated family questionnaires, biological samples and health-register linkages for longitudinal research.

label: Orkney Complex Disease Study
definition: A cohort of people aged 16–100 with Orcadian grandparents, recruited in Orkney, northern Scotland, in 2005–2011 for family-based investigation of genetic influences on cardiovascular and other complex-disease risks.

label: Outcome Reduction With Initial Glargine Intervention Trial
definition: A randomised trial cohort of adults aged at least 50 with cardiovascular disease and dysglycaemia in 40 countries, enrolled during the two years ending December 2005 to compare insulin glargine with standard glycaemic care and omega-3 fatty acids with placebo for cardiovascular prevention.

label: Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium
definition: A consortium of ovarian cancer studies established in 2005 that combines participant data to investigate genetic and epidemiological risk factors for ovarian cancer.

label: Oxford Biobank
definition: A biobank of healthy men and women aged 30–50 years from Oxfordshire, United Kingdom, recruiting from 1999 and permitting recall by genotype or phenotype to investigate mechanisms of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

label: PanCareLIFE
definition: A consortium of European childhood and adolescent cancer-survivor cohorts that combines cohort, case-control, genetic and intervention research to investigate treatment-related fertility impairment, hearing loss and health-related quality of life.

label: Parkinson Environment and Gene
definition: A case-control collection of people with early-stage Parkinson disease and population controls in central California, recruited in 2000–2007 and 2010–2017 to investigate environmental and genetic determinants of Parkinson disease.

label: People of the British Isles
definition: A cohort of people from rural areas of the United Kingdom, principally with all four grandparents originating from the same local area, providing genetic controls and information on fine-scale population structure.

label: Physical Activity and Nutrition in Children Study
definition: A cohort of children aged 7–9 at baseline in Kuopio, Finland, enrolled in 2007–2009 for long-term follow-up comparing a physical-activity and dietary intervention with a control group through repeated health assessments.

label: Population-based Colonoscopy study
definition: A cohort of Swedish-born people in Stockholm, Sweden, with bowel-symptom questionnaires, gastroenterological assessments and biological specimens assembled to investigate bowel function and gastrointestinal health.

label: Precocious Coronary Artery Disease Study
definition: A case-control collection of people with coronary heart disease and an affected sibling, together with population controls, recruited in the United Kingdom, Italy, Sweden and Germany in 2004–2008 to investigate determinants of coronary disease.

label: Pressioni Arteriose Monitorate E Loro Associazionie
definition: A cohort of adults aged 25–74 years sampled from the general population of Monza, Italy, with office, home and ambulatory blood-pressure measurements and prospective mortality follow-up to evaluate cardiovascular risk prediction.

label: Prospective Investigation of the Vasculature in Uppsala Seniors
definition: A cohort of people aged 70 sampled from the community register of Uppsala, Sweden, to investigate whether measurements of vascular structure and function predict subsequent cardiovascular events.

label: Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension
definition: A case-control collection of people of European ancestry with psoriasis and unaffected controls recruited at participating institutions for genetic analysis using the Immunochip.

label: Psychiatric GWAS Consortium
definition: A consortium of genome-wide association studies that combines data on attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, autism, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder and schizophrenia through meta-analysis to investigate genetic susceptibility to psychiatric disorders.

label: Research on Adolescent Development and Relationships
definition: A project combining the RADAR-Young and RADAR-Old adolescent cohorts in the Netherlands, followed through repeated questionnaires to investigate development and relationships with parents, friends and romantic partners.

label: Rotterdam Study
definition: A cohort of middle-aged and older residents of Rotterdam, the Netherlands, established in 1990 and followed prospectively to investigate the causes, early development and natural history of chronic diseases and possible targets for intervention.

label: Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean asthma study
definition: A cohort of families recruited through members with asthma in the founder population of Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec, Canada, with respiratory, allergy and genetic measurements to investigate inherited determinants of asthma and related traits.

label: Sahlgrenska Academy Study on Ischemic Stroke
definition: A case-control collection of patients aged 18–69 with acute ischaemic stroke recruited in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 1998–2003 and matched population controls, with longitudinal patient follow-up to investigate stroke risk factors and outcomes.

label: SardiNIA Study of Aging
definition: A cohort of residents aged 14–102 at baseline from four towns in the Ogliastra region of Sardinia, Italy, established in 2001 for longitudinal investigation of genetic influences on ageing, cardiovascular risk factors, personality and other age-related traits.

label: Scania Diabetes Registry
definition: A registry of patients with diabetes recruited through hospitals in Scania, Sweden, from 1996, with clinical follow-up and biological samples to classify diabetes subgroups and investigate genetic and biomarker predictors of complications.

label: Shanghai Study
definition: A cohort of patients with gallbladder carcinoma at Xinhua Hospital affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University whose paired tumour and normal samples undergo sequencing to investigate somatic mutations and their clinical associations.

label: Short Course Oncology Treatment trial
definition: A randomised trial cohort of adults with high-risk stage II or stage III colorectal cancer, recruited at 244 centres during 2008–2013 to compare three versus six months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy using disease-free survival as the primary outcome.

label: Simons Simplex Collection
definition: A cohort of families recruited through 12 North American clinical sites, each with one child aged 4–18 with an autism spectrum disorder and unaffected biological parents, often including unaffected siblings, assembled to investigate rare and de novo genetic contributions to autism.

label: Singapore Chinese Study
definition: A case-control collection of Singapore Chinese people aged at least 50 years with colorectal cancer and age- and sex-matched healthy controls, assembled to investigate genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer.

label: SORCE
definition: A randomised trial cohort of patients with resected renal cell carcinoma at intermediate or high relapse risk, enrolled in the United Kingdom and six other countries in 2007–2013 to compare postoperative sorafenib with placebo for prevention of cancer recurrence.

label: Spit for Science
definition: A cohort of university students followed longitudinally through surveys and DNA collection at Virginia Commonwealth University to investigate genetic and environmental contributions to alcohol use, other substance use and mental health.

label: Sweden Bipolar Disorder Cohort
definition: A case-control collection of people with bipolar disorder identified through Swedish national registers and Stockholm clinical services, with unaffected controls, assembled to investigate genetic determinants of bipolar disorder and its clinical subtypes.

label: Swedish Twin Registry
definition: A registry of twins in Sweden, established in the late 1950s to investigate smoking and alcohol in relation to cancer and cardiovascular disease while accounting for genetic susceptibility, and subsequently expanded to study common complex diseases.

label: Taiwan Type 2 Diabetes Study
definition: A case-control collection of Han Chinese people residing in Taiwan, including patients with type 2 diabetes and population controls, assembled for genome-wide identification of diabetes-susceptibility variants.

label: TEENs of Attica: Genes and Environment
definition: A cohort of healthy adolescents aged 13–15 attending public secondary schools in the Athens area of Attica, Greece, sampled for cross-sectional collection of anthropometric, medical, dietary and genetic data.

label: The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
definition: A cohort of men and women aged 50 years or older living in England, established in 2002 and assessed every two years to investigate economic, social, psychological, cognitive and biological aspects of ageing.

label: The Fenland Study
definition: A cohort of people from Cambridgeshire followed to investigate how genetic and lifestyle factors interact in the development of diabetes, obesity and related metabolic disorders.

label: The Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren
definition: A German research organisation comprising research centres that develop technologies and conduct research addressing societal challenges, including disease, climate change and quantum technologies.

label: The MANOLIS cohort
definition: A cohort of people with at least one parent from the Mylopotamos area of Crete, Greece, recruited in Anogia and surrounding villages for the Minoan Isolates (MANOLIS) collection, which links genetic data with clinical, biochemical and lifestyle measurements to investigate medically relevant complex traits.

label: The Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset
definition: A case-control collection of people with abdominal aortic aneurysm and controls in the Netherlands, assembled for genome-wide investigation of genetic susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm.

label: The Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma
definition: A biobank of patients with multiple myeloma in Trondheim, Norway, providing biological material for genetic investigations of susceptibility to multiple myeloma.

label: The Pakistan Risk Of Myocardial Infarction Study
definition: A case-control collection of adults aged 30–80 in Pakistan with a first confirmed acute myocardial infarction and matched controls, assembled to investigate genetic, lifestyle and biochemical determinants of coronary heart disease in South Asia.

label: The Secondary Manifestations of ARTerial disease study
definition: A cohort of adults aged 18–80 newly referred with atherosclerotic vascular disease or major atherosclerosis risk factors, recruited from September 1996 for prospective investigation of concomitant arterial disease and predictors of future cardiovascular events.

label: The Hellenic study of Interactions between Single nucleotide polymorphisms and Eating in Atherosclerosis Susceptibility
definition: A case-control collection of Greek individuals with angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease and individuals without coronary artery disease, used to investigate genetic susceptibility and evaluate polygenic risk prediction.

label: Treating to New Targets
definition: A randomised trial cohort of patients with clinically evident stable coronary heart disease assigned to daily atorvastatin at 10 or 80 mg to compare cardiovascular outcomes under different intensities of lipid lowering.

label: Twins Early Development Study
definition: A birth cohort of twins born in England and Wales in 1994–1996, recruited through national birth records and followed from infancy to investigate genetic and environmental influences on cognitive, emotional and behavioural development.

label: Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of international type 1 diabetes family and case-control collections, organised through Asia-Pacific, European, North American and United Kingdom networks to identify genetic determinants of diabetes susceptibility and provide shared biological samples and data.

label: UK Adult Twin Register
definition: A registry of volunteer adult twins from across the United Kingdom, established in 1992, with repeated clinical assessments, questionnaires and molecular data to investigate genetic and environmental contributions to ageing and complex disease.

label: UK Biobank
definition: A cohort of adults aged 40–69 recruited across the United Kingdom in 2006–2010, with biological samples, extensive phenotyping and prospective health follow-up, established to investigate genetic and nongenetic determinants of diseases of middle and older age.

label: UK Brain Expression Consortium
definition: A consortium of brain-tissue collections from neuropathologically normal donors in Edinburgh, United Kingdom, and the United States, combining genotypes and expression measurements across brain regions to investigate genetic regulation of brain gene expression.

label: UK Childhood Cancer Study
definition: A case-control collection of children with cancer and controls matched by sex, age and residence throughout England, Scotland and Wales during 1991–1998, assembled to investigate causes of childhood cancer using interviews, records, exposure measurements and biological samples.

label: UK Household Longitudinal Study
definition: A cohort of household members across all four United Kingdom nations, interviewed annually in Understanding Society to investigate changes in education, employment, income, health, family life, behaviour and social circumstances.

label: UK Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of inflammatory-bowel-disease patient collections across the United Kingdom combining genetic and clinical data to investigate susceptibility to Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis and variation in treatment response.

label: Viking Health Study
definition: A cohort of people from the population isolate of Shetland, assembled to identify common and rare genetic variants influencing cardiovascular and other complex-disease risks.

label: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
definition: A consortium of disease-specific case collections and shared controls, coordinated by United Kingdom research groups to identify genetic variants associated with common diseases and evaluate methods for genome-wide association analysis.

label: Basquecolon cohort
definition: A case-control collection of self-identified non-Hispanic White participants with colorectal cancer and comparison participants, contributing the Basque-colon validation sample for evaluation of polygenic prediction of colorectal cancer risk.

label: INTERVAL study
definition: A randomised trial cohort of male and female whole-blood donors recruited during 2012–2014 at NHS Blood and Transplant centres in England to compare donation intervals and assess whether more frequent donation preserves donor health while increasing blood supply.

label: CONVERGE
definition: A case-control collection of Han Chinese women with recurrent major depression and controls recruited in China to investigate depression genetics through the China, Oxford and Virginia Commonwealth University Experimental Research on Genetic Epidemiology (CONVERGE) consortium.

label: Gene-Environmental Interaction and phenotype study
definition: A cohort of Korean participants undergoing comprehensive health examinations at Seoul National University Hospital's Gangnam Center, with linked clinical and biobank data used to investigate genetic and environmental influences on phenotypes.

label: China Atherosclerosis Study
definition: A case-control collection of Han Chinese people with coronary artery disease and controls in China, assembled for genome-wide identification of coronary-disease susceptibility variants.

label: Diabetes Prediction and Prevention
definition: A birth cohort of Finnish children screened from 1994 for HLA-associated type 1 diabetes susceptibility, with genetically at-risk children followed prospectively to investigate islet autoimmunity and diabetes development.

label: Functional genomic diagnostic tools for coronary artery disease
definition: A cohort of patients undergoing coronary angiography at two hospitals in Lebanon, recruited in 2007–2010 for cross-sectional investigation of genetic and clinical factors associated with coronary artery disease.

label: German Chronic Kidney Disease Study
definition: A cohort of people under nephrological care across Germany with reduced kidney function or overt proteinuria, followed prospectively with clinical and biological measurements to investigate chronic kidney disease progression, complications and prognostic biomarkers.

label: German Longevity Study
definition: A case-control collection of German long-lived individuals aged at least 94 years and younger comparison participants, used to investigate genetic contributions to exceptional longevity and reduced susceptibility to age-related diseases.

label: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events
definition: A registry of patients hospitalised with acute coronary syndromes at centres across multiple countries, followed prospectively during admission and after discharge to compare treatment practices, clinical characteristics and outcomes and improve care.

label: TwinGene Study
definition: A cohort of twins from the Swedish Twin Registry undergoing health examinations and venous blood collection in 2004–2008, providing genetic and health data for investigations of ageing, metabolic health and mortality.

label: Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men
definition: A cohort of men aged about 50 years in Uppsala, Sweden, examined during 1970–1974 and followed prospectively to investigate cardiovascular and lifestyle risk factors, survival and functional independence in old age.

label: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Ageing
definition: A cohort of volunteers participating in the United States National Institute on Aging's longitudinal programme, established in 1958 to investigate individual variation in human ageing and distinguish ageing-related changes from disease processes.

label: Motor Neuron Disease Biobank study
definition: A biobank of adults diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at United Kingdom hospitals, collecting whole-blood DNA from 2004 for genetic research into motor neuron disease.

label: Diabetic Cohort
definition: A cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes recruited from public polyclinics and hospital outpatient clinics in Singapore in 2004–2010, followed to investigate genetic, physiological and lifestyle determinants of diabetic complications.

label: Ely Study
definition: A cohort of adults without diabetes aged 40–69 at baseline in Ely, England, followed from 1990 with clinical, anthropometric and biochemical assessments to investigate type 2 diabetes incidence and its relationship to impaired fasting glucose.

label: Genetic Asthma Susceptibility to Indoor Pollution in Peru
definition: A case-control collection of children and adolescents aged 9–19 with asthma and without asthma, recruited in two communities of Lima, Peru, in 2011–2014 to investigate genetic and environmental determinants of asthma, immunoglobulin E and lung function.

label: Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative
definition: A cohort of untreated patients with early Parkinson disease, healthy controls and people without imaging evidence of dopaminergic deficit, enrolled internationally at 24 sites for standardised longitudinal investigation of clinical, imaging, genetic and biospecimen markers of disease progression.

label: Psychosis Endophenotype Consortium
definition: A consortium of psychosis case, unaffected-relative and control collections from Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain and the United Kingdom that combines genetic data to investigate susceptibility across psychotic disorders, including schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

label: Study of Health in Pomerania
definition: A project combining the SHIP-START and SHIP-TREND population cohorts of adults aged 20–79 in West Pomerania, northeast Germany, recruited in 1997–2001 and 2008–2012 respectively, to investigate health, disease and their determinants through repeated examinations.

label: The Cooperative Health Research in South Tyrol
definition: A cohort of adults from the middle and upper Vinschgau/Val Venosta in South Tyrol, with family participation, biological samples and repeated follow-up to investigate genetic and molecular determinants of age-related chronic conditions and their interaction with lifestyle and environment.

label: The Health Effects of Arsenic Longitudinal Study
definition: A cohort of adults aged 18–75 from Araihazar, Bangladesh, recruited in 2000–2002 and assessed biennially to investigate health effects of arsenic exposure through drinking water, including chronic disease and mortality.

label: 100,000 Genomes Project
definition: A cohort of National Health Service patients with rare diseases or cancer, and their relatives, whose genomes were sequenced by Genomics England within the United Kingdom's national healthcare system to provide diagnoses and discover aetiological variants.

label: 1958 British Birth Cohort
definition: A birth cohort of people born in Great Britain in one week of March 1958, followed through life as the National Child Development Study, whose DNA collection serves as a population control set for genetic association studies such as those of the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium.

label: 300BCG
definition: A cohort of 323 healthy adults of the Human Functional Genomics Project who were vaccinated with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin and profiled before and after vaccination to investigate human variation in trained immunity.

label: AACR Project GENIE
definition: An international registry of the American Association for Cancer Research that aggregates clinical-grade tumour sequencing data and clinical outcomes from patients at participating cancer centres to support precision oncology research.

label: AC-ANGIOPREDICT Phase II trial
definition: A cohort of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer treated with bevacizumab-containing therapy in the AC-ANGIOPREDICT phase II trial, whose tumour, normal and plasma samples were sequenced to identify biomarkers of response.

label: Adjuvant Lapatinib and/or Trastuzumab Treatment Optimisation trial
definition: A cohort of women with HER2-positive early breast cancer enrolled in the ALTTO phase III trial of adjuvant trastuzumab and lapatinib, whose tumours have been profiled to define molecular subtypes associated with the risk of distant recurrence.

label: African Collaborative Center for Microbiome and Genomics Research
definition: An H3Africa cohort of women recruited in Abuja, Nigeria, by the African Collaborative Center for Microbiome and Genomics Research to investigate the vaginal microbiome, human papillomavirus persistence and cervical cancer risk, described in the centre's cohort profile.

label: African Genome Resource
definition: A resource of the African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research that combines approximately 3,000 whole-genome sequences and 600 transcriptomes from African populations into a continent-specific haplotype reference panel, an African transcriptome resource and an informatics centre in Uganda.

label: African Genome Variation Project
definition: A collection of 1,481 individuals from 18 ethno-linguistic groups in sub-Saharan Africa with dense genotype data, and 320 individuals from seven groups with low-coverage whole-genome sequence, assembled by the African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research to characterise population diversity and support the design and interpretation of genomic studies in Africa.

label: African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research
definition: A consortium of research groups in Africa and the United Kingdom that brings together population cohorts and genomic resources from sub-Saharan Africa, including the African Genome Variation Project, the Uganda General Population Cohort, the Genome Diversity in Africa Project and the Durban diabetes studies, to investigate the genetics of chronic disease in African populations.

label: ALLG ALL06
definition: A cohort of adolescent and young adult patients aged 15–39 with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia treated on the Australasian Leukaemia and Lymphoma Group's ALL06 minimal residual disease-stratified paediatric protocol and profiled genomically to relate genomic risk to outcome.

label: Alpe-DPD study
definition: A cohort of 1,181 adult cancer patients starting fluoropyrimidine-based therapy in 17 hospitals in the Netherlands, genotyped prospectively for DPYD variants and analysed genome-wide to identify variants linked to severe fluoropyrimidine toxicity.

label: APCDR Diabetes Case Control Study
definition: A collection of type 2 diabetes cases of Zulu descent assembled by the African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research for studies of the genetic basis of diabetes in African populations.

label: Atlas of Blood Cancer Genomes
definition: A project that assembles and sequences cohorts of patients with distinct blood cancers, including blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, high-grade B-cell lymphoma and T lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma, to build a genomic atlas of haematological malignancies.

label: Australian childhood AML cohort
definition: A cohort of Australian children with acute myeloid leukaemia whose exomes were analysed for rare germline variants in cancer predisposition genes, compared with the Medical Genome Reference Bank and the TARGET cohort.

label: BEACON eczema drug trial
definition: A cohort of patients with atopic dermatitis enrolled in the BEACON eczema drug trial, whose skin and blood samples were profiled by spatial and single-cell transcriptomics and genome sequencing to define cell-cell interactions in atopic dermatitis skin.

label: Beat AML
definition: A cohort of patients with acute myeloid leukaemia enrolled by the Beat AML programme in the United States, whose tumour specimens were characterised by exome and RNA sequencing and ex vivo drug sensitivity testing to guide precision therapy.

label: Belgian Approach of Local Laboratory Extensive Tumor Testing
definition: A cohort of cancer patients enrolled in the BALLETT precision oncology study of the Belgian Society of Medical Oncology, in which broad molecular tumour profiling was performed in a standardised way by local Belgian diagnostic laboratories to show its value for patient care.

label: BELLINI trial
definition: A cohort of patients with early-stage triple negative breast cancer treated in the adaptive phase 2 BELLINI trial with short neoadjuvant nivolumab alone or with ipilimumab, whose tumours were exome sequenced to study immune activation and pathological response.

label: Blood First Assay Screening Trial
definition: A global open-label multicohort trial of patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer whose targetable alterations were identified by blood-based molecular testing, evaluating the efficacy and safety of matched therapies such as entrectinib in ROS1-positive disease.

label: Born in Bradford
definition: A birth cohort of 13,858 babies and their families recruited during 2007–2011 in the city of Bradford in the north of England, about half of Pakistani heritage, followed prospectively to investigate the determinants of childhood health and used for autozygosity and exome sequencing studies.

label: CALGB 40601
definition: A cohort of women with HER2-positive breast cancer enrolled in the Cancer and Leukemia Group B 40601 phase III trial of neoadjuvant paclitaxel with trastuzumab and/or lapatinib, profiled alongside NeoALTTO for immune features that predict prognosis.

label: Cambridge Biorepository for Translational Medicine
definition: A biorepository of tissue and blood samples from organ and tissue donors in Cambridge, United Kingdom, whose donors have been genotyped genome-wide to support Human Cell Atlas and translational research.

label: Canadian Airways Research Group
definition: A cohort of patients with idiopathic or trauma-induced subglottic stenosis and controls enrolled prospectively by the Canadian Airways Research Group to investigate the clinical, transcriptional and genetic features of the disease.

label: Canadian Prostate Cancer Genome Network
definition: A cohort of men with intermediate-risk prostate cancer whose tumour genomes, including multiple regions from the same gland, were sequenced by the Canadian Prostate Cancer Genome Network to identify genetic signatures of treatment response.

label: Cancer Genomics of the Kidney
definition: A collection of constitutional and tumour DNA pairs from patients with conventional clear cell renal carcinoma assembled by the CAGEKID project of the International Cancer Genome Consortium for comprehensive analysis of somatic and constitutional variation, methylation and expression.

label: CeDNN
definition: A Dutch cohort of patients with treated coeliac disease and controls whose faecal microbiomes were characterised by shotgun metagenomic sequencing, analysed alongside the Lifelines Dutch Microbiome Project.

label: CENet Cohort
definition: A cohort of patients with genetic generalized epilepsy or non-acquired focal epilepsy collected at the CHUM Research Center in Montreal, Canada, and whole-genome sequenced to investigate the genetics of epilepsy.

label: CHILD Cohort Study
definition: A Canadian birth cohort of over 3,600 children recruited during pregnancy in four provinces and followed with environmental, clinical, genetic and microbiome measurements to investigate the developmental origins of asthma, allergy and other chronic conditions.

label: City of Hope triple negative breast cancer cohort
definition: A cohort of patients with primary, treatment-naive triple negative breast cancer at City of Hope National Medical Center whose tumours were whole-genome and RNA sequenced to relate BRCA and immune configurations to response to platinum-based chemotherapy.

label: CLUSTER consortium
definition: A United Kingdom consortium that harmonises juvenile idiopathic arthritis and uveitis cohorts and trials, including CAPS, CHARMS and the UK JIA Biologics register, to discover disease mechanisms and biomarkers of treatment response in childhood arthritis.

label: COMPARE study
definition: A cohort of 29,066 British blood donors enrolled during 2016–2017 to find the optimum technology for haemoglobin screening, of whom 4,796 consented to join the NIHR BioResource and were genotyped during the development of the UK Biobank version 2 array.

label: COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative
definition: A worldwide collaborative initiative that brings together COVID-19 case and population cohorts to identify genetic determinants of SARS-CoV-2 infection susceptibility and COVID-19 severity through meta-analysis and shared individual-level data.

label: CRCbiome
definition: A prospective biomarker cohort nested within the Bowel Cancer Screening in Norway trial, recruiting participants with a positive faecal immunochemical test since 2017 for gut metagenome, diet and lifestyle assessment before and after colonoscopy.

label: DERMATLAS
definition: A collection of 70 skin tumour subtypes defined by the World Health Organization, sampled from a range of body sites for whole exome, transcriptome and methylation sequencing to build a genomic atlas of dermatological tumours.

label: Diagnosis and Management of Febrile Illness using RNA Personalised Molecular Signature Diagnosis
definition: A cohort of children and adults with febrile illness, including multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children, Kawasaki disease and bacterial and viral infections, recruited prospectively at hospitals in the United Kingdom and the European Union by the DIAMONDS consortium to develop blood transcriptomic diagnostic signatures.

label: DKTK MASTER
definition: A prospective observational precision oncology cohort of the German Cancer Consortium that enrols adults with advanced cancer who are younger than 51 and patients with rare tumours regardless of age, and uses whole-genome or exome and transcriptome sequencing to inform their care.

label: Donor InSight III study
definition: A cohort of 3,046 Dutch blood donors recruited by Sanquin Research during 2015–2016 to gain insight into the characteristics, motivations and health of donors, genotyped during the development of the UK Biobank version 2 array.

label: East London Genes and Health
definition: A cohort of British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani adults recruited in east London and later across England, with consent for recall by genotype, established to find rare homozygous functional variants in healthy humans and to study health in South Asian communities.

label: Egyptian Collaborative Cardiac Genomics Project
definition: A cohort of Egyptian healthy volunteers free of cardiovascular disease, of whom 391 were recruited as a pilot phenotyped control cohort with cardiac MRI and targeted sequencing of inherited cardiac condition genes, to define the genetic landscape of an understudied North African population.

label: EMC-DC-IL10R study
definition: A study cohort of healthy donors, a patient with IL10RA deficiency and children with severe paediatric inflammatory bowel disease at Erasmus MC, whose monocyte-derived dendritic cells and blood mononuclear cells were profiled by RNA sequencing to investigate IL-10 control of T-cell responses.

label: Emirati Genome Program
definition: A national programme of the United Arab Emirates that sequences the genomes of Emirati citizens, 43,608 of whom have been characterised for population-scale variant discovery and allele frequencies.

label: Entebbe Mother and Baby study
definition: A birth cohort of children in Entebbe, southern Uganda, followed from birth with measures of response to infant vaccinations, malaria episodes, infection and atopy, and genotyped to investigate genetic determinants of vaccine response in sub-Saharan Africa.

label: EORTC-SPECTA RP1759
definition: A cohort of adolescent and young adult patients aged 12 to 29 with newly diagnosed or relapsed high-grade glioma recruited across Europe from 2019 in the EORTC SPECTA RP1759 study to bridge the molecular gap between paediatric and adult oncology.

label: ESTAMPA
definition: A multicentre cohort of women screened for cervical cancer with human papillomavirus testing in Latin America, whose cervical cells were duplex sequenced to explore the somatic driver landscape of healthy and pre-cancerous cervical tissue.

label: Estonian Microbiome Cohort
definition: A sub-cohort of 2,509 Estonian Biobank participants who provided stool, oral and plasma samples, supplemented with multi-omic measurements, questionnaires and linkage to national electronic health records to investigate the gut microbiome.

label: Etude des Déterminants pré et postnatals précoces du développement et de la santé de l'Enfant
definition: A French mother-child cohort of pregnancies recruited in Nancy and Poitiers during 2003–2006 to investigate the pre- and early postnatal determinants of child development and health, contributing to the MeDALL allergy project.

label: EuroEPINOMICS
definition: A European Science Foundation research networking programme of epilepsy genetics groups whose member sites contribute patients with epilepsy and related paroxysmal neurological disorders, mostly with a strong family history, to joint sequencing studies.

label: European BestAgeing Study
definition: A multicentre European cohort of 1,209 patients with acute coronary syndrome, chronic coronary artery disease, dilated cardiomyopathy or ischaemic cardiomyopathy and 848 controls, whose circulating microRNA profiles were measured to evaluate disease classification and prognosis.

label: Extended Cohort for E-health, Environment and DNA
definition: A longitudinal population-based cohort of approximately 10,000 adults aged 30–69 recruited since 2013 in Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland, United Kingdom, with baseline data and electronic health record linkage to investigate genetic, environmental and lifestyle determinants of disease and multimorbidity.

label: Genome Database of Latvian Population
definition: A national biobank of the Latvian population, 502 of whose participants were whole-genome sequenced at high coverage to build the first Latvian population-specific reference panel.

label: Genome Diversity in Africa Project
definition: A project of the African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research that performs high-depth whole-genome sequencing of up to 2,000 individuals from ethnolinguistic groups across sub-Saharan Africa to catalogue human genetic variation on the continent.

label: Genome Research at Fundació ACE
definition: A cohort of 4,120 Alzheimer's disease cases diagnosed at the Fundació ACE Memory Clinic in Barcelona and 3,289 controls from Spanish collections, genotyped genome-wide to study Alzheimer's disease susceptibility.

label: Genomic Advances in Sepsis
definition: A biobank of adult patients with sepsis due to community-acquired pneumonia or faecal peritonitis recruited from 35 hospitals across the United Kingdom during 2005–2018, with samples for functional genomics and detailed clinical data collected over the first days of intensive care.

label: German Cancer Consortium
definition: A consortium of German cancer centres, coordinated by the German Cancer Research Center in Heidelberg, that runs joint translational research programmes such as the DKTK MASTER precision oncology cohort.

label: German MI cohort
definition: A collection of German patients with early-onset myocardial infarction and a strong family history of coronary artery disease, used with the UK BHF CAD/MI cohort as the case set of the Cardiogenics re-sequencing study.

label: GMMG-BIRMA trial
definition: A cohort of twelve patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma carrying an activating BRAF V600E mutation, enrolled in the German-speaking Myeloma Multicenter Group's phase II trial of encorafenib and binimetinib and genomically profiled to identify drivers of resistance.

label: Gutenberg Health Study
definition: A population-based cohort of adults from Mainz and the Mainz-Bingen district in Germany, recruited from 2007 and followed with cardiovascular, metabolic, ophthalmological and psychological phenotyping to investigate the determinants of cardiovascular and other common diseases.

label: Haematological Malignancy Research Network
definition: A population-based cohort of all patients newly diagnosed with a haematological malignancy since 2004 within two adjacent United Kingdom cancer networks covering about four million people, diagnosed by a single integrated laboratory and followed with treatment and outcome data.

label: Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe study
definition: A prospective cohort study of urban adults in the Czech Republic, Poland, Russia and Lithuania designed to investigate the effect of classical, non-conventional, social and psychosocial risk factors on cardiovascular and other non-communicable diseases in eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union.

label: Healthy Life in an Urban Setting
definition: A longitudinal multi-ethnic population-based cohort of over 25,000 residents of Amsterdam, the Netherlands, of Dutch, Surinamese, Turkish, Moroccan and Ghanaian origin, followed with examinations, questionnaires and gut microbiome sampling to investigate ethnic differences in health.

label: ICGC Gastric Cancer China project
definition: A collection of 340 gastric cancer cases contributed to the International Cancer Genome Consortium by its Chinese gastric cancer project.

label: ICGC Gynecological Carcinosarcoma project
definition: A collection of 20 carcinosarcomas of the endometrium or ovary whose carcinomatous and sarcomatous components were characterised by whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing and methylome arrays within the International Cancer Genome Consortium.

label: ICGC India Project
definition: A collection of paired tumour and blood DNA samples from patients with gingivobuccal cancer of the oral cavity, the most prevalent cancer among men in India, recruited at the Advanced Centre for Research, Treatment and Education on Cancer in Mumbai for India's contribution to the International Cancer Genome Consortium.

label: ICGC Liver Cancer China project
definition: A collection of 88 hepatocellular carcinomas with matched adjacent normal tissue whose genomes were sequenced within the International Cancer Genome Consortium's Chinese liver cancer project to identify alterations in druggable driver genes.

label: ICGC MMML-Seq
definition: A collection of germinal-centre B-cell derived lymphomas, including Burkitt, follicular and diffuse large B-cell lymphomas from children and adults, sequenced by the German ICGC MMML-Seq project of the International Cancer Genome Consortium.

label: ICGC Oesophageal Adenocarcinoma project
definition: A collection of oesophageal adenocarcinoma tumours, Barrett's oesophagus and lymph-node samples with matched normal DNA, gathered through the UK-wide OCCAMS hospital network for the International Cancer Genome Consortium to catalogue somatic mutations in this cancer.

label: ICGC Pancreatic Cancer project
definition: A collection of 112 pancreatic cancer samples whole-genome sequenced within the International Cancer Genome Consortium's pancreatic cancer project.

label: ICGC PedBrain Tumor Project
definition: A collection of paediatric brain tumours, including medulloblastomas, low-grade astrocytomas and glioblastomas, with matched normal samples, characterised by whole-genome, RNA and methylation sequencing within the International Cancer Genome Consortium's PedBrain Tumor Project.

label: ICGC Prostate Cancer UK project
definition: A collection of prostate cancers with whole-genome, transcriptome and methylome data generated from 2011 under the International Cancer Genome Consortium's Prostate Cancer UK project, to understand multifocal disease, clinical heterogeneity, castration resistance and metastasis.

label: ICR MOPOPGEN UK exome control series
