definition: A longitudinal multicentre genetic-neuroimaging cohort of about 2,000 healthy 14-year-old adolescents recruited from high schools at eight European sites in England, Ireland, France and Germany, followed up at ages 16, 19 and 22 with behavioural, neuropsychological, MRI and genome-wide data, to study the genetic and neurobiological basis of impulsivity, reinforcer sensitivity and emotional reactivity and their value in predicting psychiatric disorders.

label: Munich Antidepressant Response Signature
definition: A naturalistic, open-label longitudinal treatment study of inpatients admitted with a moderate to severe unipolar or bipolar depressive episode to the hospital of the Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry in Munich and collaborating hospitals in Southern Bavaria and Switzerland, characterised clinically, neuroendocrinologically (dex/CRH test) and genetically and followed weekly during treatment, to identify predictors of antidepressant treatment response.

label: Minority Aging Research Study
definition: A longitudinal epidemiologic cohort of older African Americans without known dementia, recruited from 2004 from churches, senior buildings and community organisations in the Chicago metropolitan area and followed at Rush University Medical Center, with optional brain donation, to study decline in cognitive function and risk of Alzheimer disease.

label: Older Australian Twins Study
definition: A longitudinal study of Australian twins aged 65 years and over, with some of their equivalently aged siblings, recruited through the Australian Twin Registry and a recruitment drive and assessed every two years with psychiatric, neuropsychological, cardiovascular, metabolic, neuroimaging and genetic measures, to study genetic and environmental influences on healthy brain ageing and ageing-related neurocognitive disorders.

label: LymeProspect
definition: A prospective observational cohort of adults with proven or probable Lyme borreliosis in the Netherlands, included at the start of antibiotic treatment from 2015 and followed for one year with questionnaires and repeated blood sampling, run by RIVM with the Lyme borreliosis expert centres of Amsterdam UMC and Radboudumc to study the prevalence and determinants of persistent symptoms after treatment.

label: 300-Tanzania-FG
definition: A cross-sectional cohort of 323 healthy adults aged 18-65 living in the Kilimanjaro region of northern Tanzania, enrolled within the Human Functional Genomics Project by Radboudumc and Tanzanian partners, with ex vivo cytokine stimulations at the Kilimanjaro Clinical Research Institute in Moshi, to study genetic and environmental determinants of immune responses in an African population.

label: UCLA ATLAS Community Health Initiative
definition: An ancestrally diverse biobank embedded in the UCLA Health medical system in Los Angeles County, run by the UCLA Institute for Precision Health, that links genomic data from blood samples of consenting UCLA Health patients (36,736 genotyped in 2022) to their de-identified electronic health records, for genetic and precision-health research.

label: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Family Study
definition: A family study of Hispanic (Mexican American) families recruited at clinical centres in San Antonio, Texas and the San Luis Valley, Colorado and African American families recruited in Los Angeles, California, selected on family size rather than health status and examined with CT scans of visceral fat and frequently sampled glucose tolerance tests, to identify the genetic and environmental determinants of insulin resistance and visceral adiposity.

label: WHI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network
definition: A nested case-control genome-wide association sub-study of the Women's Health Initiative hormone therapy trials, comprising the coronary heart disease, stroke, venous thromboembolism and selected diabetes cases that arose during the active intervention phase and age-matched controls, genotyped under the NHGRI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network (GARNET).

label: ALS Utrecht
definition: A case-control sample of 158 people of European ancestry, patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and healthy controls, from University Medical Center Utrecht, the Netherlands, with longitudinal 3.0 T brain MRI and whole-genome sequencing, contributed to the ENIGMA Plasticity Working Group genome-wide meta-analysis of brain structure change.

label: Brain Imaging Genetics study
definition: A pool of self-reported healthy volunteers, many of them university students, who took part in diverse imaging studies at the Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, and consented to pooling of their anatomical MRI scans with DNA for imaging genetics; established in 2007 and now part of the Cognomics initiative.

label: BrainSCALE study
definition: A longitudinal study of Dutch twin families recruited from the Netherlands Twin Register, starting with 112 families of 9-year-old twins and an older sibling who were assessed at three-year intervals with IQ and neuropsychological tests, behavioural ratings, pubertal hormones, brain MRI and DNA collection, to study genetic and environmental influences on brain structure and cognition from childhood into adolescence.

label: Norwegian Cognitive NeuroGenetics sample
definition: A genetically homogeneous sample of healthy Norwegian adults spanning the adult life span, collected from 2003 to study cognitive ageing and genetic risk factors and genome-wide genotyped in 2009, with MRI and experimental cognitive data on attention and working memory, for studies of the genetics of cognitive and brain function.

label: NeuroIMAGE study
definition: A multi-site prospective cohort following up the Dutch families of the International Multicenter ADHD Genetics project together with newly recruited families, comprising 1,069 children from ADHD and control families and 848 parents assessed with diagnostic interviews, questionnaires, cognitive tests, structural and functional MRI and genome-wide genotyping, to study the course of ADHD into adolescence and adulthood and its genetic, environmental and neural underpinnings.

label: Inter99 Study
definition: A population-based randomised non-pharmacological lifestyle intervention trial for the prevention of ischaemic heart disease, run in 1999–2006 at the Research Centre for Prevention and Health in Glostrup, Copenhagen, Denmark, on random samples of adults aged 30–60 drawn from a population of 61,301 and followed through questionnaires and central registers.

label: iPSYCH case-cohort study
definition: A Danish population-based case-cohort sample established by the Lundbeck Foundation Initiative for Integrative Psychiatric Research (iPSYCH) to study the genetic and environmental architecture of severe mental disorders, combining persons diagnosed with schizophrenia, autism, ADHD or affective disorder with a random sample of the population, genotyped from neonatal dried blood spots in the Danish Neonatal Screening Biobank and linked to national registers. Its first wave (iPSYCH2012, 86,189 individuals born 1981-2005) was expanded as iPSYCH2015 to 141,265 samples, including 50,615 population controls, nested within the Danish population born 1981-2008 and adding schizophrenia spectrum and post-partum disorder cases.

label: Long Life Family Study
definition: A longitudinal, multicentre, multinational family study of 4,953 members of 539 two-generation families selected for exceptional familial longevity, recruited in 2006-2009 through field centres in Boston, New York and Pittsburgh in the United States and in Denmark and re-examined in 2014-2017, to study the genetic and non-genetic determinants of exceptional longevity and healthy ageing.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD
definition: A multicentre observational cohort of about 10,000 non-Hispanic white and African American current and former smokers with and without COPD, aged 45-80, enrolled at 21 clinical centres across the United States and followed longitudinally with chest CT imaging and genome-wide genotyping to identify genetic factors and CT-defined subtypes of COPD.

label: Genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of a representative sample of healthy adults aged 25-41 in the Principality of Liechtenstein, enrolled from June 2010 without cardiovascular disease, diabetes or severe obesity, with ambulatory blood pressure, Holter ECG, spirometry, sleep oximetry and blood, urine and genetic sampling, and followed up every 3-5 years to study genetic and phenotypic predictors of cardiovascular risk factors in young adults.

label: Women's Genome Health Study
definition: A prospective genome-wide association cohort of more than 25,000 initially healthy American female health professionals aged 45 or older from the Women's Health Study who gave a baseline blood sample, followed since 1992 for incident cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes and other outcomes.

label: Cameron County Hispanic Cohort
definition: A community-based cohort of Mexican Americans in Brownsville, Cameron County, Texas, on the United States-Mexico border, established in 2004 by the University of Texas School of Public Health Brownsville campus from households in randomly selected census tract blocks, to study the prevalence and determinants of obesity, diabetes and related chronic disease in this population.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium
definition: A US consortium that assembles genome-wide genotype data and harmonized phenotypes from many case-control, family-based, population-based and longitudinal Alzheimer disease cohorts, in more than 30 GWAS datasets of several ancestries, for genetic studies of late-onset Alzheimer disease.

label: Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America
definition: A sample of about 7,300 adult volunteers of mixed African, European and Native American ancestry, mostly university students and staff (and, in Chile, mainly soldiers), recruited by a consortium of Latin American and UK groups in México City, Medellín, Lima, Arica and Porto Alegre and characterised for physical appearance, facial photographs, self-perceived ancestry and genetic ancestry, with genome-wide genotyping of about 6,000 of them, to study admixture and the genetics of physical traits in Latin America.

label: Mexico City Prospective Study
definition: A prospective cohort of more than 150,000 adults aged 35 and over, recruited in 1998-2004 from the contiguous urban districts of Coyoacán and Iztapalapa in Mexico City with the University of Oxford, and followed to investigate known and new risk factors for mortality in people of Mexican descent; its participants have exome and genome-wide genetic data.

label: Airwave Health Monitoring Study
definition: An occupational cohort of police officers and staff of police forces across Great Britain, enrolled from 2004 (42,112 participants by the end of 2012, most of whom attended a health screening with questionnaires, food diaries, physical and cognitive measurements and stored blood and urine), set up to evaluate possible health risks of the TETRA digital radio system and broadened to study the health of the police workforce.

label: Cohorte Lausannoise
definition: A population-based cohort of a random sample of 6,188 Caucasian adults aged 35 to 75 living in Lausanne, Switzerland, extensively phenotyped and genotyped genome-wide at baseline to study the prevalence and genetic determinants of cardiovascular risk factors and the metabolic syndrome, and followed up prospectively (with its psychiatric arm PsyCoLaus) from 2003 for cardiovascular events and mortality.

label: Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 41,513 middle-aged and older adults of white European origin, almost all aged 40–69, recruited in Melbourne, Australia, in 1990–1994 by Cancer Council Victoria and followed up face to face in 2003–2007 and by record linkage to cancer and death registries, collecting socio-demographic, lifestyle and health data to study risk factors for cancer and other chronic diseases.

label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey
definition: A Dutch prospective cohort study, run in the North of the Netherlands, consisting of a population cohort of 2,230 children born between October 1989 and September 1991 and a clinical cohort of 543 children referred to child psychiatric outpatient care before age 11, followed from about age 11 into young adulthood with repeated assessments of mental health, social development and physical health.

label: ADDITION-PRO Study
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of 2,082 Danish adults at different levels of diabetes risk, sampled from the 16,136 high-risk individuals identified by the 2001–2006 stepwise diabetes screening programme in Danish general practice of the Danish arm of ADDITION-Europe, examined in 2009–2011 with detailed cardiometabolic phenotyping and followed for cardiovascular disease and death.

label: Finnish Cardiovascular Study
definition: A clinical cohort of about 4,500 patients scheduled for an exercise stress test at Tampere University Hospital, Finland, recruited between October 2001 and December 2007 with continuous high-resolution ECG, haemodynamic measurements, genotyping and follow-up of clinical events and deaths, to construct risk profiles for cardiovascular disease, events and death.

label: Health Professionals Follow-up Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 51,529 US male health professionals aged 40 to 75 enrolled in 1986, whose demographics, health, diet and lifestyle are updated by questionnaire every two years (diet every four), with follow-up exceeding 90% of eligible person-time.

label: ARGO study
definition: A Greek collection of more than 1,500 well-phenotyped patients with severe hip or knee osteoarthritis undergoing total joint replacement, recruited in hospitals of Athens (2015-2017) and Larissa together with healthy controls, set up to study the genetic architecture of osteoarthritis.

label: Ansan and Ansung Study
definition: A community-based prospective cohort of 10,030 men and women aged 40–69 from the urban city of Ansan and the rural town of Ansung (Anseong) in Gyeonggi Province, South Korea, recruited in 2001–2002 as the first cohort of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study and re-surveyed every two years, to study common chronic diseases and their genetic and environmental risk factors.

label: Nagahama Prospective Cohort for Comprehensive Human Bioscience
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of about 9,800 residents aged 30–74 years of Nagahama City, a largely rural city in Shiga Prefecture, central Japan, recruited in 2008–2010 and run from Kyoto University Graduate School of Medicine, with blood samples, questionnaires, health examinations, genotyping and follow-up examinations (the first in 2013–2016) for genomic and clinical research.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease Genetics Consortium
definition: An international collaborative consortium, co-directed by Anna Köttgen and Cristian Pattaro with its data hosted at the University of Freiburg, that meta-analyses genome-wide association results from many, mostly population-based, studies to investigate the genetic basis of kidney function and disease, releasing summary statistics for markers such as estimated glomerular filtration rate and blood urea nitrogen.

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Project
definition: A Japanese genome cohort project launched after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and run by the Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization of Tohoku University and the Iwate Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization of Iwate Medical University, comprising two prospective cohorts in Miyagi and Iwate Prefectures, the TMM Community-Based Cohort Study of adults and the TMM Birth and Three-Generation Cohort Study, with an integrated biobank of health information, biospecimens and genome and omics data.

label: Fred Hutchinson Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A prostate cancer study run at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center that comprises two population-based case-control studies in King County, Washington, whose cases, identified through the Seattle-Puget Sound SEER cancer registry, were men aged 40–64 diagnosed in 1993–1996 and men aged 35–74 diagnosed in 2002–2005, and whose controls without prostate cancer were found by random-digit dialling and frequency-matched to cases by age; its genotyped samples contribute to the PRACTICAL consortium.

label: Whole Genome Association Analysis of Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT) Outcomes
definition: A retrospective cohort of patients with a haematological malignancy or myelodysplastic syndrome who had a first allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center and Seattle Cancer Care Alliance from 1990 to 2011, together with their donors, genotyped to find variants associated with graft-versus-host disease, recurrent malignancy and other complications after transplantation.

label: Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium
definition: A collaborative consortium that combines genome-wide association and exome-array data from many cohorts of individuals without diabetes in meta-analyses of glycaemic traits (fasting glucose, fasting insulin, 2-hour glucose and HbA1c) and measures of insulin secretion and sensitivity, to find loci influencing glycaemic and metabolic traits, and releases its summary results.

label: Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Childhood Study
definition: A UK study of the molecular genetics of adverse drug reactions in children, recruiting carefully phenotyped retrospective cohorts of treated children at UK hospitals; its cisplatin cohort comprises platinum-treated paediatric cancer patients recruited between 2012 and 2018 at eight UK sites for genetic studies of ototoxicity.

label: Raine Study
definition: A pregnancy cohort in Western Australia for which 2,900 pregnant women were recruited between 1989 and 1991 at King Edward Memorial Hospital, Perth, and nearby private clinics, with the mothers (Generation 1) and their 2,868 offspring (Generation 2) followed from 18 weeks' gestation through childhood and adolescence into adulthood, to study how early life shapes later health and behaviour.

label: Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial population of 5,804 men and women aged 70 to 82 with pre-existing vascular disease or risk factors for it, screened in Scotland, Ireland and the Netherlands and randomised to pravastatin 40 mg/day or placebo for about 3.2 years to test whether statin treatment reduces coronary and cerebrovascular events in the elderly.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt Sensitivity
definition: A family feeding study in rural northern China that recruited 3,153 Han Chinese participants from 658 families, each ascertained through a proband with untreated prehypertension or stage-1 hypertension, of whom 1,906 eligible probands and their siblings, spouses and offspring underwent seven-day low-sodium, high-sodium and high-sodium with potassium supplementation dietary interventions, to localise and identify genes influencing blood pressure responses to dietary sodium and potassium.

label: Kaiser Permanente Research Bank
definition: A research resource of Kaiser Permanente, launched in May 2016 and built on the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, that collects biospecimens and surveys linked to electronic health records from consenting adult members across Kaiser Permanente's eight US regions (about 396,000 consented by July 2021), with general, pregnancy and cancer cohorts.

label: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
definition: A collection of longitudinal, community-representative twin and adoptive family studies in Minnesota, including the Minnesota Twin Registry, the Minnesota Twin Family Study, the Enrichment Study, the Adolescent Brain study and the Sibling Interaction and Behavior Study, focusing on psychological adjustment, personality, cognitive ability and brain function with an emphasis on substance use and related psychopathology.

label: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease
definition: A prospective cohort of about 1,500 healthy men and women of European ancestry aged 30 to 60, recruited without diabetes, hypertension or dyslipidaemia at centres in 13-14 European countries by the European Group for the Study of Insulin Resistance, with baseline oral glucose tolerance tests and euglycaemic insulin clamps and follow-up after 3 and 10 years to study how insulin resistance relates to atherosclerosis, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.

label: Rotterdam Study I
definition: The first cohort of the Rotterdam Study, a prospective population-based cohort of 7,983 inhabitants aged 55 and over of Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands, started in 1990 and re-examined about every 4 years with home interviews and clinical assessments to study determinants of chronic diseases in older adults.

label: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
definition: A longitudinal cohort of about 11,500 children aged 9-10, including about 1,720 twins, recruited largely through schools at 21 data acquisition sites across the United States to reflect the nation's diversity, and followed for ten years with annual assessments and biennial MRI to study adolescent brain and cognitive development.

label: Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
definition: A pharmacogenetic study established in 2007 at Massachusetts General Hospital, which from 2008 enrolled about 1,000 adults of diverse ancestry enriched for risk of type 2 diabetes and challenged them with glipizide and metformin at clinical research centres in Boston, Massachusetts, to identify genetic variants influencing the acute response to glucose-lowering drugs.

label: Colon Cancer Family Registry
definition: An international registry and cohort, funded by the US National Cancer Institute and begun in 1997, of colorectal cancer cases, their unaffected relatives and population-based controls recruited through six centres in Australasia and North America (the Australasian, Mayo Clinic, Ontario, Seattle, University of Hawaii and USC Consortium registries), as a resource for research on familial and sporadic colorectal cancer.

label: DIAbetes COhoRtE
definition: A prospective cohort of about 3,000 adult outpatients of self-reported Caucasian ethnicity with prevalent type 2 diabetes, recruited in 2010–2014 at two university-based study centres in Germany and followed with biennial visits, core phenotyping and biobanking for at least 10 years to study diabetes complications, with a primary focus on renal events.

label: Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study
definition: A US prospective multicentre cohort of men aged 65 or older recruited at six clinical centres (Birmingham, Minneapolis, Palo Alto, near Pittsburgh, Portland and San Diego), designed to examine risk factors for osteoporosis, fractures and prostate cancer in older men, with ancillary studies such as MrOS Sleep (2003-2005, in-home polysomnography of 3,135 men).

label: Prevention of Renal and Vascular End-stage Disease study
definition: A Dutch population-based cohort of 8,592 residents of the city of Groningen aged 28 to 75, enrolled in 1997-1998 from 40,856 respondents who sent a morning urine sample, enriched for people with urinary albumin of at least 10 mg/L plus a random control sample, and followed up to study renal and cardiovascular disease.

label: European Alzheimer & Dementia Biobank
definition: A European consortium bringing together the European genome-wide association consortia working on Alzheimer disease, which collated and uniformly genotyped a new dataset of about 20,000 clinically diagnosed Alzheimer disease cases and 22,000 controls from 15 European countries and pools them with existing European cohorts for genetic studies of Alzheimer disease and related dementias.

label: INTERSTROKE Study
definition: An international multicentre case-control study of risk factors for first acute stroke, which recruited 13,462 stroke cases and 13,488 community or hospital controls matched for age, sex and region from 142 centres in 32 countries between 2007 and 2015, with a genotyped subset of consenting participants used in genetic studies of stroke.

label: Shanghai Women's Health Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of 74,942 Chinese women aged 40–70 recruited in 1996–2000 from selected urban communities of Shanghai, most of whom gave blood, urine or buccal-cell samples, followed by biennial in-person recontact and linkage to cancer and vital statistics registries, to study environmental exposures, biomarkers and the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank phase2
definition: A nested case-control sample of about 3,400 French-Canadian participants of the Montreal Heart Institute Biobank (patients with coronary artery disease and controls free of it) genotyped on the Illumina MEGA array at the Université de Montréal Beaulieu-Saucier Pharmacogenomics Centre, forming the second of the biobank's two genetic data sets.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank phase1
definition: A nested case-control sample of about 2,000 French-Canadian participants of the Montreal Heart Institute Biobank (patients with myocardial infarction and controls free of coronary artery disease) whose whole genomes were sequenced at low depth (about 5.6x) at the McGill University and Génome Québec Innovation Centre, forming the first of the biobank's two genetic data sets.

label: Darmkrebs: Chancen der Verhütung durch Screening
definition: A multicentre population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in the Rhine-Neckar region of south-west Germany, led from the German Cancer Research Center in Heidelberg, which from 2003 recruited patients aged 30 or over with a first colorectal cancer diagnosis from the 22 hospitals treating the disease in the region, and actively follows the cases to study colorectal cancer risk, prevention by screening and survival.

label: British Genetics of Hypertension study
definition: A UK resource of white European families with severe essential hypertension, collected by the Medical Research Council British Genetics of Hypertension (BRIGHT) study through the MRC General Practice Framework and other primary care practices (about 1,600 families with more than 2,000 affected sibling pairs, plus parent-offspring trios), with about 2,000 normotensive controls matched by age, sex and geography across the UK, for linkage and association studies of the genetics of hypertension.

label: Genetic Investigation of ANthropometric Traits consortium
definition: An international collaboration of investigators from many groups, institutions, countries and studies that meta-analyses genome-wide association and other large-scale genetic data to identify loci modulating human body size and shape, such as height, body mass index and waist-related traits, and releases the summary data.

label: Hong Kong Degenerative Disc Disease Population Cohort
definition: A population-based cohort of about 2,900 volunteers of Southern Chinese origin aged 15–55 in Hong Kong, openly recruited through newspaper advertisements, posters and e-mails regardless of back symptoms, who underwent lumbar spine MRI, questionnaires and genome-wide genotyping, to study the genetic and environmental determinants of intervertebral disc degeneration.

label: International Lung Cancer Consortium
definition: An international consortium established in 2004 by research groups leading large molecular epidemiology studies of lung cancer, which pools data from its member case-control and cohort studies to study lung cancer risk and prognosis; its OncoArray project genotyped about 36,000 participants of European descent.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project
definition: A US National Institutes of Health initiative, started in 2012, that sequences the exomes and whole genomes of well-characterized participants of many Alzheimer disease cohorts, first from the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium and CHARGE consortium and later from ancestrally diverse cohorts, and integrates them with harmonized phenotypes to identify genetic risk and protective variants for Alzheimer disease and related dementias. Its fourth release comprised 36,361 whole genomes from 17 cohorts in 14 countries, 45% of its unique participants of non-European ancestry, and its fifth 58,507 genomes from 57 cohorts.

label: Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey
definition: A community-based birth cohort of about 3,000 singletons born in 1983-1984 in Cebu, Philippines, and their mothers, enrolled in pregnancy and followed with bimonthly surveys for two years and repeated follow-up surveys to age 35, run by the Office of Population Studies of the University of San Carlos and the University of North Carolina to study the long-term effects of early nutrition and life conditions on health.

label: HerediGene Population Study
definition: A population genomics study launched in 2019 by Intermountain Healthcare (Utah) in partnership with deCODE genetics and Amgen, aiming to enrol up to 500,000 adult patients (more than 170,000 by 2023) whose whole-genome sequence or genotype data are linked to health records, to discover genetic biomarkers of disease and return actionable findings to participants.

label: Heart and Vascular Health Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of risk factors for cardiovascular outcomes among members of Group Health (now Kaiser Permanente Washington), an integrated health care system in western Washington State, with case groups of incident myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism and atrial fibrillation and a shared control group frequency-matched to the myocardial infarction cases. Myocardial infarction, stroke and venous thromboembolism cases were identified from diagnosis codes (and, for venous thrombosis, heparin prescriptions) and validated by medical-record review; consenting participants gave blood for genotyping, and venous thromboembolism cases were followed for recurrence.

label: Intermountain Heart Collaborative Study
definition: A prospective registry and biorepository of Intermountain Healthcare, Utah, begun in 1993, that enrols consenting patients at the cardiac catheterisation laboratories of Intermountain hospitals in Salt Lake City and Ogden, with a blood sample taken at angiography and electronic follow-up for cardiovascular outcomes such as death, myocardial infarction, heart failure and stroke. It was later renamed the INSPIRE biobank registry and now collects samples and data from consenting Intermountain patients with any health condition.

label: Johnston County Osteoarthritis Project
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of African American and white civilian, non-institutionalised adults aged 45 years or older living in six townships of Johnston County, North Carolina, sampled regardless of osteoarthritis status, of whom 3,187 were enrolled in 1991-1997 and a further 1,015 in 2003-2004 to enrich the cohort for Black and younger adults, and followed about every five years to estimate the incidence and progression of knee and hip osteoarthritis and later of hand, spine and foot osteoarthritis.

label: London Life Sciences Prospective Population Study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of about 28,000 Indian Asian (South Asian) and European men and women aged 35 to 75, recruited in 2003-2008 from the lists of 58 general practitioners in West London, UK, with a structured cardiovascular and metabolic assessment and stored blood, to study the excess cardiometabolic risk of South Asians.

label: Asian Skin Traits and Genetics Research
definition: A cohort of 2,762 women from Korea, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia, established by Korean researchers with measurements of 26 skin traits, skin-related surveys and whole-genome sequencing-based genotyping, to study the genetic and non-genetic determinants of skin traits and their variation across Asian countries.

label: Diet, Activity and Lifestyle Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of colon cancer, with cases diagnosed in 1991–1994 and age- and sex-matched controls recruited from the Kaiser Permanente Medical Care Program of Northern California, Utah and the Twin Cities of Minnesota, extended in 1997–2001 by a parallel study of rectal cancer in Utah and Kaiser Permanente, collecting diet, physical activity and other lifestyle data to study their relation to colorectal cancer.

label: Invecchiare in Chianti
definition: A prospective population-based study of aging of 1,453 residents aged 20 to 102, mostly older people, selected by multistage sampling from the registries of Greve in Chianti and Bagno a Ripoli in Tuscany, Italy, examined at baseline in 1998-2000 and followed up to identify risk factors for the loss of walking ability and other age-related decline.

label: Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Study
definition: A Japanese multi-institutional genome cohort, launched in 2005, of 92,610 adults aged 35–69 years from 14 study regions in 12 prefectures (respondents to study announcements, people attending local-government health checkups or health checkup centres, and first-visit patients at a cancer hospital), who gave baseline questionnaire data and blood samples in 2005–2014 and are followed until 2025, to examine gene–environment interactions in lifestyle-related diseases, mainly cancer.

label: Nijmegen Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A case-control study of urinary bladder cancer run from Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, in which patients diagnosed from 1995 to 2010 under the age of 76 and living in the catchment area of seven hospitals in the east of the country were identified through the Netherlands Cancer Registry and invited in batches, with controls drawn from the Nijmegen Biomedical Study, to study genetic and lifestyle risk factors and outcomes of bladder cancer.

label: Norwegian Breast Cancer Study
definition: A Norwegian breast cancer case-control study in the Breast Cancer Association Consortium, whose cases are incident breast cancers from Ullevål University Hospital (1990–1994), the Norwegian Radium Hospital (1975–1986 and 1995–1998) and Haukeland University Hospital (1992–2001) and whose controls are women from Tromsø and Bergen who attended the Norwegian Breast Cancer Screening Program. It also includes a sub-study of women attending the national mammography screening programme in 2002–2007 who gave blood and breast biopsies with mammographic density measurements, and its normal and tumour breast tissue samples are used in gene expression studies.

label: QSkin Sun and Health Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 43,794 men and women aged 40–69 randomly sampled from the population of Queensland, Australia, in 2011, with baseline questionnaires on pigmentation, sun exposure, sun protection and skin cancer history and linkage to national health insurance, cancer registry and pathology records, to study the development of skin cancer and melanoma in the population with the highest reported incidence in the world.

label: RIKEN Study
definition: A Japanese knee osteoarthritis case-control collection assembled at the RIKEN Center for Genomic Medicine, of about 900 symptomatic knee osteoarthritis cases diagnosed by orthopaedic surgeons from clinical and radiographic examination at several Japanese medical institutes and about 3,400 controls from BioBank Japan and Osaka volunteers, genotyped genome-wide to find knee osteoarthritis susceptibility loci.

label: RIKEN cohort
definition: A Japanese pharmacogenetic cohort of 219 patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma treated with sunitinib, recruited from 15 Japanese medical institutes with data collected at the laboratory for pharmacogenomics of the RIKEN Center for Integrative Medical Sciences, to study germline genetic variants related to sunitinib toxicity and efficacy.

label: Swedish Mammography Cohort
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of women born 1914–1948 living in Uppsala and Västmanland counties in central Sweden, established in 1987–1990 among the 90,303 women invited to mammography screening who completed a food frequency questionnaire, re-surveyed in 1997 and followed through linkage to Swedish national registers to study diet, lifestyle and chronic disease, notably cancer.

label: Shanghai Men's Health Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of 61,480 men aged 40–74 living in urban Shanghai, recruited from 2002 with detailed lifestyle, dietary and medical data and blood, urine and DNA samples, and followed by in-person surveys every 3–4 years and linkage with cancer and vital statistics registries, to study lifestyle, environmental and genetic contributions to cancer and other non-communicable diseases.

label: VITamins And Lifestyle Study
definition: A prospective cohort of men and women aged 50–76 living in the 13-county area of western Washington State covered by the SEER cancer registry, recruited by mailed questionnaire from October 2000 to December 2002, with about 77,700 valid baseline questionnaires, to study the use of vitamins and other dietary supplements, and lifestyle, in relation to cancer risk.

label: Western Australian Sleep Health Study
definition: A clinic-based cohort of patients of European origin attending the only public sleep clinic in Western Australia, in Perth, most of them referred for sleep-disordered breathing, with questionnaires, biochemistry, DNA and in-laboratory polysomnography collected for over 3,000 patients by 2010 towards a target of 4,000 and linkage to Western Australian health data, to study the epidemiology and genetics of obstructive sleep apnoea and its comorbidities.

label: European Medical Information Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Multimodal Biomarker Discovery study
definition: A European multimodal biomarker dataset of 1,221 people aged over 50 with normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer-type dementia and known amyloid status, whose existing clinical data, samples and scans were retrospectively combined from 11 prospective European cohort studies (three multicenter and eight single-center studies) within the Innovative Medicines Initiative-funded European Medical Information Framework, with plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, DNA and MRI data for discovery of diagnostic and prognostic Alzheimer disease biomarkers.

label: NHLBI Family Heart Study
definition: A family study of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute that recruited families, about half at high risk of coronary heart disease and half selected randomly, from existing study populations at four centres in Forsyth County (North Carolina), Framingham (Massachusetts), Minneapolis (Minnesota) and Salt Lake City (Utah), examining 5,710 participants in 1993–1995, to identify genetic and non-genetic determinants of coronary heart disease, atherosclerosis and their risk factors. Its follow-up, the Family Heart SCAN study, re-examined about a third of the participants with cardiac CT in 2002–2003 and added 622 African Americans from 211 families of hypertensive sibships previously examined by the Hypertension Genetic Epidemiology Network (HyperGEN).

label: Hyperglycemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcome Study
definition: A multinational, multi-ancestry observational cohort of more than 25,000 pregnant women enrolled in 2000-2006 at 15 field centres in Asia, Australia, the Caribbean, Europe, North America and the Middle East, who had a standardised 75 g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-32 weeks of gestation, to study the association of maternal glycaemia with adverse pregnancy and newborn outcomes; mothers were later genotyped and their children followed up.

label: Catheterization Genetics
definition: A biorepository cohort of 9,334 adults recruited sequentially at the cardiac catheterisation laboratories of Duke University, Durham, North Carolina, while undergoing evaluation for ischaemic heart disease, with fasting blood samples, genotype data and clinical data from medical records, followed for cardiovascular events and survival.

label: Colorectal Cancer Genetics & Genomics
definition: A Spanish colorectal cancer study combining two case-control studies: incident colorectal cancer cases and hospital controls recruited at the University Hospital of Bellvitge, L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (Barcelona), in 1996–1998, and cases and population controls recruited at Bellvitge and the Hospital of León in 2007–2015, genotyped to study the genetics and genomics of colorectal cancer.

label: Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Carlantino
definition: A population-based cohort of about 1,000 people from Carlantino, a small isolated village in Apulia (Foggia province), southern Italy, who underwent clinical and instrumental evaluations between 1998 and 2005; one of the isolated populations of the Italian Network of Genetic Isolates, which studies the genetic basis of complex diseases and phenotypes.

label: EPIC-InterAct Study
definition: A case-cohort study nested in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, comprising 12,403 verified incident cases of type 2 diabetes occurring in 1991-2007 among 340,234 eligible EPIC participants in eight European countries and a centre-stratified random subcohort of 16,154, assembled by the InterAct consortium to study how genes and lifestyle, especially diet and physical activity, interact in the risk of type 2 diabetes.

label: Leipzig Adults
definition: A sample of about 900 adults of European ancestry aged 18 to 99 from Leipzig, Germany, with a mean BMI of about 35 to 38 kg/m2, collected with support from the Integrated Research and Treatment Centre (IFB) AdiposityDiseases of the University of Leipzig and the German Obesity Biomaterial Bank, and genotyped on the Illumina ExomeChip and Metabochip for consortium studies of obesity-related and glycaemic traits.

label: Swiss Study on Air Pollution and Lung Diseases in Adults
definition: A population-based cohort of 9,651 adults examined in 1991 in eight areas representing the range of environmental and socio-demographic conditions in Switzerland, reassessed in 2001-2003 and 2010 with spirometry, Holter ECG and a DNA and blood biobank, set up to study the long-term effects of air pollution on lung function and respiratory and cardiovascular health.

label: Bunkyo Health Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 1,629 older adults aged 65–84 years living in Bunkyo-ku, an urban area of Tokyo, sampled from the residential registries of 13 communities chosen by probability proportionate to size, examined at the Sportology Center of Juntendo University in 2015–2018 and followed for over 10 years to study muscle function, metabolic health and ageing.

label: Shimane CoHRE Study
definition: An ongoing community cohort run by the Center for Community-based Healthcare Research and Education (CoHRE) of Shimane University, built on health examinations of community-dwelling people, largely older adults in rural towns, in Shimane Prefecture, Japan, in collaboration with local municipalities, to identify factors in healthy ageing and chronic disease.

label: Fangchenggang Area Male Health and Examination Survey
definition: A population-based study of 4,303 non-institutionalized Chinese men aged 17–88 who attended routine physical examinations at the Medical Centre of Fangchenggang First People’s Hospital in Guangxi, China, from September to December 2009, surveyed and sampled to investigate environmental and genetic factors, and their interaction, in age-related chronic diseases.

label: Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Friuli Venezia Giulia
definition: A population-based cohort of about 1,700 people from six isolated villages in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region of north-eastern Italy, examined between 2008 and 2010 in the Genetic Park of Friuli Venezia Giulia project; one of the isolated populations of the Italian Network of Genetic Isolates, which studies the genetic basis of complex diseases and phenotypes.

label: Osteoarthritis Initiative
definition: A multicentre prospective observational study of knee osteoarthritis, run as a public-private partnership between the NIH and industry, that recruited 4,796 men and women aged 45-79 at four US clinical sites in 2004-2006 into progression (symptomatic knee osteoarthritis), incidence (increased risk) and non-exposed reference subcohorts, and followed them with clinical examinations, knee radiographs at baseline and 12, 24, 36, 48, 72 and 96 months, and biospecimen collection, to identify risk factors and biomarkers for the onset and progression of knee osteoarthritis.

label: SWOG Cancer Research Network
definition: A cancer clinical trials network, formerly the Southwest Oncology Group, that is one of the network groups of the US National Cancer Institute's National Clinical Trials Network and runs multicentre cancer treatment and cancer prevention trials in adults at its member sites; its trial cohorts include the CALGB/SWOG 80405 trial in metastatic colorectal cancer, the Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial and the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial.

label: Leeds Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in the United Kingdom that recruited histologically confirmed incident cases aged 45–80, diagnosed in 1997–2000 at hospitals in Dundee, Leeds and York and in 2000–2013 in Leeds only, with controls matched for age and sex from the cases' general practice lists (supplemented after 2000 by friends or spouses of Leeds cases), all interviewed about diet, smoking and other lifestyle factors.

label: North Carolina Colon Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in African Americans and whites in 33 counties of central and eastern North Carolina, United States, in which cases aged 40–80 were identified by rapid ascertainment through the North Carolina Central Cancer Registry, African Americans were oversampled, and controls were drawn from motor vehicle and Health Care Financing Administration records. Phase I enrolled colon cancer cases from October 1996 to September 2000 and phase II (NCCCS-II) cases of sigmoid, rectosigmoid and rectal cancer from May 2001 to September 2006, both collecting interview data on diet, medication use and other risk factors.

label: Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study
definition: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of alpha-tocopherol and beta-carotene supplements for the primary prevention of lung and other cancers in 29,133 male smokers aged 50–69 in Finland, recruited in 1985–1988 and supplemented for five to eight years, whose participants have since been followed as a cohort for cancer and other outcomes.

label: Growth and Obesity Chilean Cohort Study
definition: A longitudinal cohort of 1,195 children born in 2002-2003 and recruited in 2006 at about 3.5 years of age from childcare centres of the low-to-middle income South East Area of Santiago, Chile, measured annually (six-monthly from 2010) at the Instituto de Nutrición y Tecnología en Alimentos into adolescence to study growth, puberty and obesity.

label: Health Examinees Study
definition: A population-based cohort of about 173,000 Korean men and women aged 40 and over recruited in 2004–2013 from the national health examinee registry at health examination centres, mainly in urban areas, as the largest cohort of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study, to identify environmental and genetic risk factors for major chronic diseases in Koreans.

label: Newfoundland Colorectal Cancer Registry
definition: A population-based registry of colorectal cancer patients in the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador, run from Memorial University of Newfoundland, that in 1999–2003 recruited about 750 patients diagnosed under the age of 75 to study the genetic and familial factors behind the province's high colorectal cancer incidence and has followed them for recurrence and survival for up to 19 years. For a population-based case-control study, controls frequency-matched to the cases by age group and sex were selected from the province's residents by random digit dialling.

label: Toshiba cohort
definition: A corporate genome cohort of employees of Toshiba Corporation, a Japanese electronics company, whose health-care database for precision-medicine research holds genomic, health check-up, questionnaire and prescription data of consenting employees (over 11,600 of whom had given genetic samples by 2024), used for genetic studies such as of side effects after COVID-19 booster vaccination.

label: Women's Health Initiative Memory Study
definition: A genome-wide association sub-study of the Women's Health Initiative hormone therapy trials (dbGaP WHIMS+) of European-ancestry trial participants genotyped on the Illumina HumanOmniExpress array, selected so that together with WHI GARNET they represent the WHI European American hormone trial population. It comprises the participants of the WHI Memory Study (an ancillary trial of hormone therapy and cognition in 7,479 women aged 65–80) who were not in GARNET, and other hormone trial women, aged 65 or over or younger, who were in neither WHIMS nor GARNET.

label: WHI SNP Health Association Resource
definition: A genome-wide association sub-study of the Women's Health Initiative comprising a randomly selected sample of about 8,500 African American and 3,600 Hispanic women from WHI, genotyped on the Affymetrix 6.0 array under the NHLBI SNP Health Association Resource (SHARe) project.

label: Isle of Wight Whole Population Birth Cohort
definition: A whole-population birth cohort of the children born on the Isle of Wight, England, between 1 January 1989 and 28 February 1990, of whom 1,456 were enrolled for long-term follow-up and assessed at 1, 2, 4, 10, 18 and 26 years, to study the prevalence, natural history and risk and protective factors of asthma and allergic diseases from infancy into adulthood.

label: Starr County Health Studies
definition: A long-running programme of studies of type 2 diabetes and related chronic disease among Mexican Americans in Starr County, Texas, on the Texas-Mexico border, run from the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, which include a random sample of 14% of the county's population reported in 1983, type 2 diabetes case-control collections in 1987-2006, and a household survey of randomly selected blocks with examinations in 2002-2006 and re-examinations in 2010-2014, to study the prevalence, risk factors, genetics and complications of diabetes.

label: International Multicentre ADHD Genetics project
definition: A European multi-site family sample of children aged 5 to 17 with DSM-IV combined-type ADHD, their siblings and parents, all of white European Caucasian descent, recruited in 2003-2007 at specialist ADHD clinics in eight countries for molecular genetic studies of ADHD, including candidate-gene, linkage and genome-wide association analyses; a second phase (IMAGE II) combined ADHD cases from the original project and from further clinics in Germany, the Netherlands and the UK with population controls for genome-wide association.

label: Family Blood Pressure Program
definition: An NHLBI-sponsored programme uniting four independently established multicentre family networks (GenNet, GENOA, HyperGEN and SAPPHIRe) that recruited African American, Mexican American, Asian and non-Hispanic white participants, with standardised core protocols and a pooled phenotype and genotype data set of over 11,000 individuals, to study the genetic determinants of blood pressure and hypertension.

label: Women's Health Study
definition: A randomized, double-blind trial of low-dose aspirin and vitamin E for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer among 39,876 apparently healthy US female health professionals aged 45 or older, begun in 1992 and followed as a prospective cohort for incident disease.

label: Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium
definition: An international consortium coordinated at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in Seattle that pools individual-level genetic and epidemiological data from about 70 colorectal cancer case-control, cohort and trial studies in North America, Australia, Asia and Europe, over 130,000 participants, to identify genetic risk factors and gene-environment interactions for colorectal cancer and study their effects on tumours and survival.

label: Prostate Cancer Association Group to Investigate Cancer-Associated Alterations in the Genome
definition: An international consortium of prostate cancer study groups, reported in 2008 as a worldwide consortium of 13 groups, that pools genotype and clinical data from prostate cancer case-control and cohort studies in North America, Europe, Asia and Australia to investigate inherited susceptibility to prostate cancer and its clinical course.

label: Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort
definition: A population-based cohort of 14,465 Singapore citizens and permanent residents of Chinese, Malay and Indian ethnicity aged 21 years and older, recruited in 2004–2010 mainly from the Singapore Prospective Study Program and the Singapore Cardiovascular Cohort Study, with additional recruitment oversampling Malays and Indians, to study chronic disease in a multi-ethnic Asian population.

label: ADDITION-Denmark
definition: The Danish arm of the ADDITION-Europe trial, in which people aged 40–69 without known diabetes registered with 181 general practices in Denmark were screened stepwise for diabetes in 2001–2006 and those with screen-detected type 2 diabetes, in practices cluster-randomised to routine care or intensive multifactorial treatment (with or without GP training in motivational interviewing), were followed for cardiovascular events and mortality.

label: Anglo-Danish-Dutch Study of Intensive Treatment in People with Screen Detected Diabetes in Primary Care
definition: A pragmatic cluster-randomised trial in 343 general practices in Denmark, the Netherlands and the UK, in which registered patients aged 40–69 without known diabetes were screened and the 3,057 with screen-detected type 2 diabetes received routine care or early intensive multifactorial treatment and were followed for cardiovascular events and death.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank
definition: A longitudinal hospital-based cohort and biobank of patients of the Montreal Heart Institute, a cardiology hospital enriched for cardiovascular disease, who consented to give a baseline blood sample with medical, nutritional, psychosocial, sociodemographic and lifestyle data, updated through hospital record linkage and four-yearly follow-up interviews, and who are genotyped for genetic and pharmacogenomic studies.

label: Exeter Family Study of Childhood Health
definition: A prospective family study of 1,017 families (both parents and their children) from a postcode-defined area of central Exeter, United Kingdom, with anthropometry and fasting biochemistry at 28 weeks of gestation, cord blood at delivery and child follow-up to age 2 years, set up to test the fetal insulin hypothesis and identify genetic variants influencing birthweight and early postnatal growth.

label: Global Lipids Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of genome-wide association studies of blood lipid levels that meta-analyses summary statistics from primary studies of several genetic ancestry groups (about 1.65 million individuals from 201 studies in its 2021 round) to find loci for LDL and HDL cholesterol, triglycerides and total cholesterol.

label: Molecular Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of incident colorectal cancer cases and healthy controls recruited in northern Israel from 1998 to 2017, used to study genetic and environmental risk factors for colorectal cancer and the tumour immune microenvironment.

label: Nurses' Health Study II
definition: A prospective cohort of 116,429 female registered nurses aged 25–42 recruited in 1989 from 14 states of the United States, a younger population than the original Nurses' Health Study, followed by biennial mailed questionnaires and biospecimen collection to study risk factors for major chronic diseases in women.

label: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism cohort
definition: A sample of healthy controls of European American and African American ancestry recruited at the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism, National Institutes of Health, USA, who did not meet criteria for alcohol dependence or other major psychiatric disorders on the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV and gave blood samples used for genome-wide DNA methylation analysis and genotyping on Illumina OmniExpress arrays.

label: Southern Community Cohort Study
definition: A prospective cohort of about 85,000 English-speaking adults aged 40–79, predominantly Black and low-income, enrolled in 2002–2009 in 12 states of the southeastern United States, designed to study racial disparities in cancer and other chronic disease outcomes.

label: Taiwan Precision Medicine Initiative
definition: A hospital-based cohort of more than 565,000 participants recruited by Academia Sinica with 16 major medical centres across Taiwan, genotyped on arrays optimised for Han Chinese ancestry and linked to retrospective and prospective electronic medical records, for genome-wide, phenome-wide and polygenic risk studies of common disease and pharmacogenetic response.

label: Baependi Heart Study
definition: A longitudinal family-based cohort of highly admixed residents of Baependi, a small rural town in Minas Gerais, Brazil, recruited from 2005 through probands and their relatives and followed up in 2010 and 2016 to study genetic and environmental influences on cardiovascular risk factors, sleep, circadian rhythms and mental health.

label: Born in Guangzhou Cohort Study
definition: A prospective birth cohort of pregnant women living in Guangzhou, China, recruited in early pregnancy at Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center from 2012, with biological samples from mothers, fathers and infants and planned follow-up of the children to age 18 years, to study social, biological and environmental influences on pregnancy and child health and development.

label: Genetics, Osteoarthritis and Progression Study
definition: A cohort of about 190 white Dutch sibling pairs aged 40–70 with symptomatic osteoarthritis at multiple joint sites, recruited from rheumatology, orthopaedic and general practice clinics around Leiden, the Netherlands, by Leiden University Medical Center to identify determinants of osteoarthritis susceptibility and progression.

label: Physicians' Health Study
definition: A cohort of US male physicians enrolled in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, PHS I (begun in 1982 with 22,071 physicians aged 40–84) and PHS II, testing low-dose aspirin, beta-carotene and vitamins for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer, and followed thereafter as a prospective cohort.

label: Trinity Student Study
definition: A cohort of about 2,000 healthy, unrelated young adults of Irish ancestry aged 18–28, recruited at Trinity College Dublin, Ireland, in 2003–2004, with plasma and serum samples and genotypes used to study genetic influences on circulating metabolites.

label: Yale-Penn study
definition: A sample of more than 11,000 African American and European American participants recruited through treatment centres and advertisements at sites including Yale University, the University of Pennsylvania, McLean Hospital and the Medical University of South Carolina for genetic studies of cocaine, opioid and alcohol dependence, genotyped in three waves (Yale-Penn 1–3).

label: Cardiovascular Disease Association Study
definition: A population-based cohort of about 28,000 men and women aged 40 and over living in rural areas of South Korea, recruited in 2004–2011 as part of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study, with follow-up surveys in some counties, to study cardiovascular and other chronic diseases and their genetic and environmental risk factors.

label: China Health and Nutrition Survey
definition: A household-based cohort of individuals, households and communities in provinces across China, surveyed repeatedly since 1989 with all household members studied and in-depth community data collected, to understand how social and economic change in China affects nutrition and health outcomes.

label: 300-Obese
definition: A cohort of about 300 overweight or obese adults (BMI of 27 kg/m2 or more) aged 54–81 of Western European ancestry, enrolled at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, within the Human Functional Genomics Project to discover pathways, including inflammation and immune responses, that contribute to cardiovascular disease in overweight and obese people.

label: Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease Study
definition: A phase 3 clinical prevention trial that screened cognitively unimpaired adults aged 65–85 with amyloid PET at 67 sites in Australia, Canada, Japan and the USA from 2014 to 2017 and tested, in those with elevated brain amyloid, whether the anti-amyloid antibody solanezumab slows cognitive decline in preclinical Alzheimer's disease.

label: Child and Adolescent Twin Study in Sweden
definition: An ongoing longitudinal study of all twins born in Sweden since July 1992, whose parents are interviewed about the children's somatic and mental health and social environment at age 9 or 12, with follow-up questionnaires at ages 15 and 18 and clinical assessments at 15 of screen-positive twin pairs and controls, to study the aetiology of childhood mental health problems and their role in later adjustment.

label: CLUE II
definition: A community-based prospective cohort of 32,894 mostly White adults in Washington County, Maryland, USA, who gave blood samples, blood pressure readings and brief medical histories during a 1989 campaign against cancer and heart disease run from the Johns Hopkins George W. Comstock Center, followed through cancer-registry linkage to study risk factors for cancer and heart disease.

label: Genetic Regulation of Arterial Pressure in Humans in the Community Study
definition: A family cohort of about 2,000 white European adults from 520 nuclear families (both parents aged 40–60 and two adult offspring), identified through general practices in Leicestershire, UK, and recruited in 2002–2005 to study the genetic regulation of blood pressure and related cardiovascular traits.

label: Monongahela-Youghiogheny Healthy Aging Team
definition: A population-based cohort of 1982 adults aged 65 and over from southwestern Pennsylvania, USA, recruited by age-stratified random sampling from electoral rolls and followed with longitudinal cognitive assessments to study cognitive decline and dementia.

label: Utah residents (CEPH) with Northern and Western European ancestry
definition: A collection of DNA samples and lymphoblastoid cell lines from Utah residents with ancestry from northern and western Europe, originally collected by the Centre d'Etude du Polymorphisme Humain (CEPH), that forms one of the four founding population samples of the International HapMap Project and is used as a reference for human genetic variation.

label: Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria
definition: A collection of DNA samples and lymphoblastoid cell lines from Yoruba people in Ibadan, Nigeria, including parent–child trios, that forms one of the four founding population samples of the International HapMap Project and is used as a reference for human genetic variation.

label: Copenhagen Prospective Study on Asthma in Childhood
definition: A single-centre Danish prospective clinical birth cohort (COPSAC2000) of 411 children born in 1998–2001 to mothers with asthma, enrolled at 1 month of age and followed closely at the COPSAC clinical research unit in Copenhagen through childhood and to age 18 to study genetic, environmental and lifestyle risk factors for asthma, atopic dermatitis, allergy and other chronic inflammatory disorders.

label: DemGene network
definition: A Norwegian multi-centre network of clinical sites that pools Alzheimer's disease dementia and mild cognitive impairment cases from memory-clinic and other studies (among them NorCog, DemVest, the AHUS study, HUNT dementia studies, TrønderBrain and DDI), examined with standardized cognitive, functional and behavioural measures and followed for progression, together with cognitively normal and population controls, for genetic studies of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.

label: Diabetes Genetics Replication and Meta-analysis Consortium
definition: A consortium of genome-wide association studies of type 2 diabetes in people of European descent, whose successive case-control meta-analyses (DIAGRAMv2, DIAGRAMv3 and later) were used to discover and fine-map type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci.

label: Determining the Influence of Susceptibility COnveying Variants Related to one-Year mortality after BMT
definition: A study population of patients with acute myeloid leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndrome or acute lymphoblastic leukaemia who received an unrelated-donor blood or marrow transplant in 2000–2011, and their HLA-matched unrelated donors, contributed by 151 US transplant centres to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research, assembled in two cohorts to find non-HLA genetic variants associated with one-year survival after transplant.

label: European Alzheimer's Disease Initiative
definition: A French consortium whose genome-wide association dataset of 2,032 Alzheimer's disease cases and 5,328 controls from France was assembled to identify late-onset Alzheimer's disease risk loci, and which later formed one of the four founding datasets of the International Genomics of Alzheimer's Project.

label: EPICURE Consortium
definition: A European consortium of clinical and laboratory epilepsy research groups, funded in 2007–2011 by the EU Sixth Framework Programme as the EPICURE project and coordinated by the Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta in Italy, whose collections of people with genetic generalized epilepsy (such as the EPICURE-SP1 cohort) contributed cases to genome-wide association studies of epilepsy.

label: GenEpA Consortium
definition: A collection of people with epilepsy and controls recruited and phenotyped with GlaxoSmithKline funding by the GenEpA Consortium in Finland, Norway, Switzerland and Austria, whose national sample sets were genotyped and contributed to genome-wide association studies of the common epilepsies.

label: Genetic and Environmental Risk in Alzheimer's Disease Consortium
definition: A consortium led from Cardiff University that brought together Alzheimer's disease cases and screened elderly controls recruited by institutions in the United Kingdom, Germany and the United States, with population controls from existing British and German cohorts, into a genome-wide association dataset of Alzheimer's disease; one of the four datasets meta-analysed by the International Genomics of Alzheimer's Project.

label: Genes for Good
definition: A University of Michigan study that engages the public through a Facebook application for health-history and daily-tracking surveys and mails saliva kits for genotyping to participants who complete enough surveys, having engaged more than 80,000 people from all 50 US states by 2019 for genetic research on health and behaviour.

label: Imperial-Liverpool-Melbourne Collaboration
definition: A collection of people with epilepsy of European (British) ancestry, assembled by the Imperial-Liverpool-Melbourne Collaboration and genotyped genome-wide, that contributed cases to the ILAE Consortium on Complex Epilepsies meta-analyses of genome-wide association studies of the common epilepsies.

label: San Antonio Family Study
definition: A family-based study of Mexican Americans in San Antonio, Texas, United States, made up of the San Antonio Family Heart Study (extended families of randomly selected low-income Mexican American probands) and the San Antonio Family Diabetes/Gallbladder Study (extended families of probands with type 2 diabetes from the San Antonio Heart Study), both begun in 1991 and followed with repeated examinations, to study the genetics of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and related traits.

label: Swedish Adoption/Twin Study of Aging
definition: A longitudinal study of same-sex twin pairs born in Sweden and drawn from the Swedish Twin Registry, including pairs separated before age 11 and reared apart, with questionnaires and in-person testing from 1984 to 2014, to understand the factors that contribute to healthy ageing and longevity.

label: Stroke Genetics Network
definition: A network, funded by the US National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, that brought together ischaemic stroke case collections from genetic research centres in the United States, Europe and Australia, with stroke subtypes harmonised by the web-based Causative Classification of Stroke system, for genome-wide association studies of ischaemic stroke and its subtypes.

label: SubPopulations and InteRmediate Outcome Measures in COPD Study
definition: A multicentre observational cohort of current and former smokers aged 40–80 with or without airflow obstruction, and never-smoking controls, recruited at clinical sites across the United States with baseline and annual follow-up visits, to find subgroups of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and biomarkers usable as intermediate outcomes in therapeutic trials.

label: Veterans Health Service Medical Center cohort
definition: A hospital-based cohort of older adults, many with various diseases, at the Veterans Health Service Medical Center in Seoul, South Korea, with samples held by the Veterans Medical Research Institute Biobank and genotyped on the Korea Biobank Array for genome-wide association studies of body composition and cardiometabolic traits.

label: Cervical Artery Dissection and Ischemic Stroke Patients
definition: A multinational European network of patients with cervical artery dissection, with ischaemic stroke patients of other causes and healthy controls, recruited with standardised clinical, laboratory, imaging, treatment and outcome data to identify genetic variants and environmental factors associated with cervical artery dissection.

label: Genetics of Glucose regulation in Gestation and Growth
definition: A prospective prebirth cohort of about 1,000 pregnant women aged 18 or over recruited in the first trimester at the pregnancy blood-sampling clinic in Sherbrooke, Canada, between 2010 and 2013, and their children, followed to study the biological, environmental and genetic determinants of glucose regulation in pregnancy and its effects on fetal development and offspring health.

label: Manchester Asthma and Allergy Study
definition: A population-based birth cohort of children recruited in utero through the antenatal clinics of Wythenshawe and Stepping Hill Hospitals in South Manchester and Cheshire, England, with parents screened for atopy, and followed prospectively through childhood to study the genetic and environmental determinants of asthma and allergic disease.

label: Population Assessment for Tomorrow's Health Study
definition: A research registry of community volunteers aged 18 to 65 living in the Greater Hamilton area, with or without addiction problems, run by the Peter Boris Centre for Addictions Research at St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton, whose participants completed questionnaires, simple physical measurements and an in-person assessment and gave saliva for DNA genotyping through 23andMe, to build a cohort for research on the causes, consequences and treatment of addiction.

label: Peking University-University of Michigan Study of Atherosclerosis
definition: A prospective community-based cohort of 9,540 Han Chinese adults aged 40 and over enrolled in December 2011–April 2012 in the Gucheng and Pingguoyuan communities of Shijingshan district, Beijing, China, by Peking University with the University of Michigan, to study atherosclerosis, blood pressure and other cardiovascular traits.

label: Singapore Chinese Health Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of 63,257 Chinese adults aged 45–74 years from the Hokkien and Cantonese dialect groups living in Singapore, recruited from April 1993 to December 1998 and followed with repeated interviews, to study diet, lifestyle, genetic factors and chronic disease and ageing.

label: Sister Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 50,884 women aged 35–74 living in the United States and Puerto Rico who had never had breast cancer but had a sister diagnosed with it, enrolled from 2003 by the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences with biological and environmental samples to study environmental and genetic risk factors for breast cancer and other health outcomes in women.

label: UroLife study
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of more than 1,100 patients newly diagnosed with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, recruited in 2014–2021 from 22 hospitals in the Netherlands and followed with questionnaires, diaries, blood and tumour samples and cancer registry data to study how lifestyle habits relate to prognosis and health-related quality of life.

label: Chinese Antipsychotics Pharmacogenomics Consortium
definition: A six-week multicentre randomised open-label pharmacogenetic trial cohort of about 3,000 Han Chinese inpatients with schizophrenia in an acute phase, recruited through the Chinese Antipsychotics Pharmacogenomics Consortium of five research centres and their affiliated psychiatric hospitals in China, established in 2010, and randomly assigned to one of six antipsychotic treatments, to identify predictors of antipsychotic efficacy and adverse reactions.

label: CROATIA-Split Study
definition: A population-based cohort of about 1,000 adults from the mainland city of Split, the second-largest city in Croatia, recruited within the 10,001 Dalmatians biobank project as an urban counterpart to the isolated island cohorts of Vis and Korčula, for studies of the genetic, environmental and social determinants of health and disease.

label: Epidemiological study on the Genetics and Environment of Asthma
definition: A French case-control and family-based cohort of asthma cases recruited in chest clinics in Grenoble, Lyon, Marseille, Montpellier and Paris, their first-degree relatives and population-based controls, enrolled in 1991–1995 and followed up in 2003–2007 and later, to study the genetic and environmental causes of asthma, bronchial hyperresponsiveness and atopy.

label: Epidemiologische Studie zu Chancen der Verhütung, Früherkennung und optimierten Therapie chronischer Erkrankungen in der älteren Bevölkerung
definition: A population-based cohort of 9,940 adults aged 50–75 recruited by their general practitioners during routine health check-ups in Saarland, Germany, between 2000 and 2002 and followed every two to three years, run by the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg to study the prevention, early detection and treatment of chronic diseases in older people.

label: Gothenburg H70 Birth Cohort Studies and Clinical AD Sweden
definition: A collection of Alzheimer's disease cases and dementia-free controls from Sweden that combines cases diagnosed in memory clinics in different parts of Sweden or identified in two population-based studies in Gothenburg, the Prospective Population Study of Women and the Gothenburg Birth Cohort Studies (H70, H85 and 95+), with controls from those Gothenburg population studies, genotyped for genome-wide association studies of Alzheimer's disease and its biomarkers.

label: Northern California Breast Cancer Family Registry
definition: The Northern California site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry, which from 1995 enrolled about 4000 women with incident breast cancer, ascertained through the Greater Bay Area Cancer Registry in the San Francisco Bay Area with oversampling of cases with indicators of increased genetic susceptibility, together with their family members and random-digit-dialled population controls, to study the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer.

label: Breast Cancer Family Registry
definition: A breast cancer family registry established in 1995 with US National Cancer Institute support as a collaboration of six academic and research institutions in the USA, Canada and Australia, enrolling population-based families (through cancer registries) and clinic-based families with common questionnaires, biospecimen protocols and pathology review, to support studies of the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer.

label: National Institute on Aging Late Onset Alzheimer's Disease Family Study
definition: A family study that recruited 992 multiplex late-onset Alzheimer's disease families, with at least two living affected members, together with unrelated neurologically evaluated controls, from throughout the United States, for genetic studies of late-onset Alzheimer's disease.

label: Northern Manhattan Study
definition: A community-based longitudinal cohort of 3,298 stroke-free, predominantly Hispanic, Black and White adults aged 40 or older living in northern Manhattan, New York City, recruited by random-digit dialling in 1993–2001 and followed for stroke, vascular risk factors, brain MRI markers and cognitive outcomes.

label: Pittsburgh Orofacial Cleft Study
definition: A multiethnic family-based collection of people with nonsyndromic orofacial clefts, their unaffected relatives and unaffected controls, recruited by the University of Pittsburgh through cleft centres in the United States and Puerto Rico and in Argentina, the Philippines, Colombia, Guatemala and Hungary to study the genetics of orofacial clefts and related dental traits.

label: Australian Genetics of Depression Study
definition: A cohort of 20,689 adults in Australia who had been diagnosed with depression, recruited through the Australian Department of Human Services and a media campaign, who completed online questionnaires on psychiatric history and antidepressant response and provided saliva DNA, to study genetic and environmental risk factors for depression and antidepressant response.

label: Accessible Resource for Integrated Epigenomic Studies
definition: A sub-study of the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children comprising 1,018 mother-offspring pairs with genome-wide DNA methylation profiled at birth, in childhood and in adolescence for the children and at two time points for the mothers, established as an openly accessible resource to study the determinants and consequences of epigenetic variation.

label: Bellygenes initiative
definition: An international collaborative initiative that pooled individual-level and aggregate genetic data on 12,852 people with irritable bowel syndrome and 139,981 controls from multiple studies for genome-wide association studies of irritable bowel syndrome.

label: CERA cohort
