definition: A cohort of people of European ancestry with and without age-related macular degeneration, recruited, imaged with optical coherence tomography and genotyped by the Centre for Eye Research Australia, used in genetic studies of age-related macular degeneration and reticular pseudodrusen.

label: Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research - National Marrow Donor Program Research Sample Repository
definition: A biorepository of blood samples from more than 60,000 allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant recipients and their related or unrelated donors or cord blood units, held by the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (a collaboration of the Medical College of Wisconsin and NMDP) and linked to validated clinical outcome data in the CIBMTR Research Database, for research on transplant outcomes.

label: Drug Interaction With Genes in Parkinson's Disease
definition: A French multicentre longitudinal cohort of patients with early Parkinson's disease (disease duration of two years or less at recruitment) recruited from clinics in France and followed annually with clinical assessments and genotyping, supported by Assistance Publique Hôpitaux de Paris and registered as NCT01564992.

label: Duke Genetics of Kidney Disease
definition: A research collection of patients with kidney disease, including children and young adults with nephrotic syndrome and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, referred from Duke University and collaborating centres to Duke University's genetics of kidney disease research program in Durham, North Carolina, for genetic studies.

label: European Genetic Database
definition: A multicentre prospective epidemiological study enrolling patients with age-related macular degeneration and healthy control individuals aged 55 years or over at the ophthalmology departments of University Hospital Cologne, Germany, and Radboud University Medical Center, Nijmegen, the Netherlands, used to study genetic and non-genetic risk factors for age-related macular degeneration.

label: Family Atherosclerosis Monitoring In earLY life Study
definition: A Canadian longitudinal birth cohort of about 850 families (mother, father, newborn and eldest sibling) recruited during pregnancy at three hospitals in Ontario between 2002 and 2009, followed to study prenatal, early-childhood and family determinants of adiposity, cardiovascular risk factors and atherosclerosis in children.

label: Finland-United States Investigation of NIDDM Genetics
definition: A Finnish–US study of type 2 diabetes genetics that ascertained Finnish families with type 2 diabetes in at least two siblings, with spouses and offspring examined by frequently sampled intravenous glucose tolerance tests, and later Finnish type 2 diabetes cases and normoglycaemic controls, to map susceptibility genes for type 2 diabetes and related quantitative traits.

label: Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory Study
definition: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of Ginkgo biloba for preventing incident dementia in 3069 adults aged 75 and over, 2587 cognitively normal and 482 with mild cognitive impairment, conducted from 2000 to 2008 at five academic centers in the United States.

label: Genito-Urinary BioBank
definition: A biobank set up in 2008 at Princess Margaret Hospital, Toronto, Canada, holding biospecimens, including blood for DNA extraction, from patients attending its Genito-Urinary Oncology clinics for the suspicion, diagnosis or treatment of prostate, kidney, bladder, testis or penile tumours, whose non-muscle invasive bladder cancer patients, in two batches (GUB-1 and GUB-2), were used in genetic studies of recurrence and progression.

label: Hisayama-FSR study
definition: A case-control study of ischaemic stroke in Japan combining 1,113 patients with ischaemic stroke recruited in 2004 from seven hospitals in Fukuoka Prefecture (the Fukuoka Stroke Registry) with 901 controls free of stroke and coronary heart disease drawn from the population-based Hisayama Study, used in genome-wide association studies of ischaemic stroke and its subtypes.

label: International Genomics of Alzheimer's Project
definition: An international collaboration that meta-analysed genome-wide association data on late-onset Alzheimer's disease from four consortia, the Alzheimer Disease Genetics Consortium, the Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology Consortium, the European Alzheimer's Disease Initiative and the Genetic and Environmental Risk in Alzheimer's Disease Consortium, first with 17,008 cases and 37,154 controls of European ancestry.

label: Mexican-American Coronary Artery Disease Study
definition: A family study of Mexican Americans in the Los Angeles area, United States, in which the families of probands with documented coronary artery disease were recruited to examine the genetic basis of coronary artery disease and insulin resistance.

label: Genetics UndeRlying DIAbetes in HispaNics
definition: A consortium of seven Mexican-American cohorts in the United States (the IRAS Family Study, BetaGene, MACAD, HTN-IR, NIDDM-Athero, IRAS and TRIPOD; 4,336 individuals in 1,346 pedigrees) formed to conduct genome-wide association studies of insulin sensitivity and insulin clearance measured by euglycemic clamp or frequently sampled intravenous glucose tolerance test.

label: METASTROKE collaboration
definition: A collaboration that meta-analyses genome-wide association datasets from ischaemic stroke case-control cohorts of European ancestry (initially 15 cohorts with 12,389 cases and 62,004 controls) to validate previously reported associations and identify new genetic associations with ischaemic stroke and its subtypes.

label: Monongahela Valley Independent Elders Survey
definition: A prospective cohort of 1681 adults aged 65 and over living in the Monongahela Valley, Pennsylvania, USA, recruited from voter registration lists in 1987–1989 and followed every other year for up to 12 years to study cognitive decline and dementia.

label: Prediction and Prevention of Preeclampsia and Intrauterine Growth Restriction Study
definition: A Finnish pregnancy cohort of 4,785 women recruited at their first ultrasound scan in ten hospital maternity clinics between 2005 and 2010, comprising a high-risk subsample with and without risk factors for preeclampsia and intrauterine growth restriction and a community-based subsample, followed with their children to study the prediction and prevention of pregnancy complications and prenatal influences on offspring development.

label: Risk Assessment of Cerebrovascular Events Study
definition: A case-control study of stroke recruiting over 5,000 imaging-confirmed stroke cases and 5,000 controls from seven centres in Pakistan, investigating genetic, biomarker and lifestyle determinants of stroke and its subtypes, and using controls from the Pakistan Risk of Myocardial Infarction Study for genetic analyses.

label: Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of 30,239 African American and European American adults aged 45 or older recruited from the 48 contiguous US states and the District of Columbia in 2003–2007, designed to measure stroke incidence and its risk factors and to explain geographic and racial differences in stroke.

label: Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial
definition: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial of selenium and vitamin E, alone and in combination, for the prevention of prostate cancer, which enrolled 35,533 men from the United States, Canada and Puerto Rico at more than 400 clinical sites.

label: Stroke in Young Fabry Patients
definition: A multicentre, multinational European prospective observational study of 5,023 patients aged 18–55 with acute stroke or transient ischaemic attack, enrolled at 47 centres in 15 European countries between 2007 and 2010, originally designed to investigate the relation between juvenile stroke and Fabry disease and also used to study stroke patterns in young adults.

label: SpiroMeta Consortium
definition: A consortium of cohort studies of European-ancestry individuals, initially 14 genome-wide association studies with over 20,000 participants and later expanded to about 79,000, established to meta-analyse genome-wide association studies of spirometric lung function.

label: Wisconsin Longitudinal Study
definition: A longitudinal study of men and women who graduated from Wisconsin high schools in 1957, most born in 1939, and one of their randomly selected siblings, followed for almost 60 years to link family background, adolescent characteristics, education, work and family life to later-life physical and mental health, cognition and mortality, with saliva samples for genetic studies.

label: Grady Trauma Project
definition: A study of low-income, predominantly African American adults recruited from the primary care and obstetrics-gynaecology clinics of Grady Memorial Hospital, an urban public hospital in Atlanta, United States, to investigate environmental and genetic risk factors for trauma-related disorders such as posttraumatic stress disorder and depression.

label: 10,001 Dalmatians
definition: A Croatian biobank project, based at the University of Split with UK Medical Research Council funding, that recruited adults from the isolated Dalmatian islands of Vis and Korčula and from the mainland city of Split into separate cohorts, to investigate genetic, environmental and social determinants of health and disease in Croatia.

label: Lothian Birth Cohort 1936
definition: A cohort of 1,091 people born in 1936 who took an intelligence test at age 11 in the Scottish Mental Survey of 1947, recruited in 2004–2007 at a mean age of 70, mostly living in Edinburgh and the Lothians, and retested about every 3 years with cognitive, biomedical, brain imaging and lifestyle assessments to study non-pathological cognitive ageing from childhood to older age.

label: Lothian Birth Cohort 1921
definition: A cohort of 550 people born in 1921 who took an intelligence test at age 11 in the Scottish Mental Survey of 1932, recruited in 1999–2001 at a mean age of 79, mostly living in Edinburgh and the Lothians, and followed up five times to age 92 to study non-pathological cognitive ageing from childhood to older age.

label: National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health
definition: A nationally representative cohort of people in the United States born between 1976 and 1982, enrolled as adolescents and followed in repeated waves into adulthood with self-report, parent-report, geocoded and genetic data to study how adolescent circumstances shape later health and wellbeing.

label: Basque Center on Cognition, Brain and Language cohort
definition: A cohort of Spanish schoolchildren recruited at schools in Andalucía, the Basque Country, Castilla-León, Murcia and the Canary Islands by the Basque Center on Cognition, Brain and Language, who gave saliva for DNA and were assessed with reading, phonological, attention and IQ tasks, and whose genome-wide genotypes are used to study the genetics of dyslexia, ADHD and reading- and language-related skills.

label: Botnia Study
definition: A family study of patients with type 2 diabetes, their first-degree relatives and spouses without a family history of diabetes in western Finland, examined with oral glucose tolerance tests and euglycaemic insulin clamps and followed prospectively to study the inheritance, metabolic features and prediction of type 2 diabetes.

label: Colorado Learning Disabilities Research Center cohort
definition: A family-based sample selected for dyslexia by the Colorado Learning Disabilities Research Center at the University of Colorado, United States, in which children and their families were assessed with reading, spelling, phonological and IQ tests and genotyped to study the genetics of reading disability.

label: DIAGEN Study
definition: A German study run from the Technical University of Dresden, with participants from Saxony, of people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes who had a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at baseline and again after about three years, which also contributed patients with type 2 diabetes and controls to consortium genetic studies of type 2 diabetes and glycaemic traits.

label: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate End-points
definition: A 3-year multinational observational cohort of about 2,180 patients with moderate to very severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and smoking and non-smoking controls, recruited at 46 centres in 12 countries in North America, Europe and New Zealand, to define COPD subtypes and find clinical, imaging, biomarker and genetic predictors of disease progression.

label: Early Language in Victoria Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 1910 infants recruited at 8 months of age in Melbourne, Australia, in 2003–2004 and followed through childhood with parent reports and language assessments to study language development and its early-life predictors.

label: German Infant Study on the Influence of Nutrition Intervention plus Air pollution and Genetics on Allergy Development
definition: A prospective population-based German birth cohort of 5,991 healthy term newborns recruited in obstetric hospitals in Munich and Wesel in 1995–1998, comprising a double-blind randomised trial of hydrolysed infant formula in children with a family history of allergy (the German Infant Nutritional Intervention study, GINI) and a non-interventional arm, about 55% of whom were followed for the first 10 years to study the natural course of atopic diseases and their determinants.

label: Gothenburg Osteoporosis and Obesity Determinants study
definition: A cohort of 1,068 young men aged 18–20, randomly identified in the greater Gothenburg area of Sweden from national population registers, initiated to determine environmental and genetic factors involved in the regulation of bone and fat mass, with a five-year follow-up examination.

label: Genetics of Overweight Young Adults
definition: A case-control sample of extremely overweight young Danish adults and equal numbers of randomly drawn population controls, selected from women of the Danish National Birth Cohort and men of a Danish draft-board examination cohort, for genome-wide association study of body mass index.

label: International Consortium for Blood Pressure Genome-Wide Association Studies
definition: A consortium of genome-wide association studies of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, whose 2011 multi-stage meta-analysis combined about 200,000 individuals of European descent to find blood pressure loci and relate them to hypertension and cardiovascular disease risk.

label: Iowa LI cohort
definition: A case-control sample of 219 children with language impairment and 209 sex- and age-matched, unrelated controls collected at the University of Iowa, United States, who completed a battery of language measures (including the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test and nonword repetition) used to define case status, and reading, spelling and IQ assessments, used in genetic association studies of language impairment and of reading- and language-related skills.

label: Korea-Registries to Overcome Dementia and Accelerate Dementia Research
definition: A hospital-based Korean dementia research programme made up of three prospective cohorts (the PREMIER consortium, the LLOD cohort and the Samsung Medical Center amyloid PET cohort) at 28 centres, which by December 2023 had recruited over 5,800 participants across the Alzheimer's clinical syndrome, subcortical vascular cognitive impairment and frontotemporal dementia spectra, with clinical, neuroimaging, biomarker and genomic data, to study disease progression and early diagnosis of dementia in the Korean population.

label: Mayo Genome Consortia
definition: A genotype-phenotype resource assembled at Mayo Clinic from participants of multiple Mayo Clinic research studies who gave general research consent to share their high-throughput genotyping data, linked to electronic medical record data for phenotype extraction, to enable cost-effective genome-wide association studies.

label: Impact of Migration and Ethnicity on Diabetes in Malmö
definition: A population-based cohort of people aged 30–75 years born in Iraq or Sweden and resident in Malmö, Sweden, randomly selected from the Malmö census register, to study the impact of migration and ethnicity on type 2 diabetes and related metabolic traits.

label: Material and Information Resources for Inflammatory and Digestive Diseases Biobank
definition: A biobank of patients with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis and non-IBD controls recruited with informed consent at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, United States, holding clinical phenotype, serological and genetic data and specimens for inflammatory bowel disease research.

label: Lung Cancer and Smoking Phenotypes in African American Cases and Controls
definition: A collection of African American lung cancer cases and controls drawn from eight US lung cancer studies, among them the Southern Community Cohort Study, the NCI-MD Lung Cancer Case-Control Study, the MD Anderson Lung Cancer Epidemiology Study and the Northern California Lung Cancer Study, genotyped for a genome-wide association study of lung cancer and smoking phenotypes in African Americans.

label: NIDDK IBD Genetics Consortium
definition: A cohort of patients with Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis or unclassified inflammatory bowel disease recruited since 2003 by the genetic research centres of the NIDDK IBD Genetics Consortium in the United States and Canada, with diagnoses confirmed by chart review, for IBD gene discovery.

label: Oregon Health and Science University study
definition: A case-control collection of autopsied Alzheimer disease cases and non-demented controls, drawn from longitudinal aging research cohorts at 10 NIA-funded Alzheimer's Disease Centers in the United States and assembled at Oregon Health & Science University for genome-wide association studies of Alzheimer disease and its neuropathology within the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium.

label: Phenomics and Genomics Sample
definition: A sample collected at the University of Munich, Germany, of about 3,000 healthy volunteers of German descent from the Munich area, assessed with structured psychiatric interviews covering themselves and their first-degree relatives, together with about 1,000 patients with schizophrenia and about 300 people with other diagnoses, including Alzheimer's disease patients from the psychiatric memory clinic, used as a case and control resource in genetic studies of psychiatric, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders.

label: Paediatric Asthma Gene Environment Study
definition: A study of children and adolescents aged 2–16 years with physician-diagnosed asthma recruited through 15 secondary-care asthma clinics across Scotland from 2008 to 2011, with questionnaire and DNA data to study genetic and environmental influences on asthma and its treatment response.

label: Risk Stratification and Identification of Immunogenetic and Microbial Markers of Rapid Disease Progression in Children with Crohn's Disease
definition: A prospective inception cohort of patients younger than 18 years with suspected inflammatory bowel disease, enrolled at diagnosis between 2008 and 2012 at 28 sites in the United States and Canada (mostly Crohn's disease, also ulcerative colitis, unclassified IBD and non-inflamed controls), to characterise the natural history of newly diagnosed paediatric Crohn's disease and predict its complications from clinical, serological, genomic and microbial markers at diagnosis.

label: Texas Harris Alzheimer's Research Study
definition: A longitudinal research cohort begun in June 2005 by the Texas Alzheimer's Research and Care Consortium, which has enrolled more than 3,600 older adults with Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment or normal cognition, with deliberate inclusion of Mexican Americans, at the consortium's Texas sites and followed annually with clinical, neuropsychological, genetic and blood biomarker assessments, to improve the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of Alzheimer's disease.

label: Wellcome Language and Reading Project
definition: A longitudinal cohort of children at family risk of dyslexia, children with preschool language difficulties and typically developing controls, recruited from about age 3½ in 2007–2009 from York and neighbouring regions of northern England by the University of York and followed to study the development of language, reading and dyslexia.

label: Sinai-Helmsley Alliance for Research Excellence
definition: A multicentre prospective observational cohort of patients with inflammatory bowel disease recruited at seven academic medical centres in the United States, collecting longitudinal clinical and phenotypic data and biosamples for clinical outcomes and translational research.

label: Shanghai Changfeng Study
definition: A community-based prospective cohort of middle-aged and elderly adults aged 40 and over in Shanghai, China, recruited from February 2009 to study multiple chronic diseases including obesity and metabolic syndrome, diabetes, osteoporosis, liver, cardiovascular and neurological diseases.

label: Collaborative Genetic Study of Nicotine Dependence
definition: A study begun in 2001 as a National Cancer Institute programme project in which nicotine-dependent smokers and non-dependent smoking controls were recruited from communities in Detroit and St. Louis, United States, to identify genetic factors in nicotine dependence.

label: EPIDG cohort
definition: A prospective cohort of Mediterranean (southern European) pregnant women attending the Diabetes and Pregnancy Unit of Hospital Universitario Virgen de la Victoria in Málaga, Spain, after a positive glucose screening test, recruited from 2019 with and without gestational diabetes and followed with their offspring to one year after birth, to study the effect of gestational diabetes on the epigenome of mother and child during the first 1000 days.

label: Family Investigation of Nephropathy and Diabetes
definition: A multicentre family-based and case-control study of European American, African American, Mexican American and American Indian people with diabetes, with and without diabetic nephropathy, and their relatives, recruited at eight US clinical centres to identify genetic determinants of diabetic nephropathy.

label: Genetics Of Mortality In Critical Care
definition: An international study, recruiting since 2015, of critically ill patients in intensive care units in the United Kingdom and other countries, with conditions such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome and influenza and, from 2020, critical COVID-19, whose genomes are compared with those of population controls to find host genetic factors and disease mechanisms underlying critical illness.

label: Collaborative Oncological Gene-environment Study
definition: A collaborative genotyping experiment of four cancer genetics consortia, studying breast cancer (the Breast Cancer Association Consortium), ovarian cancer, prostate cancer, and breast and ovarian cancer in BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers, funded by the EU Seventh Framework Programme, which genotyped samples from their member studies on a custom Illumina iSelect array (iCOGS) of more than 200,000 SNPs to identify cancer susceptibility loci.

label: Kentucky Case-Control Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of colon cancer in Kentucky, United States, that recruited incident cases through the Kentucky Cancer Registry and population controls by random-digit dialling from 2003 to 2010, to study genetic and environmental risk factors for colon cancer.

label: Los Angeles Latino Eye Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 6,357 Latinos aged 40 years and older, mostly of Mexican origin, from six census tracts in Los Angeles, California, United States, examined from 2000 to assess the prevalence and risk factors of visual impairment and eye diseases such as cataract, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration.

label: Mexican Hypertriglyceride Study
definition: A case-control collection of Mexican adults with hypertriglyceridaemia and normotriglyceridaemic controls recruited at the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición Salvador Zubirán in Mexico City, Mexico, for the first genome-wide association study of lipids in Mexicans.

label: San Francisco Bay Area Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based multiethnic case-control study of breast cancer in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, in which women aged 35–79 diagnosed with invasive breast cancer in 1995–2002 were identified through the Greater Bay Area Cancer Registry and controls were identified by random-digit dialing and matched on 5-year age group.

label: SIGMA Type 2 Diabetes Consortium
definition: A consortium formed under the Slim Initiative in Genomic Medicine for the Americas that pooled type 2 diabetes case-control samples of Mexicans and other Latin Americans from the Diabetes in Mexico Study, the Mexico City Diabetes Study, the Multiethnic Cohort Study and the UNAM/INCMNSZ Diabetes Study to characterise the genetic basis of type 2 diabetes in Mexican and Latin American populations.

label: Mexico City sample 2
definition: A case-control sample of 898 Mexican adults with type 2 diabetes and 889 controls, covered by the Mexican Social Security Institute and studied through the Medical Center Siglo XXI in Mexico City, Mexico, used in genome-wide association studies of lipid traits and type 2 diabetes.

label: Mexico City sample 1
definition: A case-control sample of 967 Mexican adults with type 2 diabetes, preferentially diagnosed before age 55, and 343 normoglycaemic controls from Mexico City, Mexico, who are covered by the Mexican Social Security Institute and were recruited at the Medical Center Siglo XXI, used in genome-wide association studies of type 2 diabetes and lipid traits.

label: 1982 Pelotas (Brazil) Birth Cohort Study
definition: A population-based birth cohort of the 5,914 live births in 1982 to families living in the urban area of Pelotas, a city in southern Brazil, followed through repeated interviews and a clinic visit at about age 30 covering mental health, body composition, precursors of chronic disease and human capital.

label: Agricultural Health Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 57,310 licensed pesticide applicators enrolled in Iowa and North Carolina, United States, in 1993–1997, together with their spouses, who reported detailed pesticide use and agricultural practices and are followed through follow-up questionnaires and cancer registry linkages to study the health effects of agricultural exposures, including cancer.

label: Agricultural Lung Health Study
definition: A case-control study of current adult asthma nested within the Agricultural Health Study, which enrolled 3,301 farmers and their spouses from Iowa and North Carolina, United States, in 2009–2013, collecting pulmonary function, atopy and blood or saliva samples during home visits, to study farm exposures, asthma and lung function.

label: AncestryDNA Human Diversity Project
definition: A research cohort of customers of the AncestryDNA consumer genetic testing service who consented to AncestryDNA's Human Diversity Project and contribute genotype data and survey responses to genetic studies, including a COVID-19 survey of US-based adult customers used in genome-wide association studies of COVID-19 and influenza outcomes.

label: All New Diabetics In Scania
definition: An ongoing study that aims to include all individuals with newly diagnosed diabetes in the Scania region of southern Sweden, used to classify diabetes into subgroups and to study their genetics and complications.

label: Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study
definition: A longitudinal study of twins and their non-twin siblings from Queensland, Australia, begun in 1992 with twins recruited through primary and secondary schools in the greater Brisbane area and assessed repeatedly in adolescence and young adulthood (including the 19Up study), with genotyping, brain imaging and psychological assessments, to study genetic and environmental pathways to traits such as mental health and substance use.

label: Coronary ARtery DIsease Genome wide Replication and Meta-analysis
definition: A transatlantic consortium that meta-analysed 14 genome-wide association studies of coronary artery disease in individuals of European descent (22,233 cases and 64,762 controls), with replication genotyping in further samples, to identify susceptibility loci for coronary artery disease.

label: Centers for AIDS Research Network of Integrated Clinical Systems
definition: A longitudinal observational cohort of people with HIV who entered care from 1995 onwards at the HIV clinics of US Centers for AIDS Research (ten sites since 2021), whose data repository integrates clinical, laboratory and patient-reported outcome data from electronic health records for research on HIV care and outcomes.

label: Diabetes Control and Complications Trial/Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications Study
definition: A cohort of 1,441 people aged 13–39 years with type 1 diabetes from 29 centres in the United States and Canada, enrolled in the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (1983–1993), a randomised trial comparing intensive with conventional therapy to test whether glycaemic control prevents or delays the complications of type 1 diabetes, and followed since 1994 in the observational Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (EDIC) study of the durability of the treatment effects on advanced microvascular complications and cardiovascular disease.

label: Danish National Birth Cohort
definition: A nationwide Danish cohort of about 100,000 pregnant women recruited early in pregnancy between 1996 and 2002, run by Statens Serum Institut, with telephone interviews during pregnancy and after birth, biological samples from mother and umbilical cord, and long-term follow-up of the children through questionnaires and national registry linkage, established to study the causal links between early-life exposures and later disease.

label: Environment And Genetics in Lung cancer Etiology study
definition: A population-based case-control study of lung cancer in the Lombardy region of Italy, which enrolled 2,101 incident primary lung cancer cases from 13 hospitals and 2,120 matched population controls in 2002–2005, collecting epidemiological, clinical and molecular data and biospecimens to study lung cancer aetiology from smoking addiction to outcome.

label: EArly Genetics and Lifecourse Epidemiology consortium
definition: A consortium of population-based pregnancy and birth cohort studies, set up alongside the Early Growth Genetics consortium, that pools genome-wide data to study the genetic basis of phenotypes from fetal life into adolescence such as asthma, eczema, childhood psychopathology, cognition and neurodevelopment.

label: EAGLE BioVU
definition: The participants of BioVU, the Vanderbilt University Medical Center biorepository, studied by the Epidemiologic Architecture for Genes Linked to Environment (EAGLE) site of the NHGRI Population Architecture using Genomics and Epidemiology (PAGE) program in trans-ethnic genetic studies of complex traits.

label: Elucidating Loci Involved in Prostate Cancer Susceptibility
definition: An international prostate cancer genetics consortium, linked to the PRACTICAL consortium, that meta-analyses existing genome-wide association data and generates new GWAS, exome-array, iCOGS and OncoArray genotype data from prostate cancer case-control studies to discover prostate cancer risk loci.

label: Helsinki 2000 Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of ischaemic stroke in Finland, in which patients with neuroimaging-confirmed new-onset brain infarction were recruited at Helsinki University Central Hospital, with TOAST subtyping, detailed phenotype data and blood samples, and controls were FINRISK 1992, 1997 and 2002 participants from the Greater Helsinki region frequency-matched by age and sex, to investigate genetic factors underlying ischaemic stroke.

label: GEN-COVID Multicenter Study
definition: A multicentre study coordinated by the University of Siena of SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals in Italy, hospitalised and non-hospitalised, whose biospecimens, detailed clinical data and exome and genotype data are collected in the GEN-COVID Biobank, Patient Registry and Genetic Data Repository to find genetic factors for COVID-19 susceptibility and severity.

label: Hawaii Colorectal Cancer Studies 2 and 3
definition: A population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in Hawaii, United States, in which Japanese, Caucasian and Native Hawaiian residents of Oahu newly diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma between January 1994 and August 1998 were identified through the Hawaii SEER registry and matched by sex, ethnicity and age to controls from a population-based health survey of the Hawaii State Department of Health and from Health Care Financing Administration participants, with in-person interviews and blood samples; its genotyped participants take part in consortium studies of genetic and lifestyle risk factors for colorectal cancer.

label: Heinz Nixdorf Recall Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 4,814 adults aged 45–75 randomly selected from the resident registries of Bochum, Essen and Mülheim an der Ruhr in the Ruhr area of Germany, examined in 2000–2003 and followed up repeatedly, set up to evaluate coronary artery calcification measured by electron-beam CT for predicting myocardial infarction and cardiac death beyond traditional risk factors.

label: INflammation, Health, Ancestry and Lung Epidemiology study
definition: A case-control study of lung cancer in African American and non-Hispanic White adults from the Detroit metropolitan area, in which patients were enrolled within 12 months of diagnosis at the Karmanos Cancer Institute or Henry Ford Health System between 2012 and 2018, together with controls without lung cancer, to study inflammation, ancestry and other risk factors for lung cancer and racial disparities in the disease.

label: Malmö Diet and Cancer Study–Cardiovascular Cohort
definition: A randomly selected subgroup of about 6,100 participants of the Malmö Diet and Cancer Study in Malmö, Sweden, enrolled between 1991 and 1994 into a sub-study of carotid artery disease and cardiovascular risk, with fasting blood samples used in studies of cardiovascular and metabolic disease.

label: MiaLAtinX Consortium
definition: A cohort of self-identified Hispanic people with Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis or unclassified inflammatory bowel disease and non-IBD controls, recruited through the MiaLAtinX Consortium at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, the University of Puerto Rico, the University of Miami and Mount Sinai Health System in New York and whole-genome sequenced at the Broad Institute, to study the ancestral origins of IBD risk in Hispanic populations.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1986
definition: A general-population birth cohort of 9,432 live-born children with expected dates of birth between July 1985 and June 1986 in the provinces of Oulu and Lapland in northern Finland, followed from pregnancy through childhood, adolescence and adulthood with questionnaires, clinical examinations and national register linkage.

label: Ragama Health Study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of adults aged 35–64 years recruited in 2007 by age-stratified random sampling in the semi-urban Ragama Medical Officer of Health area of Gampaha district, Sri Lanka, with baseline socio-demographic, lifestyle, anthropometric, biochemical and clinical data and follow-up of mortality and its predictors.

label: Singapore Chinese Eye Study
definition: A population-based cohort of Chinese adults in Singapore examined at baseline in 2009–2011 (SCES-1) and invited for a 6-year follow-up in 2015–2017 (SCES-2) with standardised ocular and systemic examinations and questionnaires, to study the prevalence, incidence, progression and risk factors of age-related eye diseases.

label: Singapore Epidemiology of Eye Diseases Study
definition: A multiethnic population-based cohort of Malay, Indian and Chinese adults in Singapore, recruited at baseline through the Singapore Malay Eye Study (2004–2006), the Singapore Indian Eye Study (2007–2009) and the Singapore Chinese Eye Study (2009–2011) and re-examined about six years later (SEED-2), to study the incidence and risk factors of eye diseases and visual impairment.

label: Singapore Indian Eye Study
definition: A population-based cohort of adults of Indian ethnicity in Singapore, examined at baseline in 2007–2009 and again in 2013–2015 (SINDI-2), to study diabetic retinopathy and other major age-related eye diseases and the impact of migration, comparing first-generation immigrants with Singapore-born second-generation participants.

label: TAICHI Consortium
definition: A collaborative consortium in Taiwan, with Taichung Veterans General Hospital, Tri-Service General Hospital, National Taiwan University Hospital and the National Health Research Institutes ascertaining subjects, that genotyped Taiwanese Chinese participants of several studies with the Illumina CardioMetaboChip to identify genetic determinants of atherosclerosis- and metabolic-related traits.

label: University of Southern California Hormone Replacement Therapy Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of colon cancer in women in Los Angeles County, United States, comprising 831 English-speaking women aged 55–74 years diagnosed with primary colon cancer from 1998 to 2002, identified through the Los Angeles County Cancer Surveillance Program (a SEER registry), and 755 race/ethnicity- and age-matched neighbourhood control women, with in-person interviews on hormone use, reproductive history and lifestyle and blood samples, set up to study menopausal hormone therapy and colon cancer risk.

label: UK Dyslexia Cohort
definition: A clinical cohort of children and adolescents aged 7–18 with reading difficulties, comprising siblings from nuclear families recruited by research clinics in Oxford and Reading and singletons recruited in Oxford, Reading and Aston, United Kingdom, to study the genetics of dyslexia.

label: African Ancestry Prostate Cancer Consortium
definition: A consortium of epidemiological studies of prostate cancer in men of African ancestry, mainly African American men, assembled to conduct genome-wide association studies of prostate cancer susceptibility in men of African descent.

label: Prevalence, Prediction and Prevention of Diabetes-Botnia Study
definition: A population-based study of a random sample of about 5,200 people aged 18–75 years from the Botnia region of western Finland, identified through the national population registry, to study the prevalence, prediction and prevention of type 2 diabetes and related metabolic traits.

label: The Cleft Collective
definition: A national longitudinal prospective cohort of children born with cleft lip and/or palate and their families, recruited across the UK from November 2013 through NHS cleft centres, with biological samples, questionnaires, surgical data and record linkage to study the causes, treatments and long-term outcomes of orofacial clefts.

label: Children's Oncology Group
definition: A clinical trials network of more than 220 hospitals and more than 13,500 researchers, clinicians and specialists that designs and runs clinical trials and research studies to cure and prevent childhood and adolescent cancer; genetic studies use participants of its trials.

label: Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism
definition: A multi-site, multi-generational family study in which probands recruited through alcohol treatment centres and their relatives, together with community comparison families, have been assessed over more than 30 years (nearly 18,000 individuals from over 2200 families) with psychiatric interviews, questionnaires, electrophysiology and DNA to identify genetic factors in alcohol use disorder and related outcomes.

label: Colorectal Transdisciplinary Study
definition: A colorectal cancer genetic epidemiology consortium, approved at the University of Southern California and funded within the NCI GAME-ON post-GWAS initiative, that pools genome-wide genotype data from colorectal cancer case-control studies such as the Molecular Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Study, the Colon Cancer Family Registry and the Kentucky and Newfoundland case-control studies to find and characterise colorectal cancer susceptibility variants.

label: Genetic Associations and Mechanisms in Oncology
definition: A network of cancer genetic epidemiology consortia, the NIH-funded post-cancer-GWAS initiative, that brings together genome-wide association data from colorectal (CORECT), breast (DRIVE), prostate (ELLIPSE), ovarian (FOCI) and lung (TRICL) cancer consortia, mainly of people of European descent.

label: DAHANCA cohort
definition: A cohort of patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma treated with radiotherapy within the protocols of the Danish Head and Neck Cancer Group (DAHANCA) in Denmark in 2000–2011, pooled from the DAHANCA 10 and DAHANCA 19 trials and the DAHANCA prospective biobank protocol, with standardised scoring of acute and late radiotherapy toxicity, used in radiogenomic studies.

label: DiscovEHR study
definition: A collaboration between the Regeneron Genetics Center and Geisinger Health System in which adult participants of Geisinger's MyCode Community Health Initiative are exome-sequenced and genotyped and linked to longitudinal electronic health records, for genomics-guided precision medicine and therapeutic discovery.

label: Epidemiological Investigation of Multiple Sclerosis
definition: A Swedish population-based case-control study of multiple sclerosis in which incident cases were recruited from hospital-based and privately run neurology units and matched controls were randomly selected from the national population register, with questionnaires on environmental and lifestyle exposures and blood samples for genetic analyses.

label: Swedish MS registry
definition: A government-funded national quality registry of patients with multiple sclerosis, used in all Swedish neurology departments, that supports clinical decisions and serves as a research resource, hosting nested projects including an incidence cohort, a prevalence cohort and post-marketing cohorts of patients on novel disease-modifying drugs.

label: EUGENE2 study
definition: A multicentre sample of healthy non-diabetic offspring of patients with type 2 diabetes, recruited in Denmark, Finland, Germany, Italy and Sweden by the European Network on Functional Genomics of Type 2 Diabetes and examined with glucose tolerance tests and hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic clamps to study the genetics of insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity.

label: Multi-Site Collaborative Study for Genotype-Phenotype Associations in Alzheimer's Disease
definition: A multi-site case-control study run with GlaxoSmithKline that recruited people with Alzheimer's disease from memory referral clinics in Canada, with cognitively unimpaired controls from their non-biological relatives, friends or spouses, to find genetic variants associated with Alzheimer's disease risk and age at onset.

label: Hospital-based Epidemiologic Research Program at Aichi Cancer Center
definition: A hospital-based epidemiologic research programme run since 1988 at Aichi Cancer Center in Nagoya, Japan, whose participants are first-visit outpatients of Aichi Cancer Center Hospital (including the HERPACC-2, 2001–2005, and HERPACC-3, 2005–2013, phases), used for case-control studies of cancer such as oesophageal cancer and for genome-wide studies within the Japanese Consortium of Genetic Epidemiology Studies.

label: Japanese Consortium of Genetic Epidemiology Studies
definition: A consortium of Japanese population-based and hospital-based studies — the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study, the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study, the Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Study and the Hospital-based Epidemiologic Research Program at Aichi Cancer Center — that pools genome-wide genotype data on healthy participants for genetic epidemiology, including genome-wide association studies of body mass index, height and weight.

label: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of about 140,000 registered residents aged 40–69 years in 11 public health centre areas across Japan, enrolled as Cohort I in 1990 and Cohort II in 1993 with questionnaires, blood samples and health check-up data and followed with repeat surveys, to study causes of cancer, cardiovascular disease and other diseases.

label: MEGASTROKE consortium
definition: A multi-ancestry consortium that combined genome-wide association data from 29 studies (67,162 stroke cases and 454,450 controls, mainly of European and East Asian ancestry) in a meta-analysis of stroke and its aetiological subtypes, drawing on contributing groups such as METASTROKE, SiGN, CHARGE and COMPASS.

label: MEMENTO cohort
definition: A nationwide French cohort of 2323 non-demented adults with isolated subjective cognitive complaints or mild cognitive impairment, recruited in memory clinics from 2011 to 2014 and followed with standardised clinical, neuropsychological, neuroimaging and biomarker assessments to study the natural history of Alzheimer's disease and related disorders.

label: Miami Stroke Registry
definition: A prospective registry at the University of Miami that offers enrolment to consecutive patients admitted with stroke or transient ischaemic attack, a predominantly Hispanic and Black multiethnic population, contributing cases to the NINDS Stroke Genetics Network.

label: Malmö Preventive Project
definition: A population-based cohort of 33,346 residents of the city of Malmö in southern Sweden, recruited by pre-specified birth-year groups for health examinations from 1974 to 1992, whose samples and data are used in genetic and biomarker studies of disease.

label: NeuroDys cohort
definition: A European cross-linguistic sample of school-age children, including more than 900 with dyslexia sampled with homogeneous inclusion criteria across eight European countries and a comparable number of controls, assembled by the EU-funded NeuroDys consortium to study the genetics of dyslexia.

label: Nutrition and Health of Aging Population in China
definition: A population-based cohort of 3,289 adults aged 50–70 years from urban and rural Beijing and Shanghai, China, recruited in 2005 and resurveyed after six years, designed to investigate environmental and genetic factors and their interactions in cardiometabolic diseases.

label: NUgene Project
definition: A genomic biobank sponsored by the Center for Genetic Medicine at Northwestern University in partnership with Northwestern Medicine, collecting DNA samples and self-reported and electronic medical record health information from patients of Northwestern Medicine-affiliated hospitals and clinics to study the role of genes in common diseases and their treatment.

label: RADIOGEN cohort
definition: A Spanish cohort of cancer patients treated with radiotherapy at the Clinical University Hospital of Santiago de Compostela, Galicia, with prostate (RADIOGEN-Prostate, from 2005), lung (RADIOGEN-Lung, 2008–2015) and head and neck cancer sub-cohorts, collecting blood samples, dosimetry, clinical and toxicity data to identify genetic and epigenetic predictors of radiotherapy toxicity.

label: Religious Orders Study
definition: A longitudinal clinical-pathologic cohort study of ageing and Alzheimer's disease run by the Rush Alzheimer's Disease Center, which since 1994 has enrolled older Catholic nuns, priests and brothers from across the United States who are free of dementia at enrolment and agree to annual clinical evaluations and brain donation at death.

label: Study of Addiction: Genetics and Environment
definition: A genome-wide association study dataset that aggregates common measures from three large substance-abuse studies, the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism, the Family Study of Cocaine Dependence and the Collaborative Genetic Study of Nicotine Dependence, funded as part of the NIH Gene Environment Association Studies (GENEVA) initiative.

label: Study of African Americans, Asthma, Genes and Environments
definition: A clinic-based case–control study of childhood-onset asthma in African American children and youth recruited in the San Francisco Bay Area, United States, run by the University of California, San Francisco, to untangle the genetic and environmental basis of asthma in minority populations.

label: Shanghai Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer among women aged 25–70 who were permanent residents of urban Shanghai, China, recruited in two phases (August 1996–March 1998 and April 2002–February 2005).

label: Singapore Malay Eye Study
definition: A population-based study of Malay adults aged 40–79 years living in south-western Singapore, selected by age-stratified random sampling and examined with standardised interviews, ocular and systemic assessments and stored blood and urine samples, to measure the prevalence and risk factors of age-related eye diseases in people of Malay ethnicity.

label: Spanish Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of bladder cancer (the EPICURO study) that enrolled patients newly diagnosed with urothelial carcinoma of the bladder in 1998–2001 at 18 hospitals in five regions of Spain and individually matched hospital controls, to study environmental, occupational and genetic risk factors for bladder cancer.

label: Shenzhen Maternal and Neonatal NIPT cohort
definition: A hospital-based cohort of more than 100,000 Chinese pregnant women who had non-invasive prenatal testing at Longgang District Maternity and Child Healthcare Hospital and Shenzhen Baoan Women's and Children's Hospital in Shenzhen, China, whose low-depth NIPT sequencing data are linked to laboratory and electronic medical records to study the genetics of pregnancy traits and complications.

label: Translational Genomics Research Institute series 2
definition: A series of clinically and neuropathologically characterised brain donors with Alzheimer disease and cognitively normal elderly controls, assembled by the Translational Genomics Research Institute (Phoenix, United States) from NIA-supported Alzheimer's Disease Center brain banks, the Miami Brain Bank and brain banks in the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, and genotyped for genome-wide association studies of late-onset Alzheimer disease within the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium.

label: Transdisciplinary Research in Cancer of the Lung
definition: A lung cancer genetic epidemiology consortium, one of the NIH-funded GAME-ON post-GWAS consortia and working with the International Lung Cancer Consortium, that integrates genome-wide data from multiple lung cancer studies of European populations to identify lung cancer susceptibility loci.

label: UK Millennium Cohort Study
definition: A nationally representative UK observational cohort of 18,827 children from 18,552 families, born at the turn of the century, followed through repeated sweeps of data collection from age 9 months onwards on health, development, cognitive ability, education and social and economic circumstances, with linkage to administrative health records.

label: University Medical Center Groningen Head and Neck cancer Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 1,429 patients with head and neck cancer treated with primary or postoperative radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy, from 2007 to 2020 at the Department of Radiation Oncology of the University Medical Center Groningen, all enrolled in the UMCG head and neck cancer prospective data registration programme (NCT02435576), with prospective assessment of radiation-induced toxicity and patient-rated outcome measures.

label: University of Pittsburgh Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
definition: A cohort of Alzheimer disease patients, about a quarter of them autopsy-confirmed, and cognitively normal controls from the same area, recruited by the University of Pittsburgh Alzheimer's Disease Research Center in Pittsburgh, United States, and genotyped for genome-wide association studies of late-onset Alzheimer disease.

label: Vanderbilt Memory & Aging Project
definition: A case-control longitudinal study of vascular health and brain aging launched in 2012 at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, USA, which enrolled 335 adults aged 60–92 with mild cognitive impairment or normal cognition from 2012 to 2014 for repeated clinical, cardiac, brain imaging and CSF assessments.

label: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy
definition: A cohort of patients with sickle cell disease enrolled at ten centres in the United States and the United Kingdom and screened by echocardiography and laboratory tests for pulmonary hypertension to assess eligibility for a randomised clinical trial of sildenafil.

label: Wisconsin Epidemiologic Study of Diabetic Retinopathy
definition: A population-based cohort of people with diabetes receiving primary care in an 11-county area of southern Wisconsin, United States, in 1979–1980, followed for decades to study the incidence and progression of diabetic retinopathy and other diabetes complications.

label: Washington Heights-Inwood Columbia Aging Project
definition: A prospective, population-based study of aging and dementia in Medicare-eligible adults aged 65 and over living in the Washington Heights and Inwood neighborhoods of northern Manhattan, New York, first recruited in 1992 by random sampling and extended in later recruitment waves.

label: Han Chinese in Beijing, China
definition: A collection of DNA samples and lymphoblastoid cell lines from Han Chinese individuals in Beijing, China, that forms one of the four founding population samples of the International HapMap Project and is used as a reference for human genetic variation.

label: Japanese in Tokyo, Japan
definition: A collection of DNA samples and lymphoblastoid cell lines from Japanese individuals in Tokyo, Japan, that forms one of the four founding population samples of the International HapMap Project and is used as a reference for human genetic variation.

label: Rush Memory and Aging Project
definition: A longitudinal, epidemiologic clinical-pathologic cohort study of common chronic conditions of ageing run by the Rush Alzheimer's Disease Center, which since 1997 has enrolled older lay persons without dementia, mainly from retirement communities across northeastern Illinois, who agree to annual clinical evaluations and organ donation, with an emphasis on decline in cognitive and motor function and risk of Alzheimer's disease.

label: Social Science Genetic Association Consortium
definition: A consortium founded in 2011 of medical researchers and social scientists that coordinates genome-wide association studies of social-science outcomes such as educational attainment across more than 100 contributing cohorts and promotes harmonised phenotype measurement.

label: Three-City Study
definition: A population-based longitudinal study of adults aged 65 and over recruited in three French cities, Bordeaux, Dijon and Montpellier, and followed from 1999 to 2012 with repeated examinations of vascular risk factors, cognition and subclinical vascular disease to study the relation between vascular diseases and dementia.

label: Association STudy Evaluating RISK for sporadic colorectal cancer
definition: A case-control study of sporadic colorectal cancer in the Pays de la Loire region of France, which recruited about 1,000 patients diagnosed at age 40 or over in regional hospitals and clinics and about 1,100 age- and sex-matched controls at regional health examination centres in 2002–2006, to study genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer.

label: Aston Dyslexia Cohort
definition: A collection of unrelated children and adolescents referred by local schools for assessment of reading difficulties at the Aston Dyslexia and Developmental Assessment Unit in Birmingham, UK, and invited to take part in research, genotyped for genetic studies of dyslexia and reading- and language-related skills.

label: Brescia Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of bladder cancer among men resident in the province of Brescia, northern Italy, with newly diagnosed cases admitted to the urology departments of the two main Brescia hospitals in 1997–2000 and controls with non-neoplastic urological diseases, used to study occupational, environmental and genetic risk factors for bladder cancer.

label: Beijing Eye Study
definition: A population-based study of 4439 adults aged 40 years or over living in Greater Beijing, China, first examined in 2001 and re-examined in 2006 and 2011 with detailed ophthalmic and general examinations, to measure the frequency of eye diseases and visual impairment and their associated and risk factors.

label: Biomarkers of Cognitive Decline Among Normal Individuals
definition: An ongoing longitudinal cohort of primarily middle-aged adults, all cognitively unimpaired at enrolment from the community, begun in 1995 in the National Institutes of Health intramural program and later continued at Johns Hopkins University, with repeated cognitive, clinical, CSF, blood and MRI assessments to study the earliest phases of Alzheimer's disease.

label: French Prostate Cancer Case-Control Study
definition: A hospital-based prospective case-control study of prostate cancer in France, run by the Centre de Recherche pour les Pathologies Prostatiques (CeRePP) at Hôpital Tenon, Paris, whose cases are patients with histologically confirmed prostate cancer treated in French urology departments and whose controls are men found unaffected in a systematic health screening programme, used in genetic association studies of prostate cancer.

label: Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood 2010
definition: An unselected Danish mother-child birth cohort of 738 pregnant women from eastern Denmark recruited in 2008–2010 at week 24 of pregnancy and their 700 children, deeply phenotyped at the COPSAC clinic with nested randomised trials of vitamin D and fish oil in pregnancy, to study how perinatal exposures such as the microbiome and maternal nutrition interact with genetics in the development of asthma and other chronic inflammatory diseases.

label: Cohort of Swedish Men
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of men born in 1918–1952 living in Västmanland and Örebro counties in central Sweden, established in 1997 and used, with the Swedish Mammography Cohort, to study diet, lifestyle and chronic disease.

label: Czech Republic Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in the Czech Republic, with cases and controls collected at oncology departments of several Czech hospitals from 2003 onwards, used to study genetic and lifestyle risk factors for colorectal cancer.

label: Etude des Déterminants/Interaction de la Thrombose veineuse
definition: A hospital-based study at Brest University Hospital, France, launched in 2000, that enrols consecutive patients with objectively confirmed venous thromboembolism (more than 5,000 so far), with matched hospital controls, to study genetic and environmental risk factors for venous thromboembolism and their interactions.

label: Johannesburg Cancer Study
definition: A cancer case-control study that enrolled 24,971 Black patients with incident, mostly histologically proven cancers of any type in Johannesburg, South Africa, between 1995 and 2016, collecting questionnaire data and serum and whole-blood samples and using patients with cancers unrelated to the exposure of interest as controls, to study lifestyle and infection (particularly HIV) risk factors for cancer; the ERICA-SA project uses its data and samples to study lifestyle, infection and genetic susceptibility to cancer.

label: French Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of bladder cancer in France (190 cases and 316 controls, 84% men, in the International Consortium of Bladder Cancer pooled analyses), whose cases were also genotyped for the NCI bladder cancer genome-wide association study.

label: NCI Familial Testicular Cancer Study
definition: A National Cancer Institute Clinical Genetics Branch study (protocol 02-C-0178) that enrolls families with at least two cases of testicular germ cell tumour, identified through physician and self-referral, together with controls, to study the genetic and clinical features of familial testicular cancer.

label: GEnetic Factors for OSteoporosis Consortium
definition: A large international collaboration of research groups, funded by the European Union Seventh Framework Programme as a successor to GENOMOS, that brings together osteoporosis study populations with DNA and genome-wide association data to identify common genetic variants for osteoporosis and bone traits.

label: Human Early Life Exposome
definition: A European population-based exposome cohort built across six existing longitudinal birth cohorts in France, Greece, Lithuania, Norway, Spain and the UK, with a subcohort of 1,301 mother-child pairs in which biomarkers, omics signatures and child health outcomes were measured at age 6–11 years, to relate multiple early-life environmental exposures to molecular signatures and child health.

label: Helix Exome+ and Healthy Nevada Project COVID-19 Phenotypes
definition: A collection of COVID-19 phenotypes from participants sequenced with the Helix Exome+ assay, including those of the Healthy Nevada Project, a population health study established in 2016 by Renown Health and the Desert Research Institute in Reno, Nevada, contributed to COVID-19 host genetics studies.

label: International Network Against Venous Thrombosis Consortium
definition: An international consortium that meta-analyses genome-wide association studies of venous thromboembolism from many case-control and population studies (30,234 cases and 172,122 controls from 18 studies in its 2019 analysis, 29 studies in later case-only analyses) to identify genetic risk factors for venous thromboembolism and its subtypes.

label: Los Angeles Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of bladder cancer in Los Angeles County, United States, with cases aged 25–64 diagnosed in 1987–1996 identified through the Los Angeles County Cancer Surveillance Program and matched neighbourhood controls, used to study lifestyle and genetic risk factors for bladder cancer.

label: Influence of Life-style factors on Development of the Immune System and Allergies in East and West Germany plus Air Pollution and Genetics on Allergy Development
definition: A prospective population-based German birth cohort of 3,097 healthy term newborns born between 1997 and 1999 and recruited in obstetric hospitals in Munich, Leipzig, Wesel and Bad Honnef, followed through childhood and adolescence to study the influence of lifestyle, environmental exposures such as air pollution, and genetics on the development of the immune system and allergic diseases.

label: Mayo Clinic Venous Thromboembolism Study
definition: A case-control study at the Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota, of adults with objectively diagnosed venous thromboembolism and age- and sex-matched controls, supplemented by Olmsted County residents with incident venous thromboembolism and matched controls, used for candidate-gene, genome-wide and whole-genome sequencing studies of venous thromboembolism risk.

label: Multicase-Control Study in Spain
definition: A multicase-control study in Spain that recruited hospital-based cases of several common cancers, including breast, colorectal and prostate cancer, and population-based controls in 2008–2013, to study environmental, lifestyle and genetic risk factors for these cancers.

label: Microisolates in South Tyrol Study
definition: A population-based family study of about 1,300 adults from Stelvio, Vallelunga and Martello, three small, historically isolated villages of the Val Venosta (Vinschgau) in South Tyrol, Italy, surveyed by the European Academy of Bozen/Bolzano (EURAC) in 2002–2003 and 2007, with reconstructed genealogies, to study the genetic epidemiology of Mendelian and complex diseases.

label: MrOS Sweden
definition: A prospective population-based multicentre study of 3,014 men aged 69–81, randomly selected from the Swedish national population register and examined at hospitals in Malmö, Gothenburg and Uppsala in 2001–2004, the Swedish part of the Osteoporotic Fractures in Men study, set up to identify risk factors for osteoporosis and fracture.

label: New England Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of bladder cancer among residents of Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont, United States, with cases newly diagnosed in 2001–2004 and population controls frequency-matched on age, sex and state, used to study environmental, dietary and genetic risk factors for bladder cancer.

label: NINDS Parkinson's Disease dataset
definition: A collection of Parkinson's disease patients and neurologically normal controls whose samples are held in the NINDS repository at the Coriell Institute and were genotyped genome-wide and publicly released through dbGaP (phs001172, including phs000089) for studies of genetic risk of Parkinson's disease.

label: NPDPSC pathology-confirmed rpAD
definition: A set of about 115 autopsied people referred with rapidly progressive dementia resembling prion disease to the National Prion Disease Pathology Surveillance Center at Case Western Reserve University between 2009 and 2017, in whom neuropathology, prion protein typing, PRNP sequencing and record review excluded prion disease and confirmed Alzheimer's disease, whole-genome sequenced from frozen brain tissue for genetic studies of rapidly progressive Alzheimer's disease.

label: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease
definition: A cross-sectional observational cohort of more than 800 adult patients with sickle cell disease enrolled between 2002 and 2015 at sickle cell centres in the southeastern United States, coordinated from Duke University, to study genetic associations with clinical outcomes.

label: Oxford Parkinson's Disease Centre Discovery Cohort
definition: A population-based incidence cohort of people diagnosed with Parkinson's disease within the previous 3.5 years, recruited by the Oxford Parkinson's Disease Centre from 11 hospitals across the Thames Valley, England, between 2010 and 2014, and followed with motor, cognitive and non-motor assessments to study Parkinson's disease progression and subtypes.

label: Australian Alcohol and Nicotine Studies
definition: A family sample of sibships ascertained through the Australian Twin Registry, with diagnostic interviews and blood or buccal DNA, of whom 8754 individuals (2062 alcohol-dependent cases) were genotyped genome-wide to study genetic contributions to alcohol use and dependence and nicotine dependence.

label: Parkinson's Disease Biomarkers Program
definition: A longitudinal multi-project collection of clinical data and biosamples from people with Parkinson's disease at different stages, other parkinsonism, essential tremor and controls, established in 2012 by the US National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke as a consortium of biomarker discovery projects with standardized procedures and a shared data management resource.

label: Pakistan Genomic Resource
definition: A growing biobank and national consortium of case–control studies in Pakistan that aims to enrol one million participants (about 250,000 from 48 clinical sites in 17 cities by September 2023) across some 50 diseases, with whole-exome sequencing and recontact, used for genetic association and loss-of-function studies.

label: Pharmacogenetics of Nicotine Addiction Treatment
definition: A multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled smoking-cessation trial (NCT01314001) run from 2010 to 2014 at four academic medical centres in the United States and Canada, in which 1246 treatment-seeking smokers stratified by nicotine metabolite ratio were assigned to placebo, nicotine patch or varenicline.

label: Riesgo de Enfermedad TROmboembólica VEnosa
definition: A Spanish case-control study of venous thromboembolism, based at the Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau in Barcelona, whose cases had a first venous thromboembolism and were sampled after 6–12 months of anticoagulant treatment, with healthy controls recruited from the general population, used to study genetic and plasma determinants of venous thromboembolism.

label: Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification Evaluation
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of 646 patients with a first unprovoked major venous thromboembolism, enrolled from 12 tertiary care centres in 4 countries while on oral anticoagulation 5–7 months after the event and followed after stopping anticoagulation (to September 2006), to derive a clinical decision rule identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism.

label: Suivi Temporaire Annuel Non-Invasif de la Santé des Lorrains Assurés Sociaux
definition: A single-centre longitudinal family cohort of 4,295 people from 1,006 families of the Lorraine region, recruited in 1993–1995 at the Center for Preventive Medicine in Nancy, France, and re-examined over about 20 years, to study the familial and genetic determinants of cardiovascular and metabolic traits.

label: Strong Heart Study
definition: A cohort of 4,549 self-identified American Indian adults aged 45 years or older, recruited in 1989–1991 from tribal communities in Arizona, Oklahoma, North Dakota and South Dakota, United States, and followed through repeated examinations to estimate cardiovascular disease rates and risk factors in American Indians.

label: South London Ethnicity and Stroke Study
definition: A stroke study in which 1,200 black and 1,200 white stroke patients were prospectively recruited between 1999 and 2010 from three hospitals covering a contiguous area of South London, United Kingdom, with black African and African Caribbean community controls from general practice lists in the same catchment area (1999–2012), to study stroke subtypes and the genetic and other risk factors for stroke in African and African Caribbean people.

label: SLI Consortium cohort
definition: A collection of nuclear families, each ascertained through a proband with receptive and/or expressive language skills more than 1.5 SD below the age norm, gathered by the SLI Consortium from five clinical and epidemiological sites across the United Kingdom for linkage and association studies of specific language impairment.

label: US Servicemen's Testicular Tumor Environmental and Endocrine Determinants Study
definition: A case-control study of testicular germ cell tumours among US military servicemen aged 18–45 with serum stored in the Department of Defense Serum Repository, comparing men diagnosed on active duty in 2002–2005 with matched controls to study environmental, endocrine and genetic risk factors.

label: Tromsø Study
definition: A population-based study of residents of the municipality of Tromsø, Norway, run by UiT The Arctic University of Norway, begun in 1974 and repeated in seven surveys (Tromsø1–Tromsø7) that together enrolled 45,473 people, as a multipurpose health survey of chronic diseases and their risk factors.

label: Texas Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of bladder cancer in Texas, United States, with newly diagnosed, previously untreated cases recruited at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and Baylor College of Medicine and matched controls, used for genome-wide and pathway studies of bladder cancer susceptibility.

label: Asia Breast Cancer Consortium
definition: A consortium of breast cancer genetic association studies in women of Asian ancestry, with studies in mainland China, Taiwan, South Korea and Japan (genome-wide data on about 24,000 cases and 25,000 controls by 2020), formed to discover breast cancer susceptibility loci in Asian populations.

label: Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of cohort and case-control studies with genome-wide genotype data that pools them in meta-analyses of genome-wide association studies of atrial fibrillation, to identify genetic loci for atrial fibrillation; together with the Broad AF Study, its studies formed the majority of the 2018 multi-ethnic meta-analysis of more than half a million individuals.

label: ASPirin in Reducing Events in the Elderly
definition: A placebo-controlled randomized trial of daily low-dose aspirin in 19,114 community-dwelling adults aged 70 or over (65 or over for US minorities) in Australia and the United States without prior cardiovascular events, dementia or independence-limiting physical disability, followed as a cohort after the trial to study healthy ageing.

label: Austrian Stroke Prevention Study
definition: A prospective single-centre population-based study of community-dwelling elderly people without stroke or dementia, randomly selected from the community register of Graz, Austria, and enrolled between 1991 and 2004, examining the effects of vascular risk factors on brain structure and function in normal ageing.

label: Austrian Stroke Prevention Family Study
definition: A family-based extension of the Austrian Stroke Prevention Study in Graz, Austria, for which ASPS participants and their first-degree relatives were invited between 2006 and 2013 (419 individuals from 176 families), examined with clinical history, neurological examination, brain MRI, laboratory tests, cognitive testing and vascular risk factor assessment to study the cerebral effects of vascular risk factors.

label: B-Vitamins for the PRevention Of Osteoporotic Fractures
definition: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 2,919 people aged 65 and older with elevated homocysteine, recruited in 2008–2011 mainly through municipal registries around research centres in Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Wageningen, the Netherlands, testing whether two years of vitamin B12 and folic acid supplementation reduce osteoporotic fracture incidence.

label: Canadian Partnership for Tomorrow's Health
definition: A pan-Canadian prospective cohort platform, established by the Canadian Partnership Against Cancer in June 2008 as the Canadian Partnership for Tomorrow Project, that federates regional cohorts (seven across ten provinces, among them CARTaGENE and the Ontario Health Study; 307,017 participants aged 30–74 from 8 provinces in five cohorts in its 2018 profile) with harmonized questionnaire, physical measurement and biosample data and linkage to administrative health databases, to study how genetics, behaviour and environment affect cancer and other chronic diseases.

label: DeCOI cohort
definition: A cohort of about 1,220 mainly vaccine-naive individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, across the full spectrum from asymptomatic to critical COVID-19, recruited early in the pandemic at 16 sites in Germany and South Tyrol, Italy, by a national host-genetics consortium built on the German COVID-19 Omics Initiative, with whole genome sequencing to study host genetic factors in COVID-19.

label: EU-RLS-GENE consortium
definition: An international consortium of restless legs syndrome case collections recruited by expert clinicians in movement-disorder and sleep clinics in Europe, Canada and the United States, with ancestry-matched population or hospital controls, pooled (7,248 cases and 19,802 controls) for genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome.

label: Familial Influences on Literacy Abilities
definition: A Dutch family dataset of 483 children from 307 nuclear families and 505 adults, including parents, assessed for word and nonword reading fluency, phonological awareness and rapid automatized naming to study genetic influences on reading and language.

label: Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia
definition: An international consortium of lung cancer studies of never-smoking Asian women from mainland China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan, South Korea and Japan, pooling genome-wide data to identify genetic risk factors for lung cancer, particularly adenocarcinoma, in this population.

label: GlobalGout Genetics Consortium
definition: An international consortium of gout genetics research groups, named as a collective author of a genome-wide association analysis of gout in 2.6 million people, whose own case-control sample set (New Zealand/Ardea Biosciences/EuroGout: 4,713 people with self-reported clinically diagnosed gout or gout meeting the 1977 ARA classification criteria and 2,151 controls, of self-reported European ancestry) was genotyped for that study on the Illumina CoreExome array.

label: Growing Up in Singapore Towards healthy Outcomes
definition: A birth cohort in Singapore that enrolled 1468 pregnant women aged 18 years or over at their first-trimester dating scan at the two major public maternity units in 2009–2010 and follows the mothers and their children, to evaluate how early-life exposures influence later metabolic function, body composition and development.

label: Hawaii Adenoma Study
definition: A case-control study of first-time colorectal adenoma among Caucasian, Japanese and Native Hawaiian adults on Oahu, Hawaii, United States, with cases from the Hawaii site of the PLCO screening trial and Kaiser Permanente Hawaii clinics (1995–2006) and controls with normal endoscopy, used to study risk factors for colorectal neoplasia.

label: Henry Ford Heart Failure Pharmacogenomic Registry
definition: A prospective registry of Black and White patients with heart failure enrolled within the Henry Ford Health System in Detroit, Michigan, from 2007 to 2015, with genotyping and pharmacy claims data, designed to discover ways to predict heart failure prognosis and responses to heart failure therapies.

label: HS Program for Research and Care Excellence
definition: A cohort of patients with hidradenitis suppurativa recruited at the University of North Carolina Department of Dermatology in the United States from August 2018 (753 patients by July 2021, later expanded to 986), providing clinical data and DNA for genetic association studies of the disease.

label: IARC Multicenter Case-Control Study
definition: A multicentre hospital-based case–control study of lung cancer coordinated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer in Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Poland, Russia and the Czech Republic, whose genome-wide genotyped cases and controls form the IARC lung cancer GWAS used by international lung cancer consortia.

label: Identification and prevention of Dietary- and lifestyle-induced health EFfects In Children and infantS
