definition: A multi-centre European population-based cohort of 16,228 children aged 2 to 9 years examined in 2007–2008 in Belgium, Cyprus, Estonia, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Spain and Sweden, with a community-based obesity-prevention intervention, followed into adolescence by the I.Family study to identify dietary and lifestyle risk factors for childhood overweight and metabolic disorders.

label: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Study
definition: A multiethnic cohort of over 1,600 Hispanic, non-Hispanic white and African American men and women aged 40–69 years with normal, impaired or diabetic glucose tolerance, recruited at four clinical centres in California, Texas and Colorado, United States, to study the relationships between directly measured insulin resistance, atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.

label: Personalized Medicine Research Project
definition: A population-based biobank cohort of about 20,000 adults living in 19 zip codes around Marshfield, Wisconsin, United States, recruited by the Marshfield Clinic from 2002, who provided DNA, serum and plasma samples linked to their electronic medical records for genetic and gene–environment research.

label: MD Anderson Cancer Center lung cancer study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of lung cancer at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, Texas, of ever-smoking patients of European ancestry and frequency-matched ever-smoking controls, genotyped genome-wide to find lung cancer susceptibility loci and later pooled in international lung cancer consortia.

label: MD Anderson Cancer Center melanoma study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of cutaneous melanoma at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, with non-Hispanic white patients and cancer-free controls (friends or acquaintances accompanying patients) recruited between 1998 and 2008, genotyped genome-wide to find melanoma susceptibility loci.

label: National Center for Geriatrics and Gerontology Biobank
definition: A biobank at the National Center for Geriatrics and Gerontology in Obu, Japan, holding DNA samples and clinical data from tens of thousands of patients with dementia and other age-related conditions and cognitively normal older adults from the NCGG hospital and a neighbourhood cohort, used for genetic studies of dementia and ageing in the Japanese population.

label: Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-Be
definition: A prospective multicentre US cohort of 10,038 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies recruited in the first trimester at eight clinical sites between 2010 and 2013 and followed through pregnancy, to study the factors that contribute to adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth, preeclampsia and gestational diabetes.

label: Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort
definition: A population-based study of youths aged 8–21 living in the greater Philadelphia area, United States, recruited through the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia Center for Applied Genomics from non-psychiatric paediatric clinics and assessed with clinical, neurocognitive and neuroimaging measures to describe how genetics affects brain development and cognitive functioning in adolescence.

label: ProHealth Study
definition: A study within Kaiser Permanente Northern California that ascertained African-American prostate cancer cases, genotyped together with the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health cohort and the California Men's Health Study for genome-wide association studies of prostate cancer.

label: Radiogenomics Consortium
definition: An international consortium, established in 2009, of cohorts of cancer patients treated with radiotherapy (for prostate, head and neck, breast and lung cancer, among others) that shares genotype and normal-tissue toxicity data and develops meta-analysis methods to identify genetic variants associated with radiation-induced toxicity.

label: Study of Epidemiology and Risk Factors in Cancer Heredity
definition: A population-based case-control study in East Anglia, UK, run from Cambridge with Cancer Research UK funding, in which people with cancer registered with the Eastern Cancer Registration and Information Centre and controls attending general practice in East Anglia provide data and DNA to study genetic susceptibility to cancers including breast and prostate cancer.

label: SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth
definition: An observational multicentre study in the United States of physician-diagnosed diabetes in people under 20 years old, ascertaining prevalent and incident cases in geographically defined populations and health plans, with interviews, examinations and laboratory measurements, to estimate the prevalence, incidence and classification of diabetes in youth.

label: Swedish Rheumatology Quality Register Biobank
definition: A biobank of the Swedish Rheumatology Quality Register holding blood samples, linked to register data, from more than 5500 patients with rheumatoid arthritis in Sweden who have early disease or are starting a biological disease-modifying drug, used for genetic and treatment-response research.

label: Swedish Rheumatology Quality Register
definition: A nationwide quality register of patients with rheumatic diseases, established in Sweden in the mid-1990s and used by most Swedish rheumatologists to monitor the disease course of patients as part of standard care.

label: Skåne University Hospital memory clinic cohort
definition: A clinical sample of patients with Alzheimer's disease evaluated at the memory disorder unit of Skåne University Hospital, Sweden, with physical, neurological and psychiatric examination, a clinical interview, cognitive testing, APOE genotyping and brain imaging, whose cerebrospinal fluid Alzheimer's biomarker data were used in a genome-wide association meta-analysis.

label: Toledo Study for Healthy Aging
definition: A population-based study of 2,488 people aged 65 and older in the province of Toledo, Spain, selected by two-stage random sampling from the municipal census and covering institutionalised and community-dwelling persons in rural and urban settings, with data collected from 2006 to study frailty and healthy ageing.

label: Berlin Aging Study II
definition: A multidisciplinary, multi-institutional cohort of about 1,600 older adults aged 60–80 and 600 younger adults aged 20–35 recruited as volunteers in the Berlin metropolitan area, Germany, with baseline assessments completed in 2014 across geriatrics, internal medicine, immunology, genetics, psychology, sociology and economics, to identify factors associated with healthy versus unhealthy ageing; a subsample of the older group was re-examined in 2018–2020 in the GendAge study.

label: Rotterdam Study II
definition: The second cohort of the Rotterdam Study, a prospective population-based cohort of 3,011 inhabitants of Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands, who had moved to the district or turned 55 since the first cohort began, enrolled from 2000 and re-examined about every 5 years to study determinants of chronic diseases in older adults.

label: MrOS Malmö
definition: The Malmö sub-cohort of MrOS Sweden: 1,005 men aged 69–81, randomly selected from the Swedish national population register and examined at hospital in Malmö, Sweden, in 2001–2004, to identify risk factors for osteoporosis and fracture.

label: Longitudinal Aging Study Amsterdam
definition: An ongoing prospective cohort study of older adults in the Netherlands, started in 1992 with a nationally representative sample aged 55–84 and refreshed with further cohorts in 2002, 2012 and 2024, to describe determinants, trajectories and consequences of changes in physical, cognitive, emotional and social functioning.

label: Finnish Gestational Diabetes Study
definition: A multicentre Finnish study of women who gave birth in 2009–2012, with a prospective genetic case-control arm of 1,146 pregnant women with gestational diabetes and 1,066 without, their children and the children’s fathers, recruited at seven hospitals, and a national register-based arm, to study the causes and consequences of gestational diabetes.

label: MrOS Gothenburg
definition: The Gothenburg sub-cohort of MrOS Sweden: 1,010 men aged 69–81, randomly selected from the Swedish national population register and examined at hospital in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 2001–2004, to identify risk factors for osteoporosis and fracture.

label: African Ancestry Anthropometry Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of genome-wide association studies of individuals of African ancestry that meta-analyses results from participating studies (up to about 53,000 individuals for body mass index) to discover and fine-map genetic loci for adiposity and other anthropometric traits.

label: Accelerating Medicines Partnership Parkinson's Disease
definition: A public–private research programme managed by the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health that harmonizes whole-genome sequencing, RNA expression and clinical data from multiple Parkinson's disease cohort studies, including PPMI, PDBP, the Harvard Biomarkers Study and BioFIND, on a shared platform for Parkinson's disease research.

label: Salus in Apulia Study
definition: A population-based cohort of older adults aged 65 and over, recruited from the electoral rolls of Castellana Grotte, Bari, in Apulia, southern Italy, by the National Institute of Gastroenterology 'Saverio de Bellis' Research Hospital as a public health initiative funded by the Italian Ministry of Health and the Apulia Regional Government, to study ageing, frailty, cognitive decline and related conditions.

label: Beijing Atherosclerosis Study
definition: A case-control collection of Han Chinese participants from Beijing, China, with myocardial infarction cases verified by hospital records and cardiologists and controls randomly selected from a community-based survey of cardiovascular risk factors in Beijing, assembled to study genetic susceptibility to coronary artery disease and atherosclerosis.

label: BIObanks Netherlands Internet Collaboration
definition: A nation-wide Dutch collaborative project that combines genotype data from sixteen population and clinical cohorts in the Netherlands with uniform, DSM-based phenotyping of major depressive disorder, pooled centrally for genetic mega-analysis of depression.

label: Bone Mineral Density in Childhood Study
definition: A multiethnic longitudinal study of healthy children at five clinical centres in the United States, enrolled from 2002–2003 at ages 6 to 16 years (1,554 children), with a later enrolment wave of 5- and 19-year-olds, measured annually by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry for up to 6 years, established to provide reference curves for bone mineral content and density by age, sex and race.

label: Canadian Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of women aged 20–80 with in situ or invasive breast cancer diagnosed from April 2005 to May 2009 in Metro Vancouver, British Columbia, and Kingston, Ontario, Canada, with cases from the BC Cancer Registry and controls from the Screening Mammography Program of BC in Vancouver, and cases and controls from the Hotel Dieu Breast Assessment Program in Kingston.

label: NIHR Cambridge BioResource
definition: A panel of volunteers in Cambridge, England, including blood donors registered with NHS Blood and Transplant, who have consented to be recalled for research studies by genotype or phenotype; the Cambridge centre of the NIHR BioResource, funded by the NIHR Cambridge Biomedical Research Centre and NHS Blood and Transplant.

label: Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2
definition: An international consortium of research groups that collect DNA and clinical data from carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations, established to identify genetic modifiers of breast and ovarian cancer risk in mutation carriers; it began with about 30 affiliated groups and later brought together more than 60 studies.

label: UROMOL project
definition: A European multicentre prospective study of patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, with tumour multi-omics and germline genotype data and clinical follow-up for recurrence and progression, used to define molecular subtypes of the disease and in genetic studies of bladder cancer.

label: Cardiometabolic Risk in Chinese Study
definition: A community-based health examination survey cohort of 6,431 adults aged 18–93 years randomly selected in 2009 from residents of the urban area of Xuzhou, Jiangsu, China, by Xuzhou Central Hospital, to study cardiometabolic risk factors such as insulin resistance, prediabetes, hypertension and early atherosclerosis.

label: Cooperative Research Centre Cohort
definition: A cohort of clozapine-treated patients with schizophrenia recruited by the Cooperative Research Centre from inpatient and outpatient clinics around Melbourne, Australia, with symptom severity (PANSS) assessments, contributing to genetic studies of clozapine treatment outcome.

label: Consortium for Refractive Error and Myopia
definition: An international consortium of cohorts of European and Asian ancestry that pools cohort-level genome-wide association results to study refractive error, myopia and ocular biometric traits such as axial length and corneal curvature.

label: Doetinchem Cohort Study
definition: A population-based cohort study in Doetinchem, the Netherlands, started by the Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) as a monitoring study of cardiovascular risk factors, in which 12,404 inhabitants aged 20–59, drawn as an age- and sex-stratified sample of the population register, were examined in 1987–1991 and two-thirds of them were re-invited to repeated rounds, to study lifestyle and other determinants of health, functioning and chronic disease over the life course.

label: Genes-environments & Admixture in Latino Americans
definition: A clinic-based case-control study of self-identified Latino children and young adults aged 8–22 years with and without asthma, recruited at centres in the mainland United States and Puerto Rico under the University of California, San Francisco, to study the genetic and environmental basis of childhood-onset asthma.

label: Groningen Expert Center for Kids with Obesity Drenthe study
definition: A population-based Dutch birth cohort of children of almost 3,000 pregnant women living in the province of Drenthe in the northern Netherlands, recruited in 2006, followed to study early risk factors for overweight and obesity in childhood.

label: Genes and Environment in Multiple Sclerosis
definition: A Swedish population-based case-control study of multiple sclerosis in which prevalent cases fulfilling the McDonald criteria were identified from the Swedish MS registry and controls were randomly selected from the national population register, with lifestyle and environmental questionnaires and blood samples for genetic analyses.

label: Georgia Stress and Heart Study
definition: A prospective cohort of normotensive children of African or European ancestry aged 5–16 years in 1989, recruited through a county-wide public school screening in Richmond County, Georgia, United States, and re-evaluated repeatedly into adulthood to study the development of cardiovascular risk factors from childhood to adulthood.

label: Health and Ageing in Africa: A Longitudinal Study of an INDEPTH Community in South Africa
definition: A longitudinal population study of more than 5000 adults aged 40 and older in Bushbuckridge, rural Mpumalanga, South Africa, recruited in 2014–2015 within the Agincourt Health and Demographic Surveillance System, collecting socio-demographic, infection history and cognitive data to study health and ageing.

label: Agincourt Health and Socio-demographic Surveillance System
definition: A health and socio-demographic surveillance system of about 90,000 people in rural northeast South Africa close to the Mozambique border, established in 1992, which updates resident status and vital events annually and hosts observational cohorts and trials across the life course on health, population and social transitions.

label: Health2006 Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 3,471 adults aged 18–69, randomly sampled from the Danish Central Personal Register in the southern part of Copenhagen and examined in 2006–2008 at the Research Centre for Prevention and Health in Glostrup, Denmark, to study general health, allergy, diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

label: Heidelberger Langzeitstudie zu Risikofaktoren und Diagnose chronischer Erkrankungen
definition: A longitudinal population-based study of 5,133 adults from the German city of Heidelberg and its surroundings, started in the 1990s with a baseline battery of health-related personality questionnaires to characterise associations between personality and somatic disease, and later followed up and genotyped.

label: Heart Failure Molecular Epidemiology for Therapeutic Targets Consortium
definition: A global collaboration of 51 studies from 11 countries with genome-wide genotyping and data on heart failure events and prognosis, including population-based cohorts, hospital-based electronic health record cohorts, case-control studies and clinical trials, formed to conduct large-scale genetic association studies of heart failure risk, prognosis and subtypes.

label: International Glaucoma Genetics Consortium
definition: A large international consortium established to identify glaucoma risk genes through large-scale genome-wide meta-analysis of primary open-angle glaucoma and related traits such as intraocular pressure, vertical cup-to-disc ratio and central corneal thickness, across populations of European, Asian and African ancestry.

label: International HIV Controllers Study
definition: A multinational study that recruited HIV-1 controllers, people with HIV whose plasma viral load stays below 2000 RNA copies/ml (at least three measurements over at least 12 months) without antiretroviral therapy, for genome-wide association analysis of host genetic effects on the control of HIV infection.

label: Immunomodulation and Multiple Sclerosis Epidemiology
definition: A set of Swedish post-marketing (phase IV) cohorts of patients with multiple sclerosis treated with novel disease-modifying drugs, followed through the Swedish MS registry to monitor the long-term safety and risks of immunomodulatory treatments.

label: International Parkinson Disease Genomics Consortium
definition: An international research alliance founded in 2009 of more than 100 scientists who pool genetic, clinical and functional data from Parkinson's disease case-control cohorts worldwide for collaborative genetics research on Parkinson's disease, with recent efforts in East Asia and Africa.

label: Japan PGx Data Science Consortium Database
definition: A collection of 2994 healthy Japanese volunteers assembled by the Japan Pharmacogenomics Data Science Consortium, with genotypes of 2.5 million SNPs and 5 HLA loci and 121 kinds of clinical information, as control data for pharmacogenomics studies of drug safety and efficacy.

label: Justification for the Use of Statins in Prevention: an Intervention Trial Evaluating Rosuvastatin
definition: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of rosuvastatin 20 mg daily for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in 17,802 apparently healthy men aged 50 or over and women aged 60 or over with low LDL cholesterol but elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, funded by AstraZeneca and stopped early for efficacy after a median follow-up of 1.9 years.

label: KOALA Birth Cohort Study
definition: A prospective Dutch birth cohort of healthy pregnant women enrolled from October 2000 to 2002, recruited from a cohort study on pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain ('conventional lifestyles') and, for contrast, through organic food shops, anthroposophic doctors and midwives, Steiner schools and dedicated magazines ('alternative lifestyles'), and their children, set up to identify lifestyle and other early-life factors that influence atopic disease and followed into young adulthood.

label: Mayo Clinic Breast Cancer Study
definition: A clinic-based case-control study of breast cancer begun in February 2001 at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota, enrolling women aged 18 or over with invasive breast cancer who lived in the six-state region of Mayo Clinic's primary service population, and cancer-free controls frequency-matched on age, race and region from Mayo Clinic's general internal medicine practice.

label: Mayo Mammography Health Study
definition: A prospective breast screening cohort of 19,924 women aged 35 or over, resident in Minnesota, Iowa or Wisconsin and without a history of breast cancer, enrolled when having a screening mammogram at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, from October 2003 to September 2006, to study mammographic density and breast cancer risk.

label: North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium
definition: A collection of families with multiple siblings affected by rheumatoid arthritis, gathered in the United States by the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium using well-defined clinical criteria and a severe-phenotype selection of probands, later extended with case-control collections (NARAC-II, NARAC-III), for linkage and association studies of rheumatoid arthritis genetics.

label: National Biobank of Korea
definition: The central national biobank of South Korea, opened by the Korea National Institute of Health as the hub of the Korea Biobank Network with regional hospital biobanks, which holds and distributes biospecimens and data from general-population cohort studies such as the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study and from hospital patients for biomedical and public health research.

label: Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of more than 140,000 participants in Norrbotten and Västerbotten, the two northernmost regions of Sweden, initiated in the mid-1980s and managed by Umeå University, combining three sub-cohorts (the Västerbotten Intervention Programme, the expanded Northern Sweden MONICA study and the Mammography Screening Project) with over 240,000 stored blood samples, for research on the aetiology, prevention and early detection of cancer, cardiovascular and other diseases.

label: Ontario Familial Breast Cancer Registry
definition: The Ontario site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry, which enrolled women with invasive breast cancer diagnosed in 1996–1998 identified through the Ontario Cancer Registry (all those aged 20–54 at high genetic risk and random samples of others, with high-risk cases diagnosed in 2001–2002 added), together with their relatives and population controls, to study the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer.

label: Prolonged Anticoagulation During eighteen months vs placebo after Initial Six-month treatment for a first episode of idiopathic Pulmonary Embolism
definition: A randomised, double-blind trial in which 371 adults with a first unprovoked pulmonary embolism, after six months of vitamin K antagonist treatment, were randomised to a further 18 months of warfarin or placebo and followed between 2007 and 2014 at 14 French centres, comparing recurrent venous thromboembolism and major bleeding.

label: Polish Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer in Warsaw and Łódź, Poland, in 2000–2003, funded by the intramural programme of the US National Cancer Institute, in which cases were women aged 20–74 with newly diagnosed in situ or invasive breast cancer identified through a rapid identification system at participating hospitals and through cancer registries.

label: Predicting Risk Of Cancer At Screening
definition: A cohort of women aged 47–73 recruited from 2009 at routine NHS Breast Screening Programme appointments in Manchester, UK, who completed risk-factor questionnaires and had breast density measured, a subset also giving DNA, to study breast cancer risk prediction at screening.

label: Qingdao Twin Registry
definition: A registry of twins and multiples of all ages in Qingdao, China, initiated in 1998 as part of the Chinese National Twin Registry, with more than 11,000 twin pairs recruited and adolescent, adult and elderly twin cohorts sampled for studies of chronic disease, metabolic disorders, health behaviours and ageing.

label: Chinese National Twin Registry
definition: A population-based twin registry in China, established in 2001, which includes data on over 61,000 twin pairs from 11 provinces or cities and collects biological specimens from disease-concordant and disease-discordant twin pairs, to analyse genetic and environmental influences on chronic diseases, especially cardiovascular diseases.

label: Reproductive Genetics Consortium
definition: An international network of investigators that meta-analyses genome-wide association study data from many cohorts to identify genetic variants and genes affecting reproductive ageing and reproductive timing, such as age at menarche and age at natural menopause.

label: Singapore and Sweden Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of postmenopausal breast cancer in women aged 50–74 born in Sweden, with incident cases identified through the Swedish regional cancer registries and controls randomly selected from the Swedish population register, enrolled in 1993–1995, with ethical approval at Karolinska Institutet and funding from Singapore (A*STAR) and the US.

label: Samuel Lunenfeld Research Institute Study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of lung cancer in Toronto, Canada, run by the University of Toronto and the Samuel Lunenfeld Research Institute of Mount Sinai Hospital, whose genome-wide genotyped cases and controls contribute to international lung cancer consortia.

label: Seoul National University Bundang Hospital cohort
definition: A hospital-based case–control cohort of patients with gastric cancer and non-cancer controls aged 26–80 recruited at the Digestive Disease Center of Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, South Korea, with genome-wide genotypes, Helicobacter pylori status and lifestyle data, used to study genetic risk of gastric cancer by histological type and sex.

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study
definition: A community-based cohort of adults aged 20 years or over living in Miyagi or Iwate Prefecture, Japan, of whom 87,865 consented to join through health check-ups and assessment centres of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Project, to assess the long-term impact of the Great East Japan Earthquake and gene–environment interactions in major diseases such as cancer and cardiovascular disease, with genome and metabolome information.

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Project Birth and Three-Generation Cohort Study
definition: A birth and three-generation cohort in Japan conducted since July 2013 by the Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization of Tohoku University and the Iwate Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization, recruiting pregnant women and their fetuses as probands together with the fathers, grandparents, siblings and extended family members, with genome and omics information, to study disease risk across generations.

label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey Clinical Cohort
definition: A Dutch clinical cohort of 543 children who had been referred to a child psychiatric outpatient clinic in the Northern Netherlands before the age of 11, enrolled from 2004 alongside the TRAILS population cohort and followed from about age 11 with repeated assessments of mental health and development into young adulthood.

label: Taiwan-US Diabetic Retinopathy Study
definition: A collection of Chinese people with type 2 diabetes in Taiwan, with and without proliferative diabetic retinopathy, assembled from 1996 to 2011 by Taiwanese and US investigators for genetic studies of diabetic retinopathy.

label: Breakthrough Generations Study
definition: A UK general-population cohort started in 2003 that recruited 112,049 participants aged 16–102 by 2011 through a generational referral method, in which women recruited directly nominated female friends and relatives, collecting detailed questionnaires and blood samples repeatedly over decades to investigate breast cancer aetiology.

label: DiaGene Study
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of people with type 2 diabetes, with diabetes-free controls included at baseline, in the city of Eindhoven, the Netherlands, extensively phenotyped to study the aetiology of type 2 diabetes and its micro- and macrovascular complications.

label: Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood
definition: A Danish clinical research programme, the Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood, made up of mother-child birth cohorts: COPSAC2000, a high-risk cohort of 411 children of mothers with a doctor's diagnosis of asthma, enrolled in the first month of life, and COPSAC2010, a cohort of 700 children born to unselected mothers from Denmark.

label: ProHealth Kaiser GWAS
definition: A multiethnic genome-wide association study sample of prostate cancer from Kaiser Permanente health plan members in California, combining prostate cancer cases from three Kaiser Permanente studies (the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, the ProHealth Study and the California Men's Health Study) with men of the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Aging cohort without a prostate cancer diagnosis as controls (7,783 cases and 38,595 controls; 80.3% non-Hispanic white, 4.9% African American, 7.0% East Asian and 7.8% Latino).
